abstract: This analysis investigates how faculty beliefs about teaching and learning influence their methods. Through interviews with 14 professors across disciplines, we identified four key views: Career-Content, Social-Dynamic, Joyful-Coaching, and Authority-Foundations, with Career-Content associated with traditional lecturing and Social-Dynamic with active learning. Findings indicate that professors' beliefs significantly affect their teaching, often at odds with evidence-based practices. Encouraging a shift in faculty conceptualizations appears crucial for adopting effective teaching strategies.

title: Supporting Preservice Teachers’ Responsive Teaching in Artificial Intelligence-integrated Simulations
citation: Zhang, N., Ke, F., Dai, C., & Barrett, A. (2024). Supporting Preservice Teachers’ Responsive Teaching in Artificial Intelligence-integrated Simulations. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2051-2052). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Zhang, N., Ke, F., Dai, C., & Barrett, A.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This mixed-methods study explored how preservice teachers (PSTs) practiced responsive teaching in an AI-integrated teaching simulation. Twenty PSTs practiced teaching with AI students in virtual world-supported participatory simulations. Data triangulated from dialogue transcripts, observations, and interviews indicated that AI-integrated participatory simulations enabled authentic, analytical, and reflective learning experiences that empowered PSTs to attend to students’ ideas. Moreover, virtual students bring nascent resources as productive beginnings of reasoning that PSTs can build on.

title: Citation Analysis for “Student Engagement”
citation: Jackson, D. W. (2024). Citation Analysis for “Student Engagement”: Towards More Interdisciplinary and Linguistically Equitable Understandings. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2053-2054). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Jackson, D. W.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: For 40 years scholars have published systematic reviews and entire handbooks on student engagement, though to date there has been no citation analysis of student engagement across all academic disciplines. This configurative synthesis review separates “non-English language” from “all-language” publications, and it presents finer-grained analyses of four key Categories. Visualizations of citation “bursts” and calculations of “betweenness centrality” confirm some within- and between-Category relationships previously posited, and they also reveal as-yet-undocumented relationships for further exploration.

title: Designing Pedagogical Content Knowledge for Data Literacy: A Design Based Research Approach
citation: Kao, S., Donaldson, J. P., Barth, M., & Ramos, S. (2024). Designing Pedagogical Content Knowledge for Data Literacy: A Design Based Research Approach. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2055-2056). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Kao, S., Donaldson, J. P., Barth, M., & Ramos, S.
subject: Humanities, Language & Literacy
abstract: This Design-Based Research study demonstrated the process of developing a data literacy course for pre-service teachers in an online learning environment through four iterations, and how design moves were crafted and refined.

title: Toward a Theory-Grounded Associative Model of AI Literacy
citation: Relmasira, S. C., Donaldson, J. P., & Lai, Y. C. (2024). Toward a Theory-Grounded Associative Model of AI Literacy. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2057-2058). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Relmasira, S. C., Donaldson, J. P., & Lai, Y. C.
subject: Humanities, Language & Literacy
abstract: This conceptual paper introduces the Associative Model of AI Literacy (AMAIL) for developing AI literacy. Through analysis of literature and empirical data, four interdependent domains containing sixteen competencies are proposed. Principles from learning theories provide insights into AI literacy development. AMAIL integrates constructs with these principles, situating learning in authentic contexts. Further research should investigate AMAIL's real-world implementation. AMAIL can guide pedagogy to develop multidimensional AI literacy as AI proliferates.

title: The Complexity of Diverse Conceptualizations of Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion in Higher Education
citation: Armenta, V., Murray, I., & Donaldson, J. P. (2024). The Complexity of Diverse Conceptualizations of Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion in Higher Education. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2059-2060). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Armenta, V., Murray, I., & Donaldson, J. P.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This study examines diverse conceptualizations of Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) in higher education using complex conceptual systems theory. Interviews and analyses reveal four distinct DEI conceptualizations, each centering different aspects and associated practices. Understanding DEI as a complex conceptual system illuminates new directions for inclusive learning environments. The methodology provides a framework potentially applicable to other multifaceted issues in learning sciences.

title: Let them Build their House!: Youth Developing Youth Power
citation: Lau, N. G. & Greenberg, D. (2024). Let them Build their House!: Youth Developing Youth Power. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2061-2062). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Lau, N. G. & Greenberg, D.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: The house metaphor of low floors, high ceilings, and wide walls can be used as a lens to view youth power, and the healing of oppressive structures. As youth are building the house and enacting their power, adults must recognize their positionality and stand in solidarity with youth without manipulating their power. The backyard as another element is added to focus on the impactful change and transformation that youth make “in their own backyard.”

title: Creating a Science Classroom Culture where Teachers and Students Care about Learning Science Together
citation: Alzen, J. L., Edwards, K., Buell, J. Y., Zhang, Y., Griesemer, C. D., Passmore, C., Penuel, W. R., & Reiser, B. J. (2024). Creating a Science Classroom Culture where Teachers and Students Care about Learning Science Together. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2063-2064). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Alzen, J. L., Edwards, K., Buell, J. Y., Zhang, Y., Griesemer, C. D., Passmore, C., Penuel, W. R., & Reiser, B. J.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Reform-oriented science classrooms emphasize students acting as epistemic agents and working collaboratively to make sense of ideas. Establishing classroom cultures in which students adopt such efforts can be challenging. We consider how one teacher initiated such a classroom culture and investigate how she invited students to join her in the development and maintenance of that culture. Results suggest that student partnership in community-oriented classroom culture can support students in sensemaking about science.

title: Making the Self: Community and Identity in Generative Role-Playing Game (RPG) Based Learning
citation: Cooper, R. P., Barth, M., Chowdhury, M., & Donaldson, J. P. (2024). Making the Self: Community and Identity in Generative Role-Playing Game (RPG) Based Learning. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2065-2066). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Cooper, R. P., Barth, M., Chowdhury, M., & Donaldson, J. P.
subject: Humanities, Language & Literacy
conceptualisations_list: Communities of Practice & Situated Learning; Constructionism & Maker-Centered Learning
abstract: This study uses constructionism, social constructivism, cognitive constructivism, transformative learning theory, DSMRI theory, self-determination theory, and situated learning theory to analyze the impact of generative RPG-based learning in a university literature course. The findings reveal the interplay of these theories in shaping student identities, motivation, and engagement, highlighting the importance of leveraging identity within the learning process. Game-based learning transforms the ways students engage with literature and develop their identities.

title: Teamwork in Higher Education: Benefits and Barriers
citation: Robbins, J., Brandao, A., & Chowdhury, M. (2024). Teamwork in Higher Education: Benefits and Barriers. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2067-2068). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Robbins, J., Brandao, A., & Chowdhury, M.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Industry and higher education have long recognized the importance of teamwork skills and the need for quality training. Although there is an array of pedagogical approaches to teamwork training, student perceptions on their effectiveness can influence implementation. This study employed a qualitative approach to investigate student experiences with teamwork and identified distinct clusters of experiences and learning theory principles associated with them. The findings have implications for improving teamwork pedagogy and enhancing students' learning experiences.

title: Natural Language and Computational Thinking: A Tale of Symbiosis
citation: Foohs, M. M. (2024). Natural Language and Computational Thinking: A Tale of Symbiosis. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2069-2070). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Foohs, M. M.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; Humanities, Language & Literacy
tpack_ck_labels: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; Humanities, Language & Literacy
abstract: This study addresses Brazilian students' deficiencies in language skills and computational thinking. Pre-service teachers underwent active methodologies, emphasizing formative assessments. Positive outcomes include improved communication, cultural awareness, and computational thinking skills. Challenges in global variables and structured writing persist, emphasizing the need for targeted support. The integrated approach shows promise, presenting opportunities for further exploration in creative expression and computational thinking at the intersection of education.

title: Academic Buoyancy and Fear of Failure Differences Among University Students: Null Findings
citation: Dang, A. H. & Middlemiss, W. (2024). Academic Buoyancy and Fear of Failure Differences Among University Students: Null Findings. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2071-2072). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Dang, A. H. & Middlemiss, W.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Academic buoyancy refers to a student's ability to successfully deal with academic-related setbacks and challenges that are typical in the ordinary course of school life. The current study investigated the relation between academic buoyancy and fear of failure and examined the potential differences in academic buoyancy and fear of failure among university students (N =118). Results indicated there was insufficient evidence of differences in academic buoyancy and fear of failure when considering other individual characteristics, such as gender, college-generational status, native language, college-attending status, and racial backgrounds. Further, most students experience similar levels of academic buoyancy.

title: Comparing the Science Talk of AI and Human Students
citation: Barrett, A., Zhang, N., Ke, F., & Dai, C. (2024). Comparing the Science Talk of AI and Human Students. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2073-2074). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Barrett, A., Zhang, N., Ke, F., & Dai, C.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This poster reports on an exploratory comparison of middle school science classroom discourse from AI-powered virtual student agents and human students. Transcripts from both simulated science classes with preservice teachers and AI students and recordings of real science classes were coded using a framework of student science talk moves. Results suggest that the AI and human discourse is mostly similar, although the AI tended to ask questions much more frequently than human students did.

title: Identity, Power, and Imagination at a Children's Museum
citation: Steinberg, S., Quick, J., Cruz-Gonzalez, C., Greenberg, D., Lau, N. G., Fox, S., & Wolfe, B. (2024). Identity, Power, and Imagination at a Children's Museum. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2075-2076). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Steinberg, S., Quick, J., Cruz-Gonzalez, C., Greenberg, D., Lau, N. G., Fox, S., & Wolfe, B.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: We share insights on co-design to support critical engagement with museum content towards identity development. We explore how a co-designed visitor activity can 1) support critical engagement with exhibit content; and 2) support youth to reflect on their identities and power to enact change in their communities. Data are generated in a participatory co-design process with museum leadership. We engage three themes that drove exhibit creation: identity, imagination, and power.

title: Towards a Longitudinal, Qualitative Study of Computational Identity in K-12 Computer Science Education
citation: Wolf, J., Proctor, C., & Blikstein, P. (2024). Towards a Longitudinal, Qualitative Study of Computational Identity in K-12 Computer Science Education. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2077-2078). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Wolf, J., Proctor, C., & Blikstein, P.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; STEM - Natural Science
tpack_ck_labels: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; STEM - Natural Science
abstract: Broadening and deepening participation in computing requires a richer understanding of the impacts of K-12 CS education on learners’ lives and identities. We propose that qualitative, longitudinal research can contribute to this understanding and help produce better CS learning experiences. This poster presents our proposed methodology for conducting such a study along with pilot results. Our findings create space for discussion about these methods and the nuance they can provide in understanding computational identity.

title: Exploring the Interplay between Criteria and Constraints in Authentic Epistemic Practices
citation: Tang, H., Jiang, S., & Xie, C. (2024). Exploring the Interplay between Criteria and Constraints in Authentic Epistemic Practices. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2079-2080). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Tang, H., Jiang, S., & Xie, C.
subject: STEM - Engineering & Robotics
abstract: Engineering design has been widely implemented in K-12 curriculum in combination with numerous pedagogical tools to foster future engineers. To foster epistemic agentic learners, understanding how learner negotiate between criteria and constraints in authentic epistemic practices is important. Preliminary findings showcased three different patterns of how learners undergo engineering design processes. Practical implications will be offered at the presentation.

title: Looking for the Right Blend: Comparing Different Assessment Scenarios in a Blended Course
citation: Hamzah, A., Setiaji, H., Persada, A. G., Kurniawan, R., & Sosnovsky, S. (2024). Looking for the Right Blend: Comparing Different Assessment Scenarios in a Blended Course. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2081-2082). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Hamzah, A., Setiaji, H., Persada, A. G., Kurniawan, R., & Sosnovsky, S.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This paper presents a study comparing different ways of orchestrating blended learning activities in a university course. As the main instrument, the study used Quizitor - a quiz platform that supports both in-class and at-home assessment. The data analysis shows that the presence of in-class assessment has a significant positive impact on students’ engagement with at-home quiz material. There is also strong evidence that the blended scenario, in which in-class assessment is administered as a pop-up quiz in the beginning of the next lecture, is more advantageous compared to the scenario scheduling in-class assessment as a post-lecture quiz.

title: Opportunities for Guiding Development: Insights from First-Year Life Science Majors’ Post-Pandemic Use of Metacognition
citation: Stanton, J. D., Halmo, S., Carter, R. J., A.Yamini, K., & Ososanya, D. (2024). Opportunities for Guiding Development: Insights from First-Year Life Science Majors’ Post-Pandemic Use of Metacognition. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2083-2084). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Stanton, J. D., Halmo, S., Carter, R. J., A.Yamini, K., & Ososanya, D.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Students with strong metacognitive skills are positioned to learn more than peers who are still developing metacognition. Yet many come to college without well-developed metacognition. Through interviews with 52 undergraduates at three institutions we identified when, why, and how first-year life science students use metacognitive skills. We found that current first-year students vary in their use of metacognition compared to first-year students our lab studied before 2020. We provide implications for instructors for supporting metacognition.

title: Learning Math through a Game-Based Personal Excursion
citation: Sager, M. T., Sherard, M., Milton, S., Walkington, C., & Petrosino, A. (2024). Learning Math through a Game-Based Personal Excursion. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2085-2086). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Sager, M. T., Sherard, M., Milton, S., Walkington, C., & Petrosino, A.
subject: STEM - Mathematics
abstract: This case study explores how middle-grade learners use a game-based app for math learning at an informal site, the Nature Center. We apply distributed and self-directed learning theories, emphasizing learning in specific contexts, social settings, and through tools like an iPad app. We employ the embodied action conversation framework to analyze critical interactions. Two cases emerged: (1) learners followed MathExplorer app rules, and (2) learners went on personal excursions, creating their own rules to improve their MathExplorer rankings. We discuss implications for designing technologies for informal math learning.

title: Researchers as Learners: Exploring Nature, Experiences, and Biases in Data Collection and Analysis
citation: Schuh, K. L., Rahman, F., Dunphy, M., & Domingues, R. (2024). Researchers as Learners: Exploring Nature, Experiences, and Biases in Data Collection and Analysis. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2087-2088). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Schuh, K. L., Rahman, F., Dunphy, M., & Domingues, R.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: In this study researchers investigated their own prior experiences and biases related to nature in the study of experiential learning. The researchers participated in an outdoor activity in a local park, in which their accompanying family members video recorded their exploration of the park. Analysis of the researchers’ personal narratives, individual video recording summaries, and open codes revealed that personal views of nature related to affect and safety appeared to influence researcher focus and interpretation.

title: Alleviating Tensions between Culturally Relevant Pedagogy and Mathematical Practices of Proof
citation: Fenech, M., Farid, A., Anderson, E., Lin, G., & Sears, R. (2024). Alleviating Tensions between Culturally Relevant Pedagogy and Mathematical Practices of Proof. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2089-2090). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Fenech, M., Farid, A., Anderson, E., Lin, G., & Sears, R.
subject: STEM - Mathematics
abstract: Mathematical practices of proof are central to the study of mathematics. Engaging high school students in these practices may be challenging, however, as students often encounter difficulties in understanding their intricacies while teachers simultaneously struggle with conveying their nuances. Although the integration of culturally relevant pedagogy (CRP) in mathematics classes has promising benefits for students, the marriage of CRP and mathematical practices of proof is not devoid of tensions, as teachers often wrestle with harmonizing the norms and values underlying these two instructional praxes. This paper aims to alleviate these tensions by advocating for the establishment of equitable learning communities. By co-creating proof norms with their students, teachers can balance both the tenets of CRP and the disciplinary practices of proof to develop students’ mathematical proficiencies.

title: A Comprehensive Strategy for Scaffolding the Development of Students’ Mathematical Proof Skills Across a Learning Progression
citation: Fenech, M., Farid, A., Anderson, E., Lin, G., & Sears, R. (2024). A Comprehensive Strategy for Scaffolding the Development of Students’ Mathematical Proof Skills Across a Learning Progression. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2091-2092). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Fenech, M., Farid, A., Anderson, E., Lin, G., & Sears, R.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: The core practices of constructing and critiquing proofs play a pivotal role in the authenticity of mathematicians' discipline, yet engaging high school students in these practices is notoriously challenging. Although research suggests various scaffolds to aid students in developing their mathematical proof skills, a unified approach for implementing all of them often eludes teachers in the classroom. This paper proposes a comprehensive strategy for developing students’ mathematical proof skills by integrating effective pedagogical approaches with a scaffolded trajectory. By strategically implementing hard and soft scaffolds across a learning progression, teachers can help bridge the gap between informal reasoning and formal mathematical proofs in pursuit of equitable outcomes for all students.

title:
Including Diverse Image Schemas in Knowledge Building 
for STEM Learners Who are Visually Impaired
citation:
Han, H. W. & Coppin, P. W. (2024). Including Diverse Image Schemas in Knowledge Building 
for STEM Learners Who are Visually Impaired. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2093-2094). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Han, H. W. & Coppin, P. W.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: To foster epistemic agency for visually impaired (VI) learners in STEM education for Knowledge Building (KB), educational support that suits diverse image schemas may be necessary. By better understanding diverse image schemas of VI people, which are often overlooked in educational environments where the needs of sighted learners are prioritized, this study identifies challenges to overcome for KB to function equitably as a social infrastructure.

title: Understanding the Institutional Challenges, Resources, and Strategies for Minoritized Students to Pursue STEM Degrees
citation: Rivera, A., Chapman, N., Nick, S., Salehi, S., & Nardo, J. (2024). Understanding the Institutional Challenges, Resources, and Strategies for Minoritized Students to Pursue STEM Degrees. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2095-2096). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Rivera, A., Chapman, N., Nick, S., Salehi, S., & Nardo, J.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: While enrollment numbers of minoritized students at four-year institutions is increasing steadily, STEM degree retention equity gaps continue to persist. These equity gaps have been and continue to be addressed primarily through instructional reformation, and often fail to consider the role the underlying institutional structures play. In our study, we conducted 50 semi-structured interviews with diverse students across different years and disciplines to identify and compare the most common institutional challenges, resources, and strategies for students across different demographic backgrounds. Our study and seeks to provide insights for institutional leaders to support justice through enacting policies and top-down changes.

title: Research-Practice Partnership as a Context for Teachers’ Learning
citation: Hadar, L. L. (2024). Research-Practice Partnership as a Context for Teachers’ Learning. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2097-2098). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Hadar, L. L.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This study examined how participation in a Research-practice partnership (RPP) initiative contributes to teachers’ professional learning and growth. Twenty teachers and ten school principals were interviewed, focusing on their professional experiences within the RPP. Qualitative data analysis yielded three categories: Development of knowledge and skills; personal, professional growth; and RPP as a framework for professional learning. The findings underscore the significant role of the RPP as a context for teachers' professional learning.

title: The Emotional Toll of Proleptic Imagining on the Job Market: When Possible Futures are Crushed
citation: Vogelstein, L. (2024). The Emotional Toll of Proleptic Imagining on the Job Market: When Possible Futures are Crushed. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2099-2100). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Vogelstein, L.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Prolepsis is a cornerstone concept in the Learning Sciences that typically describes an expansive discursive move in which adults talk about young people’s futures, as framed by the past, to mediate activity in the present. This poster looks at prolepsis on the academic job market, expanding conceptions to include (1) perspectives of those whose futures are being constructed, (2) harmful outcomes when imagined futures are crushed, and (3) ethical concerns for interviewing job candidates.

title: Promoting Embodied Geometric Reasoning Using a Spatial Puzzle Task
citation: Schenck, K. E. (2024). Promoting Embodied Geometric Reasoning Using a Spatial Puzzle Task. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 210-217). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Schenck, K. E.
subject: STEM - Mathematics
abstract: Previous studies have shown that body-based actions such as gestures and individual differences can impact geometric thinking and learning. One important individual difference is spatial ability, a multifaceted construct with demonstrated ties to success in mathematics. Though recent empirical work has also begun investigating whether targeted interventions for spatial ability can transfer to mathematics, studies are often limited to specific populations and pen-and-paper outcome measures. This study (N = 84) expands the work on the possibility of spatial tasks improving mathematics outcomes into verbal, mathematical reasoning outcomes through a randomized control design. Undergraduates were assigned to either complete a control task or a spatial puzzle followed by a geometric reasoning task. Results found that spatial-based Tangram tasks increased the likelihood of producing transformational proof but not mathematical insight. The skills accessed in spatially based tasks may transfer to informal reasoning tasks often seen in classrooms with implications for future curriculum design.

title: A New Approach to High School Data Science: Set Theory and Logic
citation: Zhang, Y., Du, H., & Xing, W. (2024). A New Approach to High School Data Science: Set Theory and Logic. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2101-2102). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Zhang, Y., Du, H., & Xing, W.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; STEM - Mathematics
tpack_ck_labels: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; STEM - Mathematics
abstract: There is a consensus to introduce data science to secondary schools. However, data science is interdisciplinary in nature and not easy to teach in K−12 settings. We proposed a new approach to integrate mathematics, statistics, and programming—the foundations of data science—for high school students based on set theory and logic. We developed an 8-week data science foundation course and implemented it in a public high school. We conducted semi-structured group interviews to collect students’ feedback on the course and the new approach. Students thought the approach could well connect the topics and helped them learn the interdisciplinary content.

title: Supporting Equitable Noticing in Elementary Science Methods
citation: Pierson, A., Henrie, A., & Syifa, M. (2024). Supporting Equitable Noticing in Elementary Science Methods. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2103-2104). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Pierson, A., Henrie, A., & Syifa, M.
subject: STEM - Natural Science
abstract: In the past two decades, science education researchers have increasingly attended to equity as a priority. However, in science teacher preparation programs, equity in STEM is often addressed peripherally. When equity is not a central focus in science methods courses, teacher candidates (TCs) have few opportunities to surface and challenge deficit and assimilationist ideologies. In response, we analyze artifacts from an elementary science methods course developed to foreground equitable noticing.

title: A Framework for Inclusive Game-Based Learning Design, Illustrated Through the Development of a Media Literacy Game
citation: Chang, Y. K., Literat, I., Song, X., Li, X., Meng, X., & Lei, Y. (2024). A Framework for Inclusive Game-Based Learning Design, Illustrated Through the Development of a Media Literacy Game. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2105-2106). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Chang, Y. K., Literat, I., Song, X., Li, X., Meng, X., & Lei, Y.
subject: Humanities, Language & Literacy
abstract: Game-based learning (GBL) provides opportunities to support diverse learning goals but GBL can support diverse learners with different cognitive, motivational, and gaming backgrounds remains relatively unclear. A conceptual framework to guide the design and research of inclusive GBL is introduced.

title: The Potentials in Intersections of Complexity Theory and Critical Perspectives in the Learning Sciences
citation: Armenta, V., Chowdhury, M., & Donaldson, J. P. (2024). The Potentials in Intersections of Complexity Theory and Critical Perspectives in the Learning Sciences. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2107-2108). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Armenta, V., Chowdhury, M., & Donaldson, J. P.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This conceptual paper explores integrating critical theory and complex systems theory to address systemic inequities in education. Complex systems theory investigates emergent problems, while critical theory offers tools to understand and disrupt inequities. A network analysis of 39 synthesis articles revealed siloed perspectives. Integrating these perspectives could benefit both communities and transform inequitable complex systems underlying wicked problems in education.

title: Groundskeeping to Nurture Emerging Discipline-based Education Researchers
citation: Solorio, C. D., Patterson, K., Hass, C. A., Sayre, E. C., & Franklin, S. (2024). Groundskeeping to Nurture Emerging Discipline-based Education Researchers. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2109-2110). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Solorio, C. D., Patterson, K., Hass, C. A., Sayre, E. C., & Franklin, S.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Newcomers to Discipline-based Education Research (DBER) face numerous challenges and supportive practices in becoming active members of their communities of practice. We present a framework for Montgomery’s groundskeeping leadership, which seeks to mitigate barriers and nurture community members for their growth and development (2020). We then apply that framework in the context of education researchers to examine some data from a set of interviews with Emerging Discipline-based Education Researchers.

title: Putting Theory into Practice: The Complex Experiences of Veterinary Students in a Constructivist Writing Assignment
citation: Adam, K., Chaney, K., Chowdhury, M., & Donaldson, J. P. (2024). Putting Theory into Practice: The Complex Experiences of Veterinary Students in a Constructivist Writing Assignment. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2111-2112). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Adam, K., Chaney, K., Chowdhury, M., & Donaldson, J. P.
subject: Humanities, Language & Literacy
abstract: This study implements design-based research (DBR) to enhance authentic advocacy in a veterinary course. The study analyzed learner experiences through surveys and network analysis, focusing on alignment with constructivist and constructionist learning theories. Results identified varying degrees of alignment with these theories across different student clusters. Some students exhibited strong alignment with constructivist principles like knowledge construction, while others showcased elements of constructionist learning, such as real-world application and problem-solving. The findings offer insights into how instructional design influences learning experiences and informs pedagogical practices in higher education. The study concludes that authentic advocacy, when grounded in educational theories, can significantly improve learning outcomes, critical thinking, and professional development. It also prepares learners for the challenges of the 21st century. The study shows how real-world scenarios can help students learn skills that are useful for future challenges and suggests that this approach may be beneficial for other higher education courses.

title: Exploring Student Perceptions of Group Quizzes: Interconnections with Learning Theories and Implications for Practice
citation: Pate, Z. D., Donaldson, J. P., & Carter, T. (2024). Exploring Student Perceptions of Group Quizzes: Interconnections with Learning Theories and Implications for Practice. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2113-2114). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Pate, Z. D., Donaldson, J. P., & Carter, T.
subject: STEM - Mathematics
abstract: This study explores learner experiences of group quizzes in a higher education mathematics class, grounded in learning theories including cognitive constructivism, social constructivism, situated learning theory, and self-determination theory. Through network analysis we identified four distinct clusters of student experiences and theory. Our findings underline the value of group quizzes, suggesting that a collaborative approach benefits many students. However, some clusters expressed neutrality or preference towards individual quizzes, highlighting the need for a hybrid approach. This research has broad implications for designing inclusive learning strategies, advocating for a blend of individual and collaborative activities to address different student needs and dispositions.

title: Design Principles for Disciplinary Learning Designs with Unplugged Computational Thinking as Pedagogical Means
citation: Dohn, N. B. & Dohn, N. B. (2024). Design Principles for Disciplinary Learning Designs with Unplugged Computational Thinking as Pedagogical Means. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2115-2116). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Dohn, N. B. & Dohn, N. B.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
abstract: This paper presents design principles for disciplinary learning with unplugged Computational Thinking, informed by embodied cognition, motivation research, and a Design-Based Research study in upper secondary science teaching. The resulting principles provide direction for employing embodied CT in algorithmic modeling of disciplinary processes, emphasizing task integration, bodily engagement, and strategies to reduce confusion.

title: Student Engagement as Microcultural: Empirical and Conceptual Arguments from a Teacher Residency Program
citation: Jackson, D. W. & Ramdath, K. (2024). Student Engagement as Microcultural: Empirical and Conceptual Arguments from a Teacher Residency Program. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2117-2118). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Jackson, D. W. & Ramdath, K.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
abstract: Much is known about individual- to school-levels of student engagement, but more work is needed for local- to global-contexts. We worked with a 15-month residency program in the Northeast US, conducting two focus groups that sought to better understand Residents’, Mentors’, Administrators’, and students’ conceptions and perceptions of student engagement. Our qualitative phenomenological study evidences what we call microcultural engagement, a framing that juxtaposes smaller- and larger-scale levels of learning and development.

title: Collaborative Writing and Knowledge Building
citation: Chang, C., See, C., Hung, G., Wang, L., & Hong, H. (2024). Collaborative Writing and Knowledge Building. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2119-2120). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Chang, C., See, C., Hung, G., Wang, L., & Hong, H.
subject: Humanities, Language & Literacy
abstract: This study examines the teaching effect of knowledge building for writing among elementary school students in Taiwan. The experimental group involved in Knowledge Building (KB) to enhance writing, and the control group engaged in direct instruction for writing. The findings based on mixed-methods analyses indicate: (1) the KB class outperformed the control class on essay writing as a learning outcome, and (2) there are progressively more engaged collaborative and discussion activities to improve writing ideas during the KB process.

title: Do Award-Winning Serious Games Meet Benchmarks for Quality Learning Tools?
citation: Duvall, M. & Shah, H. (2024). Do Award-Winning Serious Games Meet Benchmarks for Quality Learning Tools?. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2121-2122). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Duvall, M. & Shah, H.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Helping educators identify high-quality serious games without engaging in prolonged gameplay is an ongoing concern for game-based learning in formal education. We examined the websites of six award-winning video games to understand if, and to what extent, they described the five key benchmarks proposed by Dubé and colleagues (2020). Our analysis suggests that the evaluation model needs further refinement of definitions and clarifying contexts, such as formal settings, to be more useful.

title: Drawing and Talk Reveal Dynamic Shifts in Students' Developing Knowledge of Complex Systems
citation: Tang, X. & Lira, M. (2024). Drawing and Talk Reveal Dynamic Shifts in Students' Developing Knowledge of Complex Systems. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2123-2124). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Tang, X. & Lira, M.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Complex systems pose learning challenges because students must coordinate individual entities with their aggregate system properties. We sought to better understand this challenge by assessing students’ drawings and speech after they learned with a computational environment (NetLogo). We assessed how students represented their knowledge of complex systems and found that students transitioned from describing key entities in speech to representing both entities and their physical properties in their drawings.

title: Facilitating Data Conversations with Generative AI
citation: Diederich, M. & Nguyen, H. (2024). Facilitating Data Conversations with Generative AI. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2125-2126). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Diederich, M. & Nguyen, H.
subject: Humanities, Language & Literacy
abstract: There exists a need to promote critical data literacy, so that individuals can critique the ethics behind data work. We present results from using ChatGPT, a generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) tool, to facilitate data discussions. Generally, AI-generated questions successfully built on participants’ ideas and prompted discussions of data practices. Participants engaged in critical data literacy ideas, although to a lesser extent. We discuss the promise of using AI tools to facilitate data conversations.

title: Elementary School Learner Comic-Based Digital Storytelling on Digital Safety
citation: Mushi, D., Long, S., Martin, F., & Wang, W. (2024). Elementary School Learner Comic-Based Digital Storytelling on Digital Safety. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2127-2128). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Mushi, D., Long, S., Martin, F., & Wang, W.
subject: Humanities, Language & Literacy
abstract: This study highlights the potential of using comic-based digital storytelling as an instructional strategy for digital safety education. Guided by the multimodal literacy theory, the study employs character analysis and biterm topic modeling to identify prevalent themes within the curated Pixton comics of 20 students. The study revealed digital footprint, netiquette, and privacy as key themes in student's comics. Comic characters represented students' self-inserts and revealed expressions of their understanding of the topics.

title: Middle School CS Teachers’ Perceptions of Standards-focused PD
citation: Basu, S., Rachmatullah, A., Tate, C., Rutstein, D., & Yang, H. (2024). Middle School CS Teachers’ Perceptions of Standards-focused PD. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2129-2130). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Basu, S., Rachmatullah, A., Tate, C., Rutstein, D., & Yang, H.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Standards can support access to quality instruction. We examine how a standards-focused professional development (PD) approach can supplement traditional curriculum-based CS PD to improve teacher capacity. Using a case study approach, we explore two teachers’ perceptions of standards-focused PD and its effects. Findings indicate that teachers did not initially view standards as essential to their teaching but those who persisted through PD eventually advocated for making standards-focused PD compulsory for all CS teachers.

title: Students' Perspectives on Artificial Intelligence in Biology Higher Education: Insights for Collaborative Curriculum Design
citation: Coelho, R., Bjune, A. E., Ellingsen, S., & Cotner, S. (2024). Students' Perspectives on Artificial Intelligence in Biology Higher Education: Insights for Collaborative Curriculum Design. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2131-2132). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Coelho, R., Bjune, A. E., Ellingsen, S., & Cotner, S.
subject: STEM - Natural Science
abstract: We surveyed Norwegian post-secondary students in Biology to understand their perspectives on integrating tools powered by large language models (LLMs) into higher education. Students view tools such as ChatGPT positively and primarily as supplementary learning aids. However, they raised concerns about ethics, accuracy, and bias, and are particularly concerned about what constitutes cheating. Findings emphasize the need to develop guidelines ensuring these emergent tools support learning.

title: Generative AI Tools in an Undergraduate Computer Science Program
citation: Simon, S., Coelho, R., Marfisi-Schottman, I., & Pea, R. (2024). Generative AI Tools in an Undergraduate Computer Science Program. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2133-2134). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Simon, S., Coelho, R., Marfisi-Schottman, I., & Pea, R.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
abstract: We surveyed all undergraduate students (N = 121) enrolled in a three-year Computer Science (CS) program in France to learn about their use of generative AI tools. Our findings reveal widespread use of these tools across all academic years, with a higher proportion of later-year students reporting using these tools for a wider range of coding tasks compared to first-year students.

title: Students’ Use of Cultural Practices in Astronomy Stories
citation: Plummer, J. D. & Ragonese, A. (2024). Students’ Use of Cultural Practices in Astronomy Stories. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2135-2136). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Plummer, J. D. & Ragonese, A.
subject: STEM - Natural Science; Humanities, Language & Literacy
tpack_ck_labels: STEM - Natural Science; Humanities, Language & Literacy
abstract: We investigate how preservice teachers (PTs) express the ways science is enacted through cultural practices, by writing astronomy stories. Storybooks written by PTs in an introduction to astronomy course were analyzed. Seven themes were identified describing how PTs take up anti-deficit perspectives as well as enact traditional approaches to science.

title: Students’ Systems Thinking with the Water Cycle Simulation
citation: Provost, A. & Panorkou, N. (2024). Students’ Systems Thinking with the Water Cycle Simulation. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2137-2138). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Provost, A. & Panorkou, N.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This study presents two middle school students’ development of systems thinking as they explored the water cycle using a virtual interactive ecosystem simulation.

title: Localizing the Coding as another Language: ScratchJr Curriculum Through the Culture Based Model Framework
citation: Carocca, F., Blake-West, J., & Bers, M. (2024). Localizing the Coding as another Language: ScratchJr Curriculum Through the Culture Based Model Framework. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2139-2140). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Carocca, F., Blake-West, J., & Bers, M.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; Humanities, Language & Literacy
tpack_ck_labels: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; Humanities, Language & Literacy
abstract: This article proposes a framework for designing and implementing a curriculum that develops coding and literacy skills in children ages 5 to 8 using the ScratchJr App worldwide. The Coding as Another Language (CAL) for ScratchJr curriculum is a pedagogical resource developed by the DevTech Research Group to teach computing to young children expressively and creatively and to prepare educators to cultivate positive and effective knowledge constructions using a symbolic representation system. In this study, the CAL curriculum is utilized by different organizations worldwide, all of whom create their unique adaptations and expansions, exemplifying the process of developing culturally responsive pedagogical resources.

title: From Drawing to Understanding: Constructionist Approaches in Teaching Complex Biology Concepts
citation: Chowdhury, M., Azhuvath, A., & Rao, A. (2024). From Drawing to Understanding: Constructionist Approaches in Teaching Complex Biology Concepts. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2141-2142). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Chowdhury, M., Azhuvath, A., & Rao, A.
subject: STEM - Natural Science
abstract: This paper investigates the efficacy of constructionist learning framework in enhancing students’ understanding of complex biological concepts. Utilizing a pre-and post-survey along with practical drawing exercises, this study the learners’ experiences change in confidence and comprehension. Results indicate a significant increase in learners’ confidence post-survey. It also implies a connection between hands-on drawing activities and improved conceptual understanding.

title: Cultivating Collaborative Wisdom: A Community of Practice Approach to Quantitative Ethnography
citation: Shah, M., Barany, A., & Eagan, B. (2024). Cultivating Collaborative Wisdom: A Community of Practice Approach to Quantitative Ethnography. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2143-2144). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Shah, M., Barany, A., & Eagan, B.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
conceptualisations_list: Communities of Practice & Situated Learning; Epistemic Network Analysis (ENA)
abstract: A growing number of learning scientists are applying quantitative ethnography (QE) to investigate patterns in complex behavior across a variety of contexts, constructs, and cultures. We adopt a community of practice lens to reflect on activities and principles that enable emerging and senior scholars to conduct QE research. We invite a community discussion on additional ways for lowering floors, raising ceilings, and widening walls.

title: Do Undergraduates Use the Criterion of Fit with Multiple Lines of Evidence When Evaluating Conflicting Scientific Claims?
citation: Yamaguchi, E., Chinn, C. A., Oura, H., & Mochizuki, T. (2024). Do Undergraduates Use the Criterion of Fit with Multiple Lines of Evidence When Evaluating Conflicting Scientific Claims?. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2145-2146). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Yamaguchi, E., Chinn, C. A., Oura, H., & Mochizuki, T.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Evidence is especially powerful when there are multiple lines of converging evidence. However, little is currently known about how laypersons think about such evidence. Therefore, we conducted an experiment to investigate whether non-science-major undergraduates use the criterion of fit with multiple lines of evidence when evaluating conflicting scientific claims on dinosaur metabolism. We found that the undergraduates used the criterion of fit with multiple lines of evidence when one theory was supported by multiple lines of evidence whereas the other theory was supported by single line of evidence.

title: Teacher’s Understanding and Attitude about “Ideas” Related Principles in a Knowledge Building Pedagogy Training Course
citation: Seet, C., Hong, H., Wang, L., & Lau, S. (2024). Teacher’s Understanding and Attitude about “Ideas” Related Principles in a Knowledge Building Pedagogy Training Course. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2147-2148). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Seet, C., Hong, H., Wang, L., & Lau, S.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
abstract: The study explores teachers’ understanding of four knowledge-building principles. The four principles include (1) Real ideas, authentic problems, (2) Improvable ideas, (3) Idea diversity, and (4) Rise above. Data were gathered from 55 teachers. An open coding process was conducted, paired-t-test and ANOVA were performed. Results revealed gaps between teachers’ self-rated understanding and an expert’s assessment of the participants’ understanding of these four principles. Some suggestions were proposed for practical implications.

title: Coordinating Multiple Equations that Model Complex Systems
citation: Fu, G. & Lira, M. (2024). Coordinating Multiple Equations that Model Complex Systems. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2149-2150). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Fu, G. & Lira, M.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Complex systems demand multiple representations to characterize changes to their physical and quantitative properties. We sought to determine how undergraduate students coordinated multiple equations that modeled a system in two distinct situations. Results revealed that learning experiences with a multi-representational computational environment prompted students to shift from describing calculations and quantitative dependencies to coordinating the conceptual meanings between equations. We describe how this proof of existence informs theory and the design of future learning technologies.

title: A Chemistry-Based Escape Room as a Tool for Teachers to Assess Student Thinking
citation: Saleh, A. & Avargil, S. (2024). A Chemistry-Based Escape Room as a Tool for Teachers to Assess Student Thinking. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2151-2152). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Saleh, A. & Avargil, S.
subject: STEM - Natural Science
abstract: This study explores chemistry teachers' formative assessment (FA) knowledge and approaches in a collaborative dynamic learning environment through professional noticing and FA frameworks. Observation worksheets and perception questionnaires were collected from 36 high school chemistry teachers. A mixed method design is employed. Five categories were identified based on the results of the teacher perception questionnaire. Furthermore, three dimensions of noticing were identified. Our study will contribute to teachers' professional knowledge about assessment and FA.

title: Learning about NLP in Middle School Science
citation: Chakraburty, S., Hmelo-Silver, C. E., Glazewski, K., Katuka, G., Celepkolu, M., & Boyer, K. E. (2024). Learning about NLP in Middle School Science. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2153-2154). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Chakraburty, S., Hmelo-Silver, C. E., Glazewski, K., Katuka, G., Celepkolu, M., & Boyer, K. E.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: In this paper, we examine an inquiry-based learning approach in which students employed NLP techniques such as sentiment analysis and keyword extraction to investigate an environmental conservation issue. They used a digital platform to analyze public opinions about single-use plastic straws. The pre-test/post-test study showed significant gains across all subconstructs.

title: Examining the Role of Flow in a Technology-Rich Learning Environment
citation: Tan, C., Wang, T., & Lajoie, S. (2024). Examining the Role of Flow in a Technology-Rich Learning Environment. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2155-2156). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Tan, C., Wang, T., & Lajoie, S.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Experiencing flow while learning is typically linked to positive learning results. This study investigates the relationship between 111 medical students' self-regulated learning (SRL), mental effort, flow experience, and the resulting learning outcomes students as they learn clinical reasoning skills in the context of an intelligent tutoring system. The findings suggest that mental effort mediates the relationship between SRL and the experience of flow. Moreover, the study reveals that students' flow experiences positively predict their diagnostic accuracy.

title: Trauma-Informed Tertiary Systems: A Quantitative Pilot Study
citation: Reinhardt, S., Bailie, A. L., & Berke, D. L. (2024). Trauma-Informed Tertiary Systems: A Quantitative Pilot Study. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2157-2158). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Reinhardt, S., Bailie, A. L., & Berke, D. L.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: While higher educational instructors have been leading the charge to implement trauma-informed practices, less is known about how university systems address trauma. This pilot study enlisted college instructors and administrators (N=44) to complete a 51-question survey to determine their knowledge and use of trauma-informed practices within their institutions. Descriptive statistics were used to characterize the level of understanding of trauma-informed practices in Institutes of Higher Education (IHE). Results indicate trauma aware, sensitive, responsive, and informed practices in higher education were generally low.

title: Teacher Candidates Leveraging Children’s Picture Books to Plan Equity-Oriented Instruction
citation: Plummer, J. D. & Vanderhoof, C. (2024). Teacher Candidates Leveraging Children’s Picture Books to Plan Equity-Oriented Instruction. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2159-2160). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Plummer, J. D. & Vanderhoof, C.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This study investigates how teacher candidates utilize children’s science picture books to design equity and social justice-oriented lessons. Teachers drew on references to diversity, equity, and social justice represented in the books, indicating the importance of high-quality resources for beginning teachers and demonstrating the teachers’ potential for criticality.

title: Social and Emotional Learning (SEL) in Elementary Engineering Education
citation: Pangan, T. J. & Wendell, K. (2024). Social and Emotional Learning (SEL) in Elementary Engineering Education. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2161-2162). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Pangan, T. J. & Wendell, K.
subject: STEM - Engineering & Robotics; Humanities, Language & Literacy
tpack_ck_labels: STEM - Engineering & Robotics; Humanities, Language & Literacy
abstract: Although social and emotional learning (SEL) has become more commonplace in schools, currently available frameworks (e.g., CASEL) do not detail how SEL can be used in the elementary engineering context. Using secondary analysis of transcript excerpts from the literature, this project explores which specific SEL competencies are beneficial for elementary students engaged in engineering group work and attempts to demonstrate how SEL has a place in engineering education.
