citation: Kim, B., Bastani, R., Gierus, B., Clyde, J., & Poppendorf, A. (2024). Redesigning Tabletop Games as a Culturally Sustaining Pedagogy in Canadian Middle School Classrooms. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2163-2164). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Kim, B., Bastani, R., Gierus, B., Clyde, J., & Poppendorf, A.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: We present our study of middle school students in Canada exploring tabletop game redesign as a culturally sustaining pedagogy. The teachers and the researchers co-designed the activities and data was collected on the students’ engagement with the activities and each other. We describe the design of activities and preliminary findings.

title: Is Block-Based Programming “Real Programming”?
citation: Lin, Y., Weintrop, D., & McKenna, J. (2024). Is Block-Based Programming “Real Programming”?. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2165-2166). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Lin, Y., Weintrop, D., & McKenna, J.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
abstract: This study explores high school students' perceptions of "real programming" in the context of block-based programming environments, specifically focusing on VEXcode and Scratch. The research found students held diverging views on the authenticity of block-based programming. These findings present a more nuance view on students’ perceptions of block-based programming, showing that attribution of authenticity extends beyond block-based interface itself to also include the environment its situated in and the programming tasks and capabilities it supports.

title: An Evidence-centered and Process-oriented Assessment of Computational Thinking for Learners with Autism
citation: Zhang, N., Ke, F., Barrett, A., & Sokolikj, Z. (2024). An Evidence-centered and Process-oriented Assessment of Computational Thinking for Learners with Autism. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2167-2168). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Zhang, N., Ke, F., Barrett, A., & Sokolikj, Z.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
abstract: Currently, there is a lack of established computational thinking (CT) assessment that is sensitive to the unique needs of learners with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). This paper proposed an evidence-centered, process-oriented CT competency model consisting of three constructs: computational analysis, computational practices, and dispositions. The model was pilot-tested with 61 data points collected from two adolescents with autism for up to 15 months. Principal component analysis was adopted to assess the structural validity of the proposed model. We then used correlation analysis to verify the convergent and discriminant validity. Preliminary results indicated that the empirical data generally supports the outlined structure of this theory-driven model and the orthogonality of the constructs.

title: When One Tutor Handles Students from Different Educational Levels: Their Dialogic Interactions in Online One-on-one Tutoring
citation: Wang, D., Gao, L., Niu, X., Chen, G., & Chai, C. (2024). When One Tutor Handles Students from Different Educational Levels: Their Dialogic Interactions in Online One-on-one Tutoring. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2169-2170). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Wang, D., Gao, L., Niu, X., Chen, G., & Chai, C.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: To investigate how a single tutor interacts with students from different educational levels in online one-on-one tutoring, this study analyzed 300 dialogues from these tutors and students using epistemic network analysis. Our findings reveal that when tutoring higher-grade-level students, tutors employed a higher frequency of constructive questions. Tutors’ knowledge-sharing and instruction strategies were related to advanced constructive expressions among students at higher educational levels, while primary school students primarily demonstrated simple acknowledgement without constructive engagement.

title: Fostering Lesson Plan Design Competence via Knowledge Building in Teacher Education
citation: Wu, F., Hong, H., & Wang, L. (2024). Fostering Lesson Plan Design Competence via Knowledge Building in Teacher Education. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2171-2172). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Wu, F., Hong, H., & Wang, L.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This study compares eight SDGs lesson plans using the framework of the 12 principles of knowledge building, aiming to assess the quality of lesson plan design competence among teacher trainees. The findings show that cultivation through the concept of knowledge building assists teacher trainees in enhancing their lesson plan design competence. However, some differences remain between the instructional approaches of teacher trainees and those of award-winning teachers regarding ideas, agents, and community.

title: Neuromyths About Learning and the Allure of Neuroscience
citation: Guley, O., Pasquinelli, E., Zenasni, F., & Mercier, H. (2024). Neuromyths About Learning and the Allure of Neuroscience. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2173-2174). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Guley, O., Pasquinelli, E., Zenasni, F., & Mercier, H.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Research has shown that neuromyths — misconceptions about the brain, learning, and development — are prevalent among educators and the general public. The seductive allure of neuroscience explanations suggests that even irrelevant neuroscientific explanations enhance information appeal. The present study examined if neuromyths become more credible and shareable among the general public when paired with irrelevant neuroscientific explanations. Findings indicate no increase in credibility or shareability. Further research is needed to determine the origins of neuromyth prevalence.

title: Problems of Practice in Scaling Computational Thinking and Digital Literacies in Pre-service Teacher Education Efforts
citation: Phelps, D., Santo, R., Vogel, S., Patel, A., Angevine, C., & Tello, J. V. (2024). Problems of Practice in Scaling Computational Thinking and Digital Literacies in Pre-service Teacher Education Efforts. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2175-2176). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Phelps, D., Santo, R., Vogel, S., Patel, A., Angevine, C., & Tello, J. V.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; Humanities, Language & Literacy
tpack_ck_labels: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; Humanities, Language & Literacy
abstract: This poster presents a holistic characterization of the problems of practice that emerge as faculty in colleges of education work to scale institution-wide integration of computational and digital literacies across teacher education programs. By identifying the thorny issues inherent to institutional change this analysis supports teacher educators working to transform teacher preparation programs to center teacher candidates’ computing integration.

title: Sowing Seeds for Applying Productive Failure to Reading: Pre-Reading Questions Alone are Not Enough to Reap the Benefits
citation: Carpenter, Z., Cromley, J., & Van Boekel, M. (2024). Sowing Seeds for Applying Productive Failure to Reading: Pre-Reading Questions Alone are Not Enough to Reap the Benefits. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2177-2178). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Carpenter, Z., Cromley, J., & Boekel, M. V.
subject: STEM - Natural Science; Humanities, Language & Literacy
tpack_ck_labels: STEM - Natural Science; Humanities, Language & Literacy
abstract: There is no known work mapping Productive Failure (PF)—a popular pedagogical design within the Learning Sciences—to reading. Therefore, through a secondary data analysis of students reading several expository biology excerpts, the current work attempts to bridge PF and reading. One group of students answered questions before reading the passages, while the other group did not. The results revealed that pre-reading questions had no effect on the acquisition of causal language, but the different passages did affect causal language pickup.

title: Supporting collaborative learning and/or knowledge building in initial teacher education using video: a systematic review with PRISMA
citation: Monginho, R., De Jong, F., Velazquez-Godinez, E., & Costa, P. (2024). Supporting collaborative learning and/or knowledge building in initial teacher education using video: a systematic review with PRISMA. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2179-2180). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Monginho, R., Jong, F. D., Velazquez-Godinez, E., & Costa, P.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This paper reviews the use of video technologies in teacher education, focusing on how they enhance collaborative learning and knowledge building. The review follows the PRISMA methodology and analyzes 35 peer-reviewed papers published in English between 2000 and 2023. Three main video modalities of use were identified: "Video Recording," "Video-Based Content," and "Live Video Conferencing." The findings show that video technologies play a crucial role in collaborative learning and knowledge building in teacher education. "Video Recording" supports reflective practices and collaborative self-improvement among educators. "Video-Based Content" provides access to high-quality resources, fostering collaborative learning and knowledge building. Although less studied, "Live Video Conferencing" offers real-time interaction and collaboration opportunities. This review highlights the growing importance of video technologies in shaping teacher education and emphasizes the need for further research to fully unleash their potential.

title: Haptic Experiences Shape Student-Generated Gestures While Learning with Computational Environments
citation: Tang, X., Lindgren, R., & Lira, M. (2024). Haptic Experiences Shape Student-Generated Gestures While Learning with Computational Environments. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 218-225). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Tang, X., Lindgren, R., & Lira, M.
subject: STEM - Natural Science
abstract: In science education, gestures have emerged as a valuable tool for both students to represent their reasoning and educators to assess learners’ developing knowledge. One reason is that gestures afford representing dynamic causal reasoning, a fundamental aspect of understanding various natural phenomena. However, gestures inherently lack feedback mechanisms and are possibly epiphenomenal to learning. We address these limitations by pairing haptic physical models with a computational NetLogo simulation designed to support students in comprehending dynamic interactions within complex systems. In this study, we investigated the impact of haptic learning experiences and computational environments on student-generated gestures. Our findings revealed that haptic learning experiences augment the computational environments by providing students with sensory feedback. This, in turn, leads to a shift in students' gestures, as they transition from representing aggregate patterns, such as quantity and motion, to individual interactions between physical entities and forces.

title: MakingSEL: Integrating Maker Education with Social Emotional Learning in Teacher Professional Development
citation: Kafri, R. & Berland, M. (2024). MakingSEL: Integrating Maker Education with Social Emotional Learning in Teacher Professional Development. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2181-2182). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Kafri, R. & Berland, M.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
abstract: This research poster delves into the integration of Maker Education and Social Emotional Learning (SEL) through the lens of the MakingSEL program. Aimed at educators and teacher educators, the program blends hands-on making activities with SEL principles to enrich teaching practices. Through physical and online sessions, participants explored collaborative making experiences, fostering creativity, problem-solving, and interpersonal skills. The poster presents the MakingSEL program’s structure, observed outcomes, and implications for practice and future education research.

title: Maintaining Academic Buoyancy in Higher Education: The Moderation Analysis of Age and Gender
citation: Dang, A. H. & Middlemiss, W. (2024). Maintaining Academic Buoyancy in Higher Education: The Moderation Analysis of Age and Gender. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2183-2184). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Dang, A. H. & Middlemiss, W.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Academic buoyancy refers to a student's ability to overcome common learning-related challenges or setbacks encountered in school. The present study aims to examine the relation between age and gender and university students' reported academic buoyancy. Students from a Minority-serving and Hispanic-serving public higher education in Texas (N=118) completed an online survey assessing their academic buoyancy. On average, women reported having lower academic buoyancy than men. Further, age and gender play a notable role in predicting academic buoyancy. Finally, there was no differential effect of age on the academic buoyancy of women compared to men.

title: Design of XR Technology to Prompt Deeper Psychomotor Skills Learning
citation: Yuvaraja, H. K., Koszalka, T. A., & Huang, X. (2024). Design of XR Technology to Prompt Deeper Psychomotor Skills Learning. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2185-2186). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Yuvaraja, H. K., Koszalka, T. A., & Huang, X.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Advanced extended reality (XR) technologies in psychomotor skill learning (PSL) offer promising implications to accelerate the learning process and enhance learning outcomes. The proposed prototype explores the intricate PSL mechanisms focusing on mental processing and motor body movements to achieve deeper PSL. The design of XR technology aligns with generative learning theory driving both mental processing and motor processing in PSL, with a goal to foster more effective and efficient PSL.

title: Integrated STEM: Student Sensemaking Across Time
citation: Klukowski, L. (2024). Integrated STEM: Student Sensemaking Across Time. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2187-2188). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Klukowski, L.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Many integrated STEM frameworks focus on disciplinary ideas that students learn through integrated STEM activities. They may hide how students experience and coordinate disciplinary ideas and practices in schools as they make sense of STEM problems. This poster introduces a theoretical framework that conceptualizes integrated STEM from a perspective of student sensemaking as students experience disciplinary thinking at different time scales and illustrates how it could be used to explore teacher questioning in integrated STEM.

title: Exploring Equity-Oriented Shifts in Teacher Candidates’ Noticing
citation: Kim, M. & Pierson, A. (2024). Exploring Equity-Oriented Shifts in Teacher Candidates’ Noticing. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2189-2190). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Kim, M. & Pierson, A.
subject: STEM - Mathematics
abstract: Many studies have investigated mathematics teacher noticing. Building on this research, we explore how the Framing-Attending-Interpreting-Responding (FAIR) framework (Louie et al., 2021) enhances understanding of teacher candidates’ noticing and how video clubs (van Es & Sherin, 2008) can support teacher candidates’ equitable noticing. Our findings demonstrate (1) how the FAIR framework can help researchers attend to the sociopolitical framing that influences noticing and (2) how video clubs can support teacher candidates’ equitable noticing.

title: “The Big Payback”: Using Culturally-Centered Curriculum to Retain Historically Marginalized Students in STEM
citation: McClain, J. (2024). “The Big Payback”: Using Culturally-Centered Curriculum to Retain Historically Marginalized Students in STEM. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2191-2192). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: McClain, J.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Students from historically marginalized communities frequently struggle to connect to STEM at the postsecondary level. This action research study looked at the impact of developing STEM curriculum for historically underserved STEM majors at a Midwestern university. Using culturally based instruction, the results show that the knowledge of marginalized students can be used as a resource in STEM learning environments.

title: How Research Practice Partnerships Build Comfort and Strengthen Collaborations as Research Agendas Shift
citation: Lawrence, L., Jones, B., Solola, I., & Swanson, H. (2024). How Research Practice Partnerships Build Comfort and Strengthen Collaborations as Research Agendas Shift. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2193-2194). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Lawrence, L., Jones, B., Solola, I., & Swanson, H.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Setting a research agenda that is mutually beneficial for teachers and researchers is a challenging part of a research practice partnership. Our paper examines how our engagement shifted as our research agenda changed. Our findings show increased teacher contributions as our research agenda changed. We discuss how our collaboration shifted as the trajectory of our research agenda moved out of the researchers' hands and more into the teachers' hands.

title: A Multi-Level Framework for Exploring the AI interaction through Joint Reasoning
citation: Walton, D. & Bae, H. (2024). A Multi-Level Framework for Exploring the AI interaction through Joint Reasoning. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2195-2196). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Walton, D. & Bae, H.
subject: Humanities, Language & Literacy
abstract: Conversational AI, like GPT-4, has grown in sophistication, necessitating an evolved understanding of human-AI interaction. There is a notable lack of comprehensive understanding in the literature regarding the progression of human-AI interactions, particularly in contexts of joint reasoning. Our research extends Graesser's question classification scheme into a multi-level framework that captures the complexity of user inquiries, from simple fact-checking to meta-cognitive exploration, informed by educational, cognitive, and HCI theories.

title: Using Digital Games to Enhance 21st-Century Skills Development in K-12 Education: A Systematic Review
citation: Esmaeiligoujar, S., Rahimi, S., & Babaee, M. (2024). Using Digital Games to Enhance 21st-Century Skills Development in K-12 Education: A Systematic Review. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2197-2198). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Esmaeiligoujar, S., Rahimi, S., & Babaee, M.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: In today’s rapidly evolving landscape, 21st-century skills such as creativity and problem-solving are indispensable. Digital games present a promising medium to cultivate these essential competencies. In this systematic review, we examine the impact of digital games on nurturing K-12 students’ 21st-century skills, drawing on a rigorous analysis of 81 selected studies. This paper offers a synthesis of our initial findings.

title: Storied Community-Based Learning Environments: Designing with Storywork, Storylistening, and Narrative Inquiry
citation: Killen, H. & Hock, A. (2024). Storied Community-Based Learning Environments: Designing with Storywork, Storylistening, and Narrative Inquiry. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2199-2200). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Killen, H. & Hock, A.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: We explore how the methodologies of Storywork, Storylistening, and Narrative Inquiry can support community-engaged scholarship. We discuss the varying approaches to storying contained within these three traditions and suggest that community-engaged scholars can benefit from drawing on elements of each to (1) consider the value of place-stories circulating within research spaces, and (2) to design educational spaces that convene a diversity of place-stories, further enriching and complicating researcher engagement with stories.

title: Identifying Pedagogical Opportunities for Text Data Visualizations in English Language Arts through Co-Design
citation: Lee, V. R., Abdi, D., Coelho, R., Bywater, C., Levine, S., & Demszky, D. (2024). Identifying Pedagogical Opportunities for Text Data Visualizations in English Language Arts through Co-Design. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. authors_list: Lee, V. R., Abdi, D., Coelho, R., Bywater, C., Levine, S., & Demszky, D.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This poster reports on analyses of transcripts from seven co-design sessions between researchers and educators to identify pedagogical opportunities for including text data visualization in middle-grade English Language Arts (ELA). Findings include educators' nuanced preferences for word clouds, bar graphs, and line graphs and interests in visualizations for comprehension and multilingual student support as well as the use of student-authored texts.

title: Integrating Knowledge Forum to Support Knowledge Building among Adult Learners
citation: Lin, F. (2024). Integrating Knowledge Forum to Support Knowledge Building among Adult Learners. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2203-2204). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Lin, F.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This study explores the integration of Knowledge Forum (KF) in face-to-face classes to support adult learners’ knowledge building. 10 early childhood educators joined this study while they attended a master course. Qualitative analysis of classroom observation showed how KF was integrated into face-to-face classes to foster knowledge-building among adult learners. The insights have implications for the future design of knowledge building for adult learners.

title: Fostering a Sense of Belonging in Children of Persian-speaking Immigrants through an Interactive Mobile App
citation: Hadinezhad, S., Garg, S., Halsi, A. S., & Shahi, S. (2024). Fostering a Sense of Belonging in Children of Persian-speaking Immigrants through an Interactive Mobile App. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2205-2206). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Hadinezhad, S., Garg, S., Halsi, A. S., & Shahi, S.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This paper examines the challenges faced by the children of Persian-speaking immigrants to learn their heritage language, and provides them with a culturally rich, multi-modal pedagogy. Being a complex language, along with the absence of engaging learning resources, makes learning Persian challenging outside of Iran. In solution, an interactive mobile app is proposed, immersing children in a joyful learning experience that seeks to enhance their Persian language acquisition and foster their sense of belonging.

title: Teaching Data for Power: Exploring Mathematics Teachers’ Perspectives on Data Literacy
citation: Metts, E. (2024). Teaching Data for Power: Exploring Mathematics Teachers’ Perspectives on Data Literacy. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2207-2208). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Metts, E.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; STEM - Mathematics; Humanities, Language & Literacy; Social & Civic Studies
tpack_ck_labels: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; STEM - Mathematics; Humanities, Language & Literacy; Social & Civic Studies
abstract: This study explores experienced mathematics teachers' views on data science in classrooms, acknowledging complexities from the social and cultural dimensions of data. While the push for data literacy aligns with democratic participation and economic success, teachers' perspectives are understudied. Grounded in a situative view of teacher learning, this exploratory case of two focal teachers suggests teachers see data literacy not only as a means of making mathematics relevant but also as a tool for critical awareness, empowering students to challenge, critique, and access power.

title: Achievify’s Learning-Centric and AI-powered Guide to Charting Career Paths
citation: Bowles, S. & Dinç, E. (2024). Achievify’s Learning-Centric and AI-powered Guide to Charting Career Paths. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2209-2210). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Bowles, S. & Dinç, E.
subject: Humanities, Language & Literacy
abstract: We introduced Achievify, a platform for AI-powered career guidance designed specifically for underserved communities. It emphasizes inclusivity and removes obstacles to accessibility by utilizing machine learning and natural language processing to provide simple navigation and career prediction. In addition to providing a dynamic employment information database, Achievify promotes educational advancement by introducing users to a range of career options, improving digital literacy, and encouraging lifelong learning.

title: A Dichotomy of Demonstrated vs. Perceived Knowledge in Computer Security
citation: Jensen, M. (2024). A Dichotomy of Demonstrated vs. Perceived Knowledge in Computer Security. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2211-2212). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Jensen, M.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
abstract: One approach to teaching computer security in undergraduate computer science (CS) programs is to enforce and distribute it across the curriculum. Topics accessible at even the earliest of levels (CS0, CS1, CS2) have been identified and tools studied to teach them. However, we do not know much about the process, understanding, or knowledge that students bring in when doing computer security without any coursework in computer security. We employ a series of think-aloud programming sessions and short interviews following the format of Build-it, Break-it, Fix-it (BIBIFI) competitions. In this paper, we take a closer look at one build-it session in which the actions and words of the participant conflict with their perception of being capable of doing computer security.

title: Little Logic Adventure: A Game for Learning Integrated Math and Coding in Early Elementary Classrooms
citation: Zandi, A., Ashineh, A., & Clarke-Midura, J. (2024). Little Logic Adventure: A Game for Learning Integrated Math and Coding in Early Elementary Classrooms. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; STEM - Mathematics
tpack_ck_labels: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; STEM - Mathematics
abstract: In this poster, we present “Little Logic Adventure," a digital game designed for kindergarten students that integrates computational thinking (CT) with foundational math skills. The game is designed around a cognitive model of early childhood CT and mathematics standards for kindergarten. Children complete tasks where they apply their math and CT skills concurrently. The game is designed for use in early childhood classrooms and to provide teachers with a tool for integrating CT and mathematics.

abstract: This study followed and analyzed the practices of a group of young Arab instructors (YAIs) as they facilitated STEM outreach activities in Arab schools throughout Israel. Using the construct of Figured Worlds, it unpacks the social construction and negotiation of power relations in the classroom, highlights conflicts between the YAIs and teachers, and the ways the YAIs enacted their critical agency.

subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; Humanities, Language & Literacy
tpack_ck_labels: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; Humanities, Language & Literacy
abstract: In the age of generative AI (GenAI), it is crucial to prioritize the prevalence of GenAI and its effect on student learning. This study explores how students can benefit from feedback generated by GenAI in learning programming. Applying a qualitative descriptive approach in research, the findings show that students' interactions with the GenAI-chatbot, their attitudes, and the amount of time they spend reading, comprehending, and applying the bot's feedback all impact how effective the bot is. The findings of the study will help instructors understand how best to support their students in learning programming with a GenAI-chatbot and provide crucial evidence to advance the field of educational technology development.

abstract: This is a work-in-progress case study aiming to understand university instructors’ sensemaking and learning in Knowledge Building professional development. We examined the sensemaking process of two instructors: one with the highest learning gains and one with the least learning gains in a PD program. We found that the instructors with greater learning gains adopted more assimilation and accommodations, while the instructor with the least gains displayed more toleration and distantiation while interacting with others in the classroom.

abstract: A quasi-experimental study was conducted to investigate the effect of gesture on students' spatial learning. 132 students were randomly assigned to the gesture condition and the non-gesture condition to learn cube folding and unfolding. Based on students’ behavioral data, we found that students in the non-gesture condition would check the tips at the beginning of game, whereas students in the gesture condition tended to try to solve the problem first before checking the tips.

subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This study addresses resource-rich assessments, using interactive simulations, compared to traditional resource-poor assessments to detect differences in learning outcomes induced by two different learning approaches. Students' reasoning about complex relationships within scientific phenomena was assessed. 71 undergraduate students completed resource-poor pretest, exploration task using interactive simulation (before or after instruction) and resource-poor and resource-rich posttests. Results show that resource-rich assessments do not offer significant advantages over resource-poor assessments, regardless of the learning approach utilized.

abstract: This study systematically reviewed 117 articles that contained at least one of the four elements of embodiment (an articulation of the learning environment design) in the conjecture map. We found differences in the use of the four elements: Discursive practices were the least used. Our analysis using word clouds suggests that such limited use of discursive practices might result from the greater challenge of locating discursive practices than other elements in the embodiment.

This poster shares conjecture maps driving two iterations of a professional learning institute for education faculty, and rationale for revisions made, finding that the second iteration acknowledged the need for more situated definitions and conceptions of equity.

abstract: Our poster explores visualization methods for participation in an identity-aligned, multiplayer video game world for learning data science through relationship and community building. We extend methods of representing engagement and learning in both educational games and in data science education contexts. Using simulated game play data and screen capture records of interviews with middle school girls playing an early version of the game, we explore representations for individual and multiplayer learning.

subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Peer-feedback can be supported by formal or subject-matter-related scaffolds. However, it is unclear whether these scaffolds differ in their effects on process-related and outcome-related variables. In our meta-analysis including N=22 studies with N=2.473 learners, results show a statistically significant effect only for subject-matter-related scaffolds on process-related variables. The lack of further effects might represent a power problem, i.e., more research is necessary to judge the effectiveness of the different scaffolds on process and outcome-related variables.

abstract: The objective of this research was to explore how educators and researchers can collaborate to create research-to-practice briefs that make research accessible for classroom implementation. Specifically, we examined the benefits, opportunities, and difficulties of working together. While there were challenges, our findings suggest that both researchers and teachers can benefit from collaborating. This pilot research is shaping future work to further bridge the gap between research and practice.

title: Cocreative Llearning is More Effective than Direct Instruction Argument on Basis of Hanna Arendt’s Vita Activa
citation: De Jong, F., van den Brande, K., Bent, M., Bernasco, B., & Monginho, R. (2024). Cocreative Llearning is More Effective than Direct Instruction Argument on Basis of Hanna Arendt’s Vita Activa. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. authors_list: Jong, F. D., Brande, K. V. D., Bent, M., Bernasco, B., & Monginho, R.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: When learning must contribute to resilience, and community cocreative learning is more effective than direct instruction. This position paper draws on Hannah Arendt’s Vita Activa: Labor, Work, and Speech and Action. Labor is about meeting basic needs and creating a ‘home’ where life is good. Work concerns creating languages and culture and therefore an artificial world. Speech and Action involve organizing society and engaging in politics.Linking learning and education to the Vita Activa, an educational picture emerges that mainly focuses on Labor and Work, with a strong emphasis on direct instruction and the acquisition of skills and knowledge. Speech and Action, e.g., the development of ideas and working together for a better world, remain underdeveloped in education. Direct instruction may be efficient, but it is not effective in view of our overall development as human beings. Space is needed for idea development, co-creation, knowledge building, and dialogical learning.

title: Capturing Interdisciplinary Dialogic Argumentation among Science Teachers: An Analysis of Epistemic Practices in a Dialogue
citation: Perl-Nussbaum, D., Schwarz, B. B., & Yerushalmi, E. (2024). Capturing Interdisciplinary Dialogic Argumentation among Science Teachers: An Analysis of Epistemic Practices in a Dialogue. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2239-2240). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Perl-Nussbaum, D., Schwarz, B. B., & Yerushalmi, E.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
abstract: Research in the learning sciences has recognized dialogic argumentation as a key approach to enhance learning. Productive features of such dialogues include openness to alternative perspectives, critical examination, and collaborative knowledge construction. Such deliberation is difficult to achieve within the compartmentalized structure of traditional science teaching, which hinders the exploration of different perspectives on a scientific problem. We propose interdisciplinarity as a means to promote deliberativeness in the discourse of science teachers from different disciplinary backgrounds. We introduce a quantitative coding instrument to examine both the dialogic and epistemic aspects of teachers' discourse and to account for deliberation through the integration of different disciplinary epistemic practices.

title: From Prompt to Paper: A Case Analysis of AI and Academic Writing
citation: Adam, K. & Chowdhury, M. (2024). From Prompt to Paper: A Case Analysis of AI and Academic Writing. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. authors_list: Adam, K. & Chowdhury, M.
subject: STEM - Engineering & Robotics; Humanities, Language & Literacy
tpack_ck_labels: STEM - Engineering & Robotics; Humanities, Language & Literacy
abstract: This paper critically examines the role of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), specifically ChatGPT and Grammarly, in supporting academic writing with a focus on the role of prompt engineering. The study centers on a case involving a college sophomore who employs these AI tools to complete an English composition assignment. We evaluate how AI chatbots potentially enhance knowledge construction and academic performance through the lens of the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT), constructionist theory, and social cognitive theory. The paper also explores the ethical considerations regarding the use of AI in academic writing, including issues of attribution and intellectual property, which are of the most importance. The study underscores the urgent need to develop comprehensive rules and guidelines for AI use in educational settings, ensuring responsible integration that contributes positively to the educational process.

abstract: Data science has garnered interest in K-12 education and has catalyzed designs conducive to learning experiences that integrate data science, disciplinary content, and justice issues. This poster reports on recent progress made by a project that integrates data science in secondary science and history classes following a justice-oriented data science education framework. Teacher debrief meetings after two classroom pilots revealed both productive seeds of justice-oriented data science and opportunities to refine the designed support.

abstract: We draw on constructionism to design a group rope weaving activity as an illustration of concepts in matrix algebra. The study, conducted in an undergraduate Informatics class, involved a rope-weaving activity to assess the concept of cloth separability and the matrix representation of weaving patterns. Results showed significant learning gains, with distinct approaches observed: one group emphasizing physical manipulation, the other relying on mathematical principles. This study underscores the value of tangible engagement in understanding abstract concepts.

abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become integrated into students’ daily lives. It is crucial to expose young students to AI knowledge early on to build core competencies. In this poster, we showcase how a facilitator scaffolded student groups to connect their design ideas with learned AI concepts in their final presentations of a design problem solving project and how those interactions were turned into meaningful learning moments for the entire class at an AI summer camp.

The development and content validation of the instrument will be shared and discussion of the ongoing research will be included.

citation: Li, X. & Zhang, Y. (2024). PM2.5 Exposure and Student’s Classroom Learning: A Mediation Analysis. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This study investigates the influence of short-term exposure to PM2.5 on students' classroom learning. Linear mixed effects models reveal that increased exposure to PM2.5 before class reduces mental effort (standardized coefficient: -12.80%; 95% CI: -2.30%, -23.03%; p= 0.017) of students in class. Mediation analysis shows that cognitive regulation fully mediates PM2.5's impact on students' reduced mental effort. These findings suggest that low air quality may impede classroom learning, requiring greater attention.

abstract: Responding to calls for increasing learning sciences’ efforts to understand how people reason with online information, we present a methodological tool for qualitatively capturing epistemic engagement on social media. Drawing on the AIR framework and prior efforts to conceptualize epistemic engagement on social media, we developed a codebook to capture Aims, Ideals, and Reliable epistemic process. This contribution discusses this effort, and how it can be used to understand apt epistemic engagement on social media.

abstract: This empirical case study utilizes conjecture mapping to capture and systematically map conjectures about the support needed for K-12 teachers to incorporate computational thinking into teaching. The case analysis highlighted a teacher’s year-long professional development experience focused on integrating computational thinking. The evolving conjecture map provides a framework to trace and understand relationships between the learning designs, activities, and teacher outcomes. Using rich data from the teacher's experience, the study tests and refines the hypothesized connections laid out in the original conjecture map to build an understanding of effective computational thinking professional development design.

abstract: This study investigates how playwriting supports agency as an outcome of participation among a group of elementary school students. We engaged in a multimodal linguistic analysis of student agency, analyzing youth interview transcripts and creative artifacts to better understand students’ sense of intentionality, autonomy, and creative freedom within arts practices. This paper offers possibilities for a more comprehensive study of student agency in the arts by introducing a multimodal linguistic approach.

title: Transmuting Intellectual Liabilities into Assets for Engagement
citation: Liu, M., Rahmati, M., McElroy-Heltzel, S., & Lira, M. (2024). Transmuting Intellectual Liabilities into Assets for Engagement. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. abstract: Learners’ emotional experiences can lead to disciplinary engagement or abandonment. We aimed to determine how students early emotional experiences when learning during discomfort can be transmuted from liabilities into assets that promote engagement. To accomplish this aim we combine theories from Positive Psychology and Knowledge-in-Pieces. We triangulate surveys, clinical interviews, and physiological data (EDA) to determine the psychological mechanisms that underpin disciplinary engagement.

title: Which Bright Side to Look at? Cultivating Goal-oriented Shame Regulation Under Challenging Problem-Solving Contexts
citation: Wang, F., Sinha, T., & Kapur, M. (2024). Which Bright Side to Look at? Cultivating Goal-oriented Shame Regulation Under Challenging Problem-Solving Contexts. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
abstract: Emotion regulation in authentic learning settings has traditionally been understudied. In the context of problem-solving, understanding how students perceive their emotional experiences and how teachers can effectively facilitate emotion regulation remains unclear. In this study, we introduce an iteratively developed coding framework to examine how students navigate their feelings of shame, a hedonically negative emotion, while attempting problem-solving tasks intentionally designed to be challenging. Our qualitative findings reveal a notable increase in goal-oriented behaviors in the condition where students receive emotion regulation tips to maintain and utilize their shame, compared to conditions where students are provided with hedonic regulation tips or no guidance.

abstract: The study explores the factors influencing Chinese academic mothers’ course design decisions during the COVID-19 pandemic. A qualitative online survey followed by 10 in-depth interviews was conducted in 2022 with over 150 participants. Thematic analysis was used to analyze the survey and interview transcripts. The results highlighted the significance of spousal support and academic mothers’ motivation to sacrifice personally. The findings call for interventions that support academic mothers as course designers.

title: A Qualitative Look at Fostering Computational Thinking Within a Game-based Learning Environment
citation: Tseng, C., Pan, Y., Klinkert, L. J., Geller, L. K., Larson, E. C., & Clark, C. (2024). A Qualitative Look at Fostering Computational Thinking Within a Game-based Learning Environment. subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
abstract: This study explored how participants practice computational thinking (CT) concepts and skills while playing the game. Regarding 11 learning standards from the Computer Science Teacher Association (CSTA), researchers designed gameplay tasks in Minecraft and a supplemental platform called Minecraft Factory Planner (MFP). Data was collected through the cognitive walkthrough with a think-aloud method and semi-structured retrospective interview. One coder generated what game actions the players did while playing the game and the players’ words. Comparing the meaning of CT operational definition, we attempted to connect gameplay actions and CT skill practice. The preliminary findings showed the potential relationship between them.

title: Unveiling FlitGap's Program Success for Increasing Non-Dominant Group Participation in Computer Science Disciplines
citation: Nti-Asante, E. & Secules, S. (2024). Unveiling FlitGap's Program Success for Increasing Non-Dominant Group Participation in Computer Science Disciplines. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2265-2266). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Nti-Asante, E. & Secules, S.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
abstract: This study investigates the contextual practices driving the success of the Flit-GAP (Florida IT Graduation Attainment Pathways) project, a collaborative initiative funded by the NSF involving Florida International University, University of Central Florida, and University of South Florida. Despite the diminished attraction towards diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) projects and initiatives in the state, Flit-GAP has exhibited resilience in recruiting, retaining, and supporting academically talented yet financially challenged students, particularly those from non-dominant groups, to increase their participation in computing disciplines. By analyzing audio recordings, videos, and field notes from two case studies within Flit-GAP, this research systematically unveiled the critical roles of social and academic integration in driving the project's effectiveness in supporting students from diverse backgrounds in the computing field. Therefore, prioritizing both academic and social integration is recommended as valuable guidance for improving practices in other struggling contexts.

title: An Initial Systematic Review on Intersubjectivity and Play: a solid foundation for learning?
citation: Dario, N. & Lund, K. (2024). An Initial Systematic Review on Intersubjectivity and Play: a solid foundation for learning?. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2267-2268). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Dario, N. & Lund, K.
subject: Humanities, Language & Literacy
abstract: We use the PRISMA method to systematically explore the relationship between intersubjectivity and play. Ending with 54 papers, predominantly from developmental psychology, we assess how these themes are connected to learning. The study finds 6 initial gaps in the literature and notes a lack of interdisciplinarity. Gaps are related to methods, implicated disciplines, epistemological connections, subjects’ age, notion of play, and disorders.

title: Emerging Findings on Learning Transfer Between Novel Roles for Working Learners and Learning Workers
citation: Forshaw, T. & Longmire, M. (2024). Emerging Findings on Learning Transfer Between Novel Roles for Working Learners and Learning Workers. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2269-2270). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Forshaw, T. & Longmire, M.
subject: Social & Civic Studies
abstract: The study of learning transfer from a cognitive and sociocultural perspective has a long history. Nonetheless, there is a need for a deeper understanding and consideration of supporting learning transfer in contexts where working and learning co-occur. This qualitative study describes how learning transfer to novel roles is experienced in a multi-national consulting firm.

title: Evaluating Private Artificial Intelligence (AI) Curriculum in Computer Science (CS) Education: Insights for Advancing Student-Centered CS Learning
citation: Haddadian, G., Panzade, P., Takabi, D., & Kim, M. K. (2024). Evaluating Private Artificial Intelligence (AI) Curriculum in Computer Science (CS) Education: Insights for Advancing Student-Centered CS Learning. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2271-2272). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Haddadian, G., Panzade, P., Takabi, D., & Kim, M. K.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
abstract: This study was undertaken to pilot a Private AI curriculum designed with a problem-centered instruction (PCI) approach for post-secondary Computer Science (CS) education. To this end, a condensed version of one of the ten curricular modules was implemented in a two-hour workshop. The mixed-method data analysis revealed participants' positive motivation and interest in the curriculum, while also pinpointing opportunities to further improve the design strategies of the curriculum.

title: A Case of Middle Schoolers Reasoning with Multiple Models in Science Learning: Quantitative, Qualitative, or Both?
citation: Fackler, A. K., Zangori, L. A., Mahapatra, S., Xu, Z., & Sadler, T. D. (2024). A Case of Middle Schoolers Reasoning with Multiple Models in Science Learning: Quantitative, Qualitative, or Both?. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2273-2274). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Fackler, A. K., Zangori, L. A., Mahapatra, S., Xu, Z., & Sadler, T. D.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Most attention on model-based reasoning only explores how students reason either qualitatively or quantitatively. Opportunities to reason about a phenomenon using qualitative models and quantitative modeling have rarely been explored. Yet, scientists require fluid movement between these reasoning structures using models that are qualitative and quantitative. Therefore, this case study examined how middle school students shift back and forth between qualitative and quantitative reasoning through mechanistic and computational models to explain how respiratory diseases spread.

title: Knowledge Building Through Video Dialogues
citation: Beal, C. (2024). Knowledge Building Through Video Dialogues. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2275-2276). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Beal, C.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: In this study, we designed video mind maps in which preservice teachers could engage through video dialogues. The data analysis focuses on what characterizes the organization of the mind map and how it supports students’ knowledge-building practices by analyzing their interactions. Video-based mind maps afford students to produce video dialogues and build upon and negotiate knowledge introduced in peers’ video dialogues. As the mind map evolved, it became the interface for the students’ knowledge-building practices.

title: Reflections on Flexible and Constrained Agency as Affordances for Embodied Learning Design
citation: DeLiema, D., Lindgren, R., & Danish, J. (2024). Reflections on Flexible and Constrained Agency as Affordances for Embodied Learning Design. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2277-2278). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: DeLiema, D., Lindgren, R., & Danish, J.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: As one pathway toward generating more transparent and systematic descriptions of embodied learning design decisions, we integrate two design frameworks – the Learning in Embodied Activity Framework (LEAF) and another highlighting Viewpoint, Embodiment, and Roles – and foreground this synthesis in reflections on our own past design efforts. Through this reflection, we provide a generative account of how embodied designs constrain agency to give students more or less latitude in their movements as pathways to learning.

title: Using Teacher Feedback to Refine an Educational Video Game Evaluation Model
citation: Duvall, M., Chen, J., He, A., Lou, V., Shah, H., Shi, Y., Shuai, Y., & Tian, M. (2024). Using Teacher Feedback to Refine an Educational Video Game Evaluation Model. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2279-2280). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Duvall, M., Chen, J., He, A., Lou, V., Shah, H., Shi, Y., Shuai, Y., & Tian, M.
subject: Social & Civic Studies
abstract: As part of an ongoing project, our research team worked with three social studies teachers to refine the Teacher Lens for Digital Relevance (TLDR) model for evaluating educational video games (EVGs). We found that the model was useful to teachers for focusing their attention on important aspects of EVGs. Our findings suggest that the TLDR model is a promising tool for helping teachers but may benefit from further refinements to enhance its usability and adoption.

title: An Exploratory Study on Enhancing Student Learning Experiences in Knowledge Building Teacher Training Program
citation: Xian, L. S., Wang, L., & Seet, C. (2024). An Exploratory Study on Enhancing Student Learning Experiences in Knowledge Building Teacher Training Program. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Xian, L. S., Wang, L., & Seet, C.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
abstract: This study examined 55 students’ understanding on the knowledge building principles (community aspects) from the knowledge telling, knowledge sharing and knowledge creation dimensions. Results indicate that to provide sustainable knowledge building environment, program designer conduct survey before program started, it helps provide customized program to better fit students’ learning need in the different stages in this program.

title: Being Fair & Equitable: A Qualitative Study of Science Teachers’ Shifts in Priorities and Expectations During COVID-19
citation: Raj, A., Wittmann, M., & Kayumova, S. (2024). Being Fair & Equitable: A Qualitative Study of Science Teachers’ Shifts in Priorities and Expectations During COVID-19. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2283-2284). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Raj, A., Wittmann, M., & Kayumova, S.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This study examines how secondary science teachers described the shift in their priorities and expectations to be more equitable towards their affected students during the initial COVID-19 lockdown. Ten teachers were recruited via a purposeful convenient sampling from diverse socioeconomic status (SES) schools and interviewed through Zoom. Findings indicate SES-based differences in teachers’ perception of the impact of COVID-19 on students, and their approach to fairness and equity through subsequent shifts in priorities and expectations.

title: The Development of Indigenous Allyship Among White Settlers
citation: Bell, P. (2024). The Development of Indigenous Allyship Among White Settlers. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2285-2286). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Bell, P.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: The promotion of Indigenous sovereignty is approached as a coalitional justice project involving decolonial and anti-colonial efforts. This necessitates that non-Indigenous people engage in developmental processes focused on recognizing and unlearning coloniality, disrupting white colonial structures, and taking direction from Indigenous Peoples through trusting relationships. I present a social practice framework to guide development of Indigenous allyship among white settlers based on case studies and interviews from Living in Indigenous Sovereignty (Carlson-Manathara & Rowe, 2021).

title: Integrating Introductory Structural Engineering Courses in Architecture Program
citation: Khodadadi, A. (2024). Integrating Introductory Structural Engineering Courses in Architecture Program. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2287-2288). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Khodadadi, A.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; STEM - Engineering & Robotics
tpack_ck_labels: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; STEM - Engineering & Robotics
abstract: This study investigated the cognitive learning challenges and concerns of architecture program students taking introductory courses in Structural Engineering. The outcome will contribute to our knowledge of the suitable pedagogical approach and instructional strategies to develop engineering analysis and design skills among architecture students.

title: Investigating Linguistic Landscapes to Empower Multicultural Community Building in the University and Beyond
citation: Li, Z. & Thompson, N. (2024). Investigating Linguistic Landscapes to Empower Multicultural Community Building in the University and Beyond. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E.
