International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Li, Z. & Thompson, N.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Students often interpret their communities as the school context, however, exploring the wider range of their communities, especially in the context of seeking culturally diverse and multicultural environments is crucial. Here we investigate the Linguistic Landscape (LL) of Buffalo NY, which is home to many universities. The goal is to foster critical thinking and multicultural competence, to empower linguistically diverse students to recognize their language and cultural heritage, and to promote equity for all students.

title: Visualizing Data about Student Well-Being
citation: Wisittanawat, P. & Peterson, R. A. (2024). Visualizing Data about Student Well-Being. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2291-2292). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Wisittanawat, P. & Peterson, R. A.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Schools regularly collect and display student data, but they often only focus on data about achievement. Intended to motivate academic performance, these data practices can instigate negative emotions in students. This poster presents our ongoing work aimed at designing a component of a secondary teacher preparation course to engage pre-service teachers (PSTs) in considering how they can mitigate harmful accountability data practices in school by collecting and visualizing data that attend to student well-being.

title: Sustaining a Learning Community Approach to Foster Digital Age Competencies: A Study of Process, Outcomes, and Infrastructures
citation: Benjamin, A., Hod, Y., Kashi, S., Rahmian, L., & Tueg, S. (2024). Sustaining a Learning Community Approach to Foster Digital Age Competencies: A Study of Process, Outcomes, and Infrastructures. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2293-2294). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Benjamin, A., Hod, Y., Kashi, S., Rahmian, L., & Tueg, S.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: The digital age has drastically changed many aspects of human life, with significant implications on education. Transforming school structures so they can foster digital age competencies sustainably is a grand challenge for educational systems and research. Learning community pedagogies provide a potent way to approach this challenge. We present a large, multi-year study that is supported by the national department of education that attends to the learning processes, outcomes, and infrastructures necessary to do this.

title: A Framework to Integrate Computational Modeling Practices with Three-dimensional NGSS Learning
citation: Wagh, A., Wendel, D., Anderson, E., Schoenfeld, I., & Conlin, L. D. (2024). A Framework to Integrate Computational Modeling Practices with Three-dimensional NGSS Learning. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2295-2296). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Wagh, A., Wendel, D., Anderson, E., Schoenfeld, I., & Conlin, L. D.
subject: STEM - Engineering & Robotics
abstract: Computational modeling (CM) supports scientific and computational practices. Little work has examined how CM practices align with the scientific and engineering practices (SEPs) in the Next Generation Science Standards (NGSS). This poster presents a conceptual framework to align five CM practices with SEPs. This framework is being used to develop CM NGSS-aligned curriculum for high school science classrooms in a district. We provide one curricular unit example and discuss design tensions in doing this work.

title: Seeing is Believing? Students’ Evaluation of Visual Misinformation
citation: Cohen, S. G., Copti-Mshael, T., Barzilai, S., & Hadar, L. L. (2024). Seeing is Believing? Students’ Evaluation of Visual Misinformation. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2297-2298). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Cohen, S. G., Copti-Mshael, T., Barzilai, S., & Hadar, L. L.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: As misinformation spreads online, discernment of reliable information is a crucial skill to make informed decisions. This study explores middle-school students’ abilities to evaluate fabricated and manipulated visual representations, and which strategies they use to evaluate visual misinformation. Findings indicate that students partially identified visual misinformation and employed various strategies including visual evaluation, content evaluation, corroboration, and source evaluation.

title: Collaborative Sense-making: Strategies for Co-Researching in a Research-Practice Partnership
citation: Coenraad, M., Mills, K., Rangel, A., Burke, Q., & Dunbar, K. (2024). Collaborative Sense-making: Strategies for Co-Researching in a Research-Practice Partnership. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2299-2300). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Coenraad, M., Mills, K., Rangel, A., Burke, Q., & Dunbar, K.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
abstract: Within our RPP, we have made a commitment to practice-side partners being co-researchers and supporting data-centered development and implementation of computational thinking pathways. We present seven strategies our research-side team utilized to support collaborative sense-making throughout data collection and analysis. This work counters traditional paradigms of researcher and practitioner roles in research and provides concrete strategies for co-researching and collaborative sense-making to enable practice-side partners to take agency and ownership over data collection, analysis, and sense-making.

title: Challenging Inequality: A Proposal to Raise Conscientização about Financialization with Colombian Rural Communities
citation: Sandoval-Llanos, J. & Sharma, P. (2024). Challenging Inequality: A Proposal to Raise Conscientização about Financialization with Colombian Rural Communities. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2301-2302). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Sandoval-Llanos, J. & Sharma, P.
subject: Humanities, Language & Literacy
conceptualisations_list: Co-Design & Participatory Design; Racial Equity, Power & Social Justice
abstract: In this poster, we explore the relationship of Freire’s notion of critical consciousness with critical and sociocultural theories for learning. Specifically, we use conscientização as a construct to co-design an intervention to raise awareness about the impact of financialization on small farmers’ everyday lives. We draw upon qualitative data gathered with rural Colombian farmers to articulate strategies for engaging in co-design of financial literacy strategies for underserved and marginalized communities.

title: EMPOWER: Enacting Materials to Promote Ownership, Engagement, and Relevance
citation: Ko, M. M., Krist, C., Hug, B., Wingert, K., Suárez, E., Lauren, L. H., Leonardi, N., Hall, K., & Light, E. (2024). EMPOWER: Enacting Materials to Promote Ownership, Engagement, and Relevance. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2303-2304). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Ko, M. M., Krist, C., Hug, B., Wingert, K., Suárez, E., Lauren, L. H., Leonardi, N., Hall, K., & Light, E.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Fostering locally relevant and community-centered forms of science learning that develop students’ critical science agency problematizes a “one-size-fits-all” model of teacher learning; teachers must examine how community needs and resources, local inequities and justice issues, and curriculum materials can converge to design novel learning opportunities for science learners. This paper presents the core commitments of EMPOWER, a cross-institutional effort that aims to support teachers' sensemaking and adaptations of curriculum materials to promote student ownership, engagement, and relevance at multiple sites across the U.S.

title: Navigating Scale-Free Out-of-School Time (OST) Provider Networks Within Afterschool Ecosystems
citation: Liu, S. K., Pinkard, N., & Majors, Y. J. (2024). Navigating Scale-Free Out-of-School Time (OST) Provider Networks Within Afterschool Ecosystems. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2305-2306). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Liu, S. K., Pinkard, N., & Majors, Y. J.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
abstract: Centralized resources within afterschool program ecosystems risk overdependency on singular funders and overlooking local community providers. By combining opportunity landscaping data with social network analysis, we introduce new methods of understanding funding allocations and identifying vulnerabilities within after-school ecosystems.

title: Healing Justice Practice Professional Development Program for Black K-12 Educators
citation: Raysor, A. (2024). Healing Justice Practice Professional Development Program for Black K-12 Educators. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2307-2308). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Raysor, A.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
abstract: Buffalo-Niagara is one of the most racially segregated regions in the nation. The majority of students in Buffalo city schools are Black while the employees are predominantly white. Black communities in Buffalo live in constant fear exacerbated by a deteriorating quality of life and mass shooting. K-12 schools have the potential to become sites for healing regimens, self-care, and protection led by Black educators trained in Healing Justice practice-based curriculum.

title: Investigating the Influence of AI-Augmented Summarization on Concept Learning, Summarization Skills, Argumentative Essay Writing, and Course Outcomes in Online Adult Education
citation: Kim, J., Bae, Y., Stravelakis, J., & Kim, M. K. (2024). Investigating the Influence of AI-Augmented Summarization on Concept Learning, Summarization Skills, Argumentative Essay Writing, and Course Outcomes in Online Adult Education. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2309-2310). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Kim, J., Bae, Y., Stravelakis, J., & Kim, M. K.
subject: Humanities, Language & Literacy
abstract: This study aims to explore the influence of concept learning facilitated by an AI-augmented summarization feedback tool, the Student Mental Model Analyzer for Research and Teaching (SMART), on various learning outcomes within an undergraduate English course using linear mixed-effects (LME) modeling and Bayesian correlations with data from 22 participants. Significant improvements in learners’ mental models and associations of concept learning with subsequent learning activities suggest the potential of such tools in improving learning performance.

title: Justice and Creativity: Leveraging Creative Learning Principles for Youth-Led Social Change
citation: Trapp, J. (2024). Justice and Creativity: Leveraging Creative Learning Principles for Youth-Led Social Change. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2311-2312). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Trapp, J.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Young people who come from marginalized identities and are given access to creative learning spaces and tools are positioned to address social change and implement tangible solutions. This paper describes how youth in The Clubhouse Network are using creative computing tools to develop social justice awareness campaigns and considers how they have the potential to spark change within their communities.

title: Estimating Action-Specific Expertise in AR-Guided Learning and Training by Modeling Visual Attention
citation: Yoo, D. W., Tarashiyoun, H., & Moghaddam, M. (2024). Estimating Action-Specific Expertise in AR-Guided Learning and Training by Modeling Visual Attention. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2313-2314). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Yoo, D. W., Tarashiyoun, H., & Moghaddam, M.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This paper explores a new method for estimating expertise in Augmented Reality (AR) learning and training, emphasizing the learner’s familiarity with action-relevant Areas of Interest (AoI) and their decision-making processes. By examining both gaze behavior and object tracking based on egocentric video data from a group of 15 participants, we investigate the interaction dynamics of learners within AR environments to distinguish between expert and novice behaviors. Key findings highlight notable variations in visual attention and engagement strategies, reflecting different degrees of task familiarity and decision-making capabilities among participants with varying self-reported expertise levels. This approach advances the understanding of visual attention behavior and its relation with expertise in the context of AR learning, offering new insights for the design of adaptive, learner-centered AR education systems. The study contributes to the field of learning sciences by enhancing the effectiveness and personalization of AR learning and training models.

title: Lessons Learned from Co-Designing Phenomena Driven Student Centered AI Curriculum with Teachers New to AI
citation: Chakarov, A. G., Bush, J. B., & Biddy, Q. (2024). Lessons Learned from Co-Designing Phenomena Driven Student Centered AI Curriculum with Teachers New to AI. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2315-2316). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Chakarov, A. G., Bush, J. B., & Biddy, Q.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This poster describes the collaborative design process between researchers and teachers to create student centered phenomena driven middle school artificial intelligence content. The co-design process is based on the CT-Integration Cycle which has been successfully used to co-design CT-integrated science units. The initial findings highlight the successes and challenges in our current design process and outline how others can uptake components of the PL model to co-design their own AI-integrated units.

title: The Iterative Science and Engineering Instructional Model
citation:
Songer, N. B., Calabrese, J., Cordner, H., & Aina, D. (2024). The Iterative Science and Engineering Instructional Model 
. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2317-2318). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Songer, N. B., Calabrese, J., Cordner, H., & Aina, D.
subject: STEM - Mathematics; STEM - Engineering & Robotics
abstract: Science is a multidimensional endeavor that requires deep engagement with phenomena. Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) discoveries often advance through a fluid and messy process that includes iterations of science investigation, engineering design, and interdisciplinary collaboration. In contrast, most pre-college STEM instructional programs do not foster experiences that promote deep engagement with phenomena through iterations of science investigation, engineering design and collective feedback and sharing with others, including key stakeholders. This poster presents the Iterative Science and Engineering (ISE) instructional model and student learning outcomes when an ISE-aligned instructional unit was implemented in secondary classrooms over three consecutive years. Outcomes include curricula adapted to the model, adaptation guidelines, assessment instruments, and research results that advance theory and practice for fostering fluid, iterative cycles of science and engineering grounded in local phenomena.

citation: Akdemir, Z. G. & Menekse, M. (2024). Designing Quantum-Infused NGSS-Aligned Science Curriculum to Support Learning and Engagement of Middle School Students. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. abstract: Introducing quantum concepts at the K-12 level is an innovative practice that offers varied educational opportunities across different subjects. However, there are persistent challenges, particularly in teaching basic quantum concepts in middle school, with concerns raised by teachers about training, materials, and time constraints. Despite these obstacles, recognizing the significance of engaging students in cultivating science and engineering practices, this study introduced a middle school science curriculum infused with quantum concepts aligned with Next Generation Science Standards (NGSS). Assessing its impact on the science learning outcomes and multidimensional engagement of 873 students revealed significant gains in learning fundamental quantum concepts as well as engagement in different dimensions. This study emphasizes the potential of integrating quantum concepts into middle school science education within the learning sciences framework, offering valuable insights for researchers and educators interested in incorporating emerging quantum technologies and their societal applications.

abstract: As Machine Learning (ML), a branch of Artificial Intelligence (AI), proliferates across society, youth need to learn basic fundamentals of this new technology. Furthermore, the field of AI reflects the persistent lack of diversity seen in broader STEM fields, which may impact historically underrepresented groups pursuing these fields. In response, we created an ML-embedded, out-of-school-time program for high school age students focused on scientific inquiry, constructed through a justice-lens. This paper reports findings from a repeated measures study of 35 youth (82% from underrepresented groups in STEM) introduced to ML concepts through a 4-week Institute followed by an academic-year-long research internship with a mentor-scientist. Student learning outcomes were measured using a new ML concept inventory. Findings suggest ML knowledge increased after the Institute and persisted 9 months afterwards for those participating in mentored research.

abstract: Native American youth receive exclusionary discipline more frequently and severely for more subjective reasons such as disrespect in the United States. Racialization of discipline is a contextually situated problem whose patterns and predictors change from one social, historical, and spatial context to another. Addressing inequity requires a historicized and situated understanding of important relevant issues to help develop localized solutions in response to school communities’ diverse and often conflicting histories, needs, and goals. In this study, we investigated how Indigenous Learning Lab, a community-based problem-solving intervention, facilitated collaborative transformation effort at a rural high school to design a culturally responsive behavioral support system in partnership with the Anishinaabe nation, school staff, and researchers from a local university.

abstract: We invite learning scientists to consider how we might include older people in our studies and designs. Our field is poised to study learning across the lifespan but has yet to take up the experiences of older people. We draw on our experiences with older people as starting points for connection, appreciation, and inquiry. Our stories highlight the material, relational, and ideational resources that shape older people’s lives and their learning, underscoring the value of viewing older people’s experiences ecologically, complexly, and dynamically.

We describe our design of a storyline framework aimed at supporting minoritized youth engagement in critical technology education. We present preliminary data to highlight the contextual complexities, researchers' role in design, and challenges in adapting established design research frameworks. We close with three considerations focused on students anticipated interests, embracing nonlinearity, and being responsive to context needs.

To support and expand these efforts, team members will conduct a needs assessment and task analysis to develop a field guide for library professionals seeking to design radio programming in partnership with their local communities.

abstract: In this paper, we present a case study of designing AI-human partnerships in a real-world context of science classrooms. We designed a classroom environment where AI technologies, teachers and peers worked synergistically to support students’ writing in science. In addition to an NLP algorithm to automatically assess students’ essays, we also designed (i) feedback that was easier for students to understand; (ii) participatory structures in the classroom focusing on reflection, peer review and discussion, and (iii) scaffolding by teachers to help students understand the feedback. Our results showed that students improved their written explanations, after receiving feedback and engaging in reflection activities. Our case study illustrates that Augmented Intelligence (USDoE, 2023), in which the strengths of AI complement the strengths of teachers and peers, while also overcoming the limitations of each, can provide multiple forms of support to foster learning and teaching.

The results lead to a discussion on the value of teacher scaffolding in facilitating the implementation of Knowledge Building in the classroom.

The pedagogical practices in this study, including scaffolding, front loading, and the use of a teddy bear as an inanimate instructional aide will be compared to, and contrasted with, prior studies of facilitation in formal and informal makerspaces.

abstract: Collaborative learning is known to be effective, but not all students engage and benefit from it. Here, we applied video coding in conjunction with electroencephalography (EEG) recordings to examine how students engage in collaborative learning. Our findings indicate that students frequently alternated between on-task, off-task, and idle states. The duration of continuous on-task engagement was associated with better learning. Finally, students’ EEG brain activity during idle moments resembled off-task brain activity.

abstract: This study examines elementary, middle, and high school students’ understanding of engineers and engineering practices. I probed students’ views through drawings and interviews. Through analysis of these data, I intend to gain insight on how students conceptualize who engineers are, what they do, and how they do it. I aim to identify deficits in engineering knowledge as opportunities for tailored instruction in future curricula.

abstract: We exposed Brazilian teachers to a professional development (PD) program incorporating action research into teacher education and documented it in this study, evaluating how the program influenced educators' pedagogy in the school setting. We engaged teachers in a mentorship activity fostering reflection on classroom practice, engagement with theory, and academic dissemination. Results highlight growth in teachers' conscious awareness over classroom practices and the role of connecting theory and practical applications in education with action research.

Providing post-secondary students with opportunities to conduct culturally relevant, place-based science research has the potential to engage and retain students in STEM pathways. This study explores the impact of science research experiences using CO2 meters. Initial findings show that students’ confidence in their ability to do research increased as well as their perception of if others thought they were ‘good at STEM.’

abstract: This study of 24,390 Duolingo reviews employed text mining to analyze users' motivational and cognitive expressions, classifying feedback by thumbs-up count for agreement levels. The findings underscore a substantial difference in feedback among agreement groups, particularly in users’ cognitive expression. Reviews garnering more thumbs up proved more relevant for learning, emphasizing their importance in tailoring platforms for educational needs.

abstract: The main goal of this poster is to explore the idea of “Organizational Learning” in the context of structured learning environments. The ability to meet a requirement or standard over the duration of a professional workshop goes hand-in-hand with the structural systems put in place to keep track of the progress that is made. By having a clearly communicated system that can be developed as the needs of the instructor/classroom becomes apparent, the efficacy and success of instructors may be highlighted more thoroughly.

Using epistemic network analysis, we identified differences in students’ verbalized SRL processes between groups who differed in their level of adherence. Future work will be broadened to explore the relationship between student adherence and learning outcomes.

This study uses post-course reflections from a non-traditional math course that incorporates programming and art, to investigate what features students appreciated. The course improved student attitudes towards math. The aspects of math classes that students find supportive may lead to increased resilience in learning mathematics.

abstract: As interest in teacher learning towards transformative education has increased, so too has the need for learning environments that conceptualize learning as imagining possibilities for future social action. In this study, I explore how fiction writing can orient teacher learners towards the projective—or future-focused—dimension of their agency. One teacher’s discourse illustrates how narrative mediates learning through the release from systemic constraints and expands pathways for future action.

subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: The study explored the testing effect’s impact on subsequent test performance. It examined this effect's variability among 310 elementary students based on knowledge complexity, using tasks with differing interactivity levels. Tasks with low interactivity yielded superior performance in both immediate and delayed tests. Additionally, example-problem tasks outperformed example-example tasks in delayed tests. The study concluded that the interplay between interactivity and the testing effect remains uncertain, advocating for managing cognitive load within working memory boundaries.

abstract: Epistemological beliefs, defined as cognition about knowledge, is important for science education. Despite this importance, few studies explored epistemological beliefs about science among undergraduate students in the context of biology and none examine potential differences between subdisciplines of biology. This paper investigates how epistemological beliefs about science could differ between two biology subdomains, ecology, and molecular biology, among first year life science students. Initial findings indicate that different sub-domains of biology may influence epistemological beliefs.

title: Social Media as a Space for Youth’s Algorithmic Resistance
citation: Hurtado, S. & Keune, A. (2024). Social Media as a Space for Youth’s Algorithmic Resistance. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2371-2372). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Hurtado, S. & Keune, A.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Youth spend a significant portion of their time on social media with a wide range of activities. Social media can present risks for youth, and the impact of these is still being discussed in current research. Building on a connected learning framework, this poster qualitatively analyzed youths’ social media walkthroughs for practices that showcase algorithmic resistance. The study found that youth navigate social media skillfully, develop awareness about risks, and build strategies to circumvent them.

title: Learning Engineering for the Professional Science Communicator
citation: Peffer, M. E. (2024). Learning Engineering for the Professional Science Communicator. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2373-2374). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Peffer, M. E.
subject: STEM - Engineering & Robotics
abstract: Professional science communicators face a daunting task: communicating science information in an effective manner to a society increasingly polarized over scientific issues and awash in misinformation. Many professional science communicators exist outside the academy and have minimal access to the resources and knowledge needed to develop evidence-based science communication activities. Learning engineering, defined here as the practical use of learning sciences knowledge to design outreach activities, may be a solution. Here I describe a pilot workshop on learning engineering and science communication delivered to professional science communicators. Overall, the idea of engineering science communication activities was well received by this population. Participants left the workshop desirous of more knowledge of the evidence on human learning generated by the field of the learning sciences. Additional work in this space is justified and new opportunities for a bidirectional relationship between learning scientists and professional science communications will benefit both fields.

title: Solo vs. Collaborative Programming? Cognitive and Affective Outcomes, Problem Design and Solving Patterns in a Game-Based Learning Environment
citation: Na, H., Fulwider, G. C., Caskurlu, S., & Jun, B. (2024). Solo vs. Collaborative Programming? Cognitive and Affective Outcomes, Problem Design and Solving Patterns in a Game-Based Learning Environment. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2375-2376). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Na, H., Fulwider, G. C., Caskurlu, S., & Jun, B.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
abstract: This study explores how individual and collaborative game-based learning environments for computer science (CS) affect learning outcomes and patterns in problem-design and problem-solving. A significant difference between individual and collaborative programming was found in computational thinking skills, but not in attitudes toward CS. Log data analysis further revealed similar but distinct patterns in problem-design and problem-solving between groups. We discuss the implications of these findings and suggest directions for future research.

title: Prison Industrial Complex Abolition Pedagogies: A Conceptual Framework for Uprooting Carceral Logics in Teacher Education
citation: Hewko, C. (2024). Prison Industrial Complex Abolition Pedagogies: A Conceptual Framework for Uprooting Carceral Logics in Teacher Education. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2377-2378). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Hewko, C.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: PIC abolition pedagogies is a flexible framework—conceptualizing PIC abolition as a pedagogy and tool for understanding learning—that is rooted in PIC abolition and pedagogies of joint activity. The possibilities of prison industrial complex (PIC) abolition pedagogies are explored through a community-engaged approach to teacher education, in which ethnic studies teachers and community members participated in monthly workshops to develop PIC abolition pedagogies. Implications for teacher (un)learning are also examined through this analysis.

title: Professional Learning Integrating Computer Science and Storytelling through Culturally Responsive Computing
citation: Dyer, E. B., Parker, B., & Ibrahim, N. (2024). Professional Learning Integrating Computer Science and Storytelling through Culturally Responsive Computing. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2379-2380). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Dyer, E. B., Parker, B., & Ibrahim, N.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
abstract: This study presents a critical case study of a redesign of a professional development activity for elementary teachers to understand design decisions that lead to opportunities to integrate computer science and computational thinking aspects with social/societal dimensions in learning. We conducted qualitative analysis of culturally responsive-sustaining aspects of the original and redesigned activities, along with reflections and debriefs about the activity. Findings from the case study highlight potential affordances and limitations of taking an adaptation approach towards computer science professional development design in order to better reflect critical and/or culturally responsive computing in elementary grades.

title: Positionality Shifts through Theatre Arts Practices
citation: Cawelti, L., Chew, P., Peppler, K., Adesida, T., & Cuéllar, N. (2024). Positionality Shifts through Theatre Arts Practices. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2381-2382). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Cawelti, L., Chew, P., Peppler, K., Adesida, T., & Cuéllar, N.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Understanding educator positionality is important to socially just learning. Teachers can apply arts practices when reflecting on their own backgrounds, experiences, and potential biases toward understanding their own positionality. From two semi-structured interviews, we explore how practices inherent in theatre arts can facilitate positionality shifts in arts learning environments. Implications for leveraging the arts toward disrupting inequities.

title: Using Technology-Mediated Lesson Study with Rural Teachers to Improve Three-Dimensional Science Instruction
citation: Hudson, M., Sansom, R., Leary, H., Stowers, J., Smith, C., Poulsen, T., Longhurst, M., & Moore, A. (2024). Using Technology-Mediated Lesson Study with Rural Teachers to Improve Three-Dimensional Science Instruction. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2383-2384). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Hudson, M., Sansom, R., Leary, H., Stowers, J., Smith, C., Poulsen, T., Longhurst, M., & Moore, A.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Rural teachers have fewer collaborative and professional learning opportunities. Technology-Mediated Lesson Study bridges the isolation of rural teachers by connecting them to colleagues. This research aimed to build teachers’ capacity to understand and implement three-dimensional (3D) science principles. After one year, interviews reported rural teachers’ growth with 3D science knowledge and implementation and increased value for 3D science.

title: The Effects of Technology-enhanced Embodied Learning Intervention for Mathematics in K-12 Classrooms
citation: Na, H. & Sung, H. (2024). The Effects of Technology-enhanced Embodied Learning Intervention for Mathematics in K-12 Classrooms. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2385-2386). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Na, H. & Sung, H.
subject: STEM - Mathematics
abstract: This research explores the effects of a mobile device-based embodied learning intervention that leverages computer vision techniques, on fourth graders' understanding, attitudes, and engagement in geometry learning. We found significant improvements in students’ understanding between pre- and post-tests, whereas their attitudes remained unchanged. A multiple regression on log data showed that time spent on making-angle activities predicts students’ cognitive learning gain. These findings highlight the potential of applying mobile device-based embodied learning in classroom settings.

title: More-than-human Empathizing for Science Identity, Ethical Accountability and Solidarity
citation: Papendieck, A., Azevedo, F., & Lee, H. H. (2024). More-than-human Empathizing for Science Identity, Ethical Accountability and Solidarity. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2387-2388). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Papendieck, A., Azevedo, F., & Lee, H. H.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Here, we examine empathizing as a sociocultural process that promotes science identity development. In particular, we attend to how students learn about themselves and their science by empathizing with nonhuman others. We find that empathizing often looks very difficult, uncomfortable and risky, and that it is likely an essential process in learning environments that promotes dignity-affirming scientific solidarities.

title: Syndrome versus Phenomenon: A Conceptualization of Imposter Phenomenon
citation: Lamothe, M. & Keifert, D. T. (2024). Syndrome versus Phenomenon: A Conceptualization of Imposter Phenomenon. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2389-2390). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Lamothe, M. & Keifert, D. T.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This paper explores Black female graduate students’ experiences with identity development as scholars through secondary analysis of ethnographic data. Drawing on Cultural Historical Activity Theory (CHAT) and Critical Race Theory (CRT), I explore how cultural influences shaped internalized ideas of imposter phenomenon. Findings show reasons for manifestations of feelings of imposition. We hope that conceptualizing the phenomenon more clearly will decrease feelings of imposter phenomenon in Black female graduate students.

title: Examining Asian American Student Experiences with Racism in STEM
citation: Trinh, A., Forsythe, D., Tsai, J., Lee, L., Hsu, J., Sung, R., & Lo, S. M. (2024). Examining Asian American Student Experiences with Racism in STEM. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2391-2392). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Trinh, A., Forsythe, D., Tsai, J., Lee, L., Hsu, J., Sung, R., & Lo, S. M.
subject: STEM - Mathematics; STEM - Engineering & Robotics
abstract: Asian American students studying STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) in higher education in the United States are not as well studied in comparison to other minoritized groups. Our research examines how these students navigate through their STEM and university environments and how racism may impact that navigation. Preliminary results show differences in experiences when comparing first-generation Asian American students and adopted Asian American students to other Asian American students.

title: Connecting the Dots: Expanding on What is Scaffolded in Inquiry-Based Lab Approaches for College-level Physics
citation: Charles, E. S., Adams, R., Lenton, K., Dugdale, M., & Zhang, C. (2024). Connecting the Dots: Expanding on What is Scaffolded in Inquiry-Based Lab Approaches for College-level Physics. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2393-2394). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Charles, E. S., Adams, R., Lenton, K., Dugdale, M., & Zhang, C.
subject: STEM - Natural Science
abstract: Scaffolding is essential for inquiry approaches, yet little is known about how it is designed into inquiry based labs (IBL) in science courses. Using a conjecture mapping framework, we describe the design progression of scaffolds in a two-year design-based research IBL physics curriculum. This highlights how and why changes were made to the intervention, and reveals what it took to align the design to the learning processes to ultimately improve learning outcomes.

title: Using Biterm Topic Modeling to Explore Gender Differences in Secondary Students’ Wonderings about AI Concepts
citation: Mushi, D., Chao, J., Jiang, S., Ellis, R., Rosé, C. P., & Wiedemann, K. (2024). Using Biterm Topic Modeling to Explore Gender Differences in Secondary Students’ Wonderings about AI Concepts. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2395-2396). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Mushi, D., Chao, J., Jiang, S., Ellis, R., Rosé, C. P., & Wiedemann, K.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: The study reveals gender-based differences in how secondary students express curiosity in an AI curriculum. The study used biterm topic modeling to explore questions posed by male and female learners (n=239) in Grades 8-12. The findings revealed that keywords related to model accuracy and prediction such as Words and Weights were prevalent in both groups. Key variations were observed in technical terms, such as Machines. The discussions highlight the need for socially relevant AI curriculums.

title: “Trust me, this is gonna be something”: Agency Through Un/Learning with Materials in Arts Integration
citation: Preston, E. A. & Knecht, J. (2024). “Trust me, this is gonna be something”: Agency Through Un/Learning with Materials in Arts Integration. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2397-2398). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Preston, E. A. & Knecht, J.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Offering choice is not enough to support student agency, because we co-create with materials (Hood & Kraehe, 2017). This qualitative study used a materialist lens to understand how teaching artists supported agency through material engagement within arts integration. We found teaching artists expanded student agency by 1) facilitating material exploration as a pathway to un/learn material relationships toward perceptual expansion, and 2) using varied practices for reorganizing and troubling time to reshape activity and material relationships.

title: Connecting Agency: Linking Funds of Knowledge
citation: Lopez-Parra, R. D., Kussainova, G., Konara, K., Wilson-Fetrow, M., & Svihla, V. (2024). Connecting Agency: Linking Funds of Knowledge, Engineering Practices, and Foundational Coursework. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2399-2400). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Lopez-Parra, R. D., Kussainova, G., Konara, K., Wilson-Fetrow, M., & Svihla, V.
subject: STEM - Natural Science; STEM - Mathematics; STEM - Engineering & Robotics
tpack_ck_labels: STEM - Natural Science; STEM - Mathematics; STEM - Engineering & Robotics
abstract: We used mixed-methods to investigate how an engineering course supported students to become responsible for building connections between foundational mathematics/physics, engineering practices and knowledge, and cultural/everyday experiences. Qualitative analysis of student talk sheds light on the nature of connecting agency and its development. Analysis of survey data show significant increases in students’ connecting agency.

title: Exploring Narratives about People and the Environment in the Context of Resilience Education
citation: Tayne, K., Stevenson, K., McCollum, A., DeMattia, E., & Jeffs, P. (2024). Exploring Narratives about People and the Environment in the Context of Resilience Education. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2401-2402). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Tayne, K., Stevenson, K., McCollum, A., DeMattia, E., & Jeffs, P.
subject: Humanities, Language & Literacy
abstract: This paper offers a conceptual contribution for the study of environmental learning, considering which stories about people and the environment might be told through a lens of resilience. Grounded in our research project and broader literature, we introduce narrative themes that may emerge from an interdisciplinary resilience framework: collaborative communities and agentic hope for people and the environment. We also propose narrative tensions for justice and global socio-environmental challenges that should be considered.

title: Problematic Problems: Navigating the Design Process Amidst Challenges
citation: Lemee, M. & Blikstein, P. (2024). Problematic Problems: Navigating the Design Process Amidst Challenges. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2403-2404). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Lemee, M. & Blikstein, P.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: In education, design frameworks are often used to cultivate creativity, innovation, and problem-solving skills but often overlook the complexities of design problems. As students identify personally relevant problems, their perspectives are shaped by their experiences with the challenges of the complex world. There is a need for learning activities that connect design methods and students’, empowering them to tackle challenges creatively and confidently.

title: Art as a Cornerstone for Learning and Community Engagement: A Case Study on Supporting Children’s Affect-driven Identities as Change Makers
citation: Lee, C., Lozano, O., Lee, S., & Jen, T. (2024). Art as a Cornerstone for Learning and Community Engagement: A Case Study on Supporting Children’s Affect-driven Identities as Change Makers. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2405-2406). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Lee, C., Lozano, O., Lee, S., & Jen, T.
subject: Humanities, Language & Literacy; Social & Civic Studies
tpack_ck_labels: Humanities, Language & Literacy; Social & Civic Studies
abstract: This poster investigates how the arts can support children’s identities as learners and valuable community members who engage in environmental issues. We build on literature that positions art as a political medium, and places affect at the forefront of learning, identity, and engaging with communities. Findings come from an art installation children (6-8 years) created as a PSA for the school community on the importance of pollinators in our ecosystem. We use artifact analysis to examine wire sculptures, signs, and videography to illustrate how art supported children’s identities as change makers who cared for the environment.

title: Responsive Teaching in the Context of Theory-Building Activities
citation: Swanson, H. & Lawrence, L. (2024). Responsive Teaching in the Context of Theory-Building Activities. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2407-2408). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Swanson, H. & Lawrence, L.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Theory-building activities are a powerful context for eliciting and building on student ideas. We present an approach to structuring responsive teaching in the context of theory-building activities, which is designed to help students articulate, evaluate, and refine their ideas through generating, testing, and revising theoretical knowledge artifacts, such as models and explanations. Our approach focuses on the design of theory-building activities and teacher moves to support student knowledge construction, in alignment with constructivist ideals.

title: Examining Teacher Supports for Visibility, Believability, and Meaningfulness in Place-Based Citizen Science
citation: Meza-Torres, C., Jordan, M., Zuiker, S., Jongewaard, R., Adeloju, E., & Spreitzer, K. (2024). Examining Teacher Supports for Visibility, Believability, and Meaningfulness in Place-Based Citizen Science. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2409-2410). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Meza-Torres, C., Jordan, M., Zuiker, S., Jongewaard, R., Adeloju, E., & Spreitzer, K.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: A limiting factor in school-based citizen science is teachers’ capacity to facilitate active student engagement in place-based inquiry practices. We extend Harris and colleagues’ student data interaction constructs of visibility, believability and meaningfulness using a design-based research approach to qualitatively examine professional development structures designed to enable teachers to foster students’ contributions as visible, believable, and meaningful.

title: “We Appreciate That Reviewers Pointed Out This”: Exploring Knowledge Co-construction in the Process of Peer Review
citation: Shi, H. & Wei, S. (2024). “We Appreciate That Reviewers Pointed Out This”: Exploring Knowledge Co-construction in the Process of Peer Review. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2411-2412). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Shi, H. & Wei, S.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Knowledge co-construction within the academic peer review process is an area yet unexplored empirically. This study analyzed peer review reports. Preliminary findings reveal that Negotiating Meaning is the most frequent phase, contrary to previous assertions of dominance by lower complexity thinking phases in knowledge co-construction. This analysis of expert dialogues offers insights that could enhance student peer review processes.

title: Leveraging Student Choice and Interest to Design an Engaging Lesson about Artificial Intelligence
citation: Ellis, R., Chao, J., Jiang, S., Rosé, C. P., & Wiedemann, K. (2024). Leveraging Student Choice and Interest to Design an Engaging Lesson about Artificial Intelligence. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2413-2414). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Ellis, R., Chao, J., Jiang, S., Rosé, C. P., & Wiedemann, K.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: As advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) continue, we can expect that students will live and work with AI. It is important that students know how this technology works and its impact on their futures. This paper looks at a lesson that was designed to foster secondary students’ interest in AI technologies, and to help students consider how AI can be used to improve jobs and solve problems. This lesson was designed using the principles of self-determination theory (Reis et al., 2000) to support student engagement and interest.

title: Centering Relationality When Investigating the Utility of Mathematics with Early Adolescents
citation: Dobie, T. E. & Ondricek, B. (2024). Centering Relationality When Investigating the Utility of Mathematics with Early Adolescents. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2415-2416). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Dobie, T. E. & Ondricek, B.
subject: STEM - Mathematics
abstract: While there are benefits of perceiving mathematics as useful, most perspectives on mathematical utility center on usefulness for individual advancement or for the economy and global competitiveness. Given the emphasis in many communities on interdependence and the importance of prosocial goals and social responsibility in early adolescence, we argue for integrating the notion of relationality—between both humans and the more-than-human world—into conceptions of utility in mathematics.

title: Exploring Preservice Teachers’ Perceptions and Experiences of Teaching Artificial Intelligence Students in Virtual Simulations
citation: Zhang, N., Ke, F., Dai, C., Southerland, S. A., Barrett, A., Bhowmik, S., West, L., & Yuan, X. (2024). Exploring Preservice Teachers’ Perceptions and Experiences of Teaching Artificial Intelligence Students in Virtual Simulations. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2417-2418). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Zhang, N., Ke, F., Dai, C., Southerland, S. A., Barrett, A., Bhowmik, S., West, L., & Yuan, X.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This case study explored preservice teachers’ (PSTs) perceptions and experiences of teaching AI students in virtual simulations. Eighteen PSTs participated in a 2-hour AI-based teacher training individually. Data were collected from participatory observations, in-simulation student-teacher dialogue transcripts, field notes, and semi-structured interviews. The findings revealed that PSTs exhibited positive perceptions toward AI-based simulation, which both engaged and challenged them in active problem solving. The simulation also prompted authentic rehearsals and in-situ reflection.

title: On STEM Teachers’ Surprise
citation: Azevedo, F. S., Sherard, M., Novelli, M., & Freed, N. (2024). On STEM Teachers’ Surprise. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2419-2420). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Azevedo, F. S., Sherard, M., Novelli, M., & Freed, N.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: A common learning activity in STEM teacher education courses consists of teachers observing K-12 classroom practice (video recorded or in situ) and reflecting on various kinds of observed events. We contribute to these research efforts by theorizing a class of classroom events that have thus far received little or no attention—namely, teachers’ surprise—and considering its implication for teacher education and professional development.

title: Connecting Chemistry Understanding: An Integrated Framework for Concretizing Abstract Visual Representations
citation:
Beier, J. P., Swart, M. I., Pazicni, S., & Nathan, M. J. (2024). Connecting Chemistry Understanding: An Integrated Framework for Concretizing Abstract Visual Representations 
. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 242-249). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Beier, J. P., Swart, M. I., Pazicni, S., & Nathan, M. J.
subject: STEM - Natural Science
abstract: Visual representations play an important role in students’ understanding of abstract concepts in technical fields like chemistry. However, it can be difficult for students to understand how these representations relate to one another, to underlying scientific concepts, or to the physical world they represent. Education research has explored this issue extensively, proposing approaches such as concreteness fading intended to progressively ground abstractions to concrete experiences; however, these may be theoretically inadequate for domains like chemistry that depend on maintaining (not fading) flexible ties among a triad of three key dimensions: abstract formalisms, scientific concepts, and the physical world. In this conceptual paper, we present a novel, integrative framework that draws inspiration from fine-grained constructivist, multimedia, grounded, and embodied learning theories with the explicit goal of concretizing students’ triadic understanding of chemistry concepts.

title: Bridging Equity and Play: Conceptual Insights into Learning and Assessment
citation: Kim, Y. & Saplan, K. (2024). Bridging Equity and Play: Conceptual Insights into Learning and Assessment. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2421-2422). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Kim, Y. & Saplan, K.
subject: Humanities, Language & Literacy
abstract: Playfulness is increasingly valued as a crucial design component in the Learning Sciences community. Its emphasis on learners' freedom, agency, and meaningful choices implies that playful design holds promise for promoting equitable learning opportunities. However, the precise mechanisms through which a playful approach can enhance equity in learning and assessment require further investigation. We explore theoretical connections between play and equity, focusing on how the Four Freedoms of Play intersect with contemporary understandings of equitable learning environments within the Learning Sciences and the broader literature on Play.

title: Gamified Self-regulation Assessments in Early Childhood Education: Aiming for Equity and Feasibility
citation: Didrichsen, S., Starke, K., Kwan, T., McClelland, M. M., Noel, T. K., & Cameron, C. E. (2024). Gamified Self-regulation Assessments in Early Childhood Education: Aiming for Equity and Feasibility. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. authors_list: Didrichsen, S., Starke, K., Kwan, T., McClelland, M. M., Noel, T. K., & Cameron, C. E.

abstract: Self-regulation skill development in early childhood lays the foundation for academic success by enabling children to take advantage of learning opportunities. Early childhood educators must be prepared to target self-regulation skills using developmentally appropriate assessments, which limit the potential for bias which is common in observational approaches. This study reports on n=14 teachers’ perceptions and experiences with a new teacher-facilitated, largely child-led tablet-based assessment of self-regulation called HTKS-Kids. Findings have implications for increasing equitable assessment opportunities for students with disabilities and English language learners.

title: Adolescent Identity as a Complex Adaptive System: Implications for Informal Pre-college STEM Education
citation: Hamilton, E., Espino, D., Lee, S., & Lux, K. (2024). Adolescent Identity as a Complex Adaptive System: Implications for Informal Pre-college STEM Education. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2425-2426). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Hamilton, E., Espino, D., Lee, S., & Lux, K.
subject: STEM - Mathematics; STEM - Engineering & Robotics
abstract: This theoretical poster conceptualizes adolescent identity formation as a system of representational systems, using the terminology of semiotics to distinguish between signifiers (identity-relevant cues and how they are interpreted) and their referents. This approach facilitates the use of complex adaptive systems to model the dynamic and reciprocal interactions that constantly shape overall identity formation and that are shaped by overall identity. Theoretical frameworks of self-determination theory, social cognitive career theory, and interest-driven creator theory furnish considerations for informal science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) intervention designs while addressing what drives the dynamics of the complex identity formation systems. The poster further suggests that finding congruence between the semiotic and the referent is a motivational force fueling identity formation. While conceptual in nature, the poster treats identity formation as operationally relevant to the design of informal STEM interventions and furnishes interview excerpts from two such interventions to illustrate selected constructs.

title: Exhibiting Escape: Demonstrating Knowing through (Mis)Reading the Body in Play
citation: Wargo, J. (2024). Exhibiting Escape: Demonstrating Knowing through (Mis)Reading the Body in Play. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 18th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2024 (pp. 2427-2428). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Wargo, J.
subject: Humanities, Language & Literacy
abstract: Games are not only forms of documentation, communication, expression, and play but critical sites and technologies for learning. Indeed, as recent research illustrates, games not only further the development of domain-specific knowledge but also provide the designed constraints – analog or digital – rendered necessary to learn specific practices. Moving beyond the content/context divide, this paper brings together methodological insights from ethnomethodology and conversation analysis with theoretical concepts and tools from game studies to reimagine what learning looks like in the peripheries of play. More specifically, it examines how the designed landscapes and environments of an immersive escape room served as a mediational resource and palimpsests that fostered and advanced consequential learning for players to “claim” or “exhibit” understanding.

title: Designing Measurements for Learning Transfer of Computational Thinking in Game-Based Learning Environment
citation: Liu, Z. (2024). Designing Measurements for Learning Transfer of Computational Thinking in Game-Based Learning Environment. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. authors_list: Liu, Z.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
abstract: This study reports the design and evaluation of measurement instruments to assess the transfer of computational thinking (CT) skills from a game-based learning environment to new contexts. A near transfer test and a far transfer test was designed by mapping game elements to an existing CT assessment. Although further refinement is needed to improve reliability and validity, the results provide initial evidence that tailored assessments can evaluate CT transfer beyond gameplay.

citation: Kim, C., Puntambekar, S., Lee, E., Gnesdilow, D., Karizaki, M. S., & Passonneau, R. (2024). NLP-Enabled Automated Feedback about Science Writing. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. abstract: Eighth grade students received automated feedback from PyrEval - an NLP tool - about their science essays. We examined essay quality change when revised. Regardless of prior physics knowledge, essay quality improved. Grounded in literature on AI explainability and trust in automated feedback, we also examined which PyrEval explanation predicted essay quality change. Essay quality improvement was predicted by high- and medium-accuracy feedback.

title: Sandboxing in Data Science: An Exploration of Youth Learning Using Open-Inquiry Approaches for Computing-based Data Mining
citation: Acquah, A., Barany, A., Johnson, M. A., Scarola, A. S., Rivera, C., & Walker, J. T. (2024). authors_list: Acquah, A., Barany, A., Johnson, M. A., Scarola, A. S., Rivera, C., & Walker, J. T.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; STEM - Natural Science
tpack_ck_labels: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; STEM - Natural Science
abstract: The integration of data science into high school computer science education is recognized for fostering productive learning with "big data." However, less attention has been placed on exercises where students generate datasets themselves rather than from sources curated by others, resulting in the need to explore learning designs that emphasize free inquiry. Few insights exist on designing and assessing learning outcomes in authentic practices, where learners lead inquiries and engagement processes. This research explores learning among eight youth participants in a two-week online computer science-based data mining workshop. Qualitative analysis of post-interviews and workshop artifacts reveals insights into youth learning during these activities. The findings highlight the significance of learning design strategies promoting active engagement in open-ended data science inquiries in computing education.

abstract: This study presents analysis of an episode about the sensemaking among facilitators and a researcher-designer about youth’s learning of artistic data visualization in an informal education program. With micro-analysis of discourse, it explores the framing and interpretation participants use about youth, the scope of framing, and themes when re-framing occurs. The findings speak to the dynamic nature of the resources used in educators’ sensemaking, as well as potential opportunities for re-framing that position youth in asset-oriented perspectives.

title: Learning With and About Technology in Rural Western India
citation: Kedari, A., Honwad, S., & Tirthali, D. (2024). Learning With and About Technology in Rural Western India. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding

abstract: A program addressing a global challenge in computer and ICT education for youth, was developed in rural Western India. Based on Culturally Relevant Computing (CRC) theories, the program emphasizes cultural relevance and tackles issues faced by rural students, such as limited internet access. Using the framework of a research-practice partnership, 20, 8th and 9th-grade students were recruited for the program. The program design objectives focused on critical thinking, collaboration, and technological understanding. Students selected topics, conducted research, interviewed community members, and authored articles that were published online. Through critical thinking, collaboration, and awareness of social justice in technology, the program aims to empower rural communities by supporting students to explore technologies for enhanced everyday living.

title: The Role of Entry Points in Defining, Cultivating, and Sustaining Community Learning with Data Artists
citation: Schafer, G., Dyer, E. B., Wright, C., Hodge, L., & Zhao, Y. (2024). The Role of Entry Points in Defining, Cultivating, and Sustaining Community Learning with Data Artists. International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Schafer, G., Dyer, E. B., Wright, C., Hodge, L., & Zhao, Y.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This poster proposal focuses on entry points as a lens for analyzing learning in community learning events (CLEs), which involve youth ‘data artists’ and community members. Thematic analysis of qualitative data is used to understand how entry points influence learning at CLEs and inform future iterations of the current project. Early analysis shows three emergent themes: geography and physicality; relationality, and communication.

title: Students’ Expressions of Community Health Concerns in the Third Space in a Community-Based Science Class
citation: Gyles, S. (2024). Students’ Expressions of Community Health Concerns in the Third Space in a Community-Based Science Class. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. authors_list: Gyles, S.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This qualitative study analyses a mechanism 7th and 8th grade Black and Latinx students used to express their understandings and knowledge of a socioscientific phenomenon when engaging in a community-based science curriculum. Findings demonstrate how students created third spaces in science learning, and provide educators with a conceptual understanding to be mindful of, and account for, when engaging in community-based science learning.

title: Connected Learning: A Dual Reflexive Pedagogical Identity
citation: Malcolm, B. (2024). Connected Learning: A Dual Reflexive Pedagogical Identity. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. T., & Suárez, E. authors_list: Malcolm, B.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This paper utilizes an interdisciplinary lens to explore self-learning as a critical pedagogical mechanism. The relational aspect of connected learning is specifically explored through Vygotsky’s sociocultural paradigm and Heinz Kohut’s theory of self psychology. Kohut views identity formation as a dual reflexive relational dynamic. Pedagogical identity construction, then, is a two-pronged relational sociocultural process. Exploration through this framework critically situates identity within learning.

abstract: This exploratory research analyzes the video-recorded data of four elementary-grade teachers debugging a school tour activity while utilizing a programable robot, Photon. This summer’s professional development session on computational thinking (CT) integration was four hours long and was focused on debugging as a key CT component. The results indicate that teachers worked collaboratively to debug their way through errors using different strategies, such as step-by-step execution or incremental code development.

title: Does Shrinking and Growing in VR Induce Awe In Young Students?
citation: Harper-Gampp, T., Delgado, C., Alharbi, K., Peterson, M., & Chen, K. B. (2024). Does Shrinking and Growing in VR Induce Awe In Young Students?. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Harper-Gampp, T., Delgado, C., Alharbi, K., Peterson, M., & Chen, K. B.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Awe enhances scientific learning, and is thought to be triggered by experiences of vastness or accommodation. We examined self-reported causes of awe among grade 3-6 students in a virtual environment where students can shrink and grow from the scale of an atom to the Sun. We implemented, reworded, and restructured survey items to modify a previously identified potentially leading item. Similar results suggest that the previously leading item did not inflate results. Most students indicated experiencing feelings of awe, with vastness as the primary cause. One response did relate to accommodation. Therefore, the results demonstrate that young students can experience awe in VR, and have the self-awareness to describe the need for accommodation.

International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Gutiérrez, J. F. & Onwubuya, G.
subject: STEM - Mathematics; Humanities, Language & Literacy
abstract: There is growing scholarship researching emergent bi/multilingual learners (MLs) in STEM contexts. However, there have been calls for more research on how students engage in content-specific work, such as mathematics. We present an in-process literature review that will contribute to discussions about supporting MLs in mathematics by identifying effective pedagogical practices, especially around two strands: 1) using translanguaging approaches, and 2) engaging in disciplinary practices, such as reasoning abstractly and quantitatively.

title: Leveraging Eye Gaze Data for Metacognition and Perceptual Scaffold in Visual Problems
citation: John, D. & Mitra, R. (2024). Leveraging Eye Gaze Data for Metacognition and Perceptual Scaffold in Visual Problems. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. authors_list: John, D. & Mitra, R.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
conceptualisations_list: Self-Regulated Learning (SRL) & Metacognition; Scaffolding & Guided Inquiry
abstract: An eye gaze display is a dynamic representation of a person's eye movement. Gaze displays capture problem solving processes due to the substantial coupling between a person’s eye movement, attention, and cognition. This has prompted the design of instructional approaches that assist learners in information processing and make expert processes observable. We consider a novel approach of using such displays to generate problems, where learners engage with another person's problem-solving process through questions that require them to interpret a gaze display within the context of the underlying problem. We analyze the verbalizations of a dyad solving such tasks to study the potential of such problems to elicit metacognition and offer perceptual scaffolding during problem solving.

title: Developing a Rubric to Evaluate the Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion Statement for Teaching Professors
citation: Arevalo, E., Sato, B. K., Lo, S. M., & Wilton, M. (2024). Developing a Rubric to Evaluate the Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion Statement for Teaching Professors. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Arevalo, E., Sato, B. K., Lo, S. M., & Wilton, M.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Issues of representation for faculty continue to be a challenge for institutions of higher education to address. Even within emerging faculty positions such as teaching professor/professors of teaching, there is a lack of diversity that is similar to research focused positions. To address this issue, we examined the hiring process for teaching professors/professors of teaching by designing an evaluation tool that promotes an equitable search process. More specifically, we designed a rubric that evaluates the work that has historically been undervalued. To design and construct our rubric, we utilized different aspects of design based research and faculty learning communities to ground and contextualize our rubric within communities of practitioners. From the design process, we present our validation process and key insights from our learning communities that informed our rubric.

title: Toward Writing Effective Solutions for Computational Problems: An Analysis of LeetCode Solutions
citation: Lu, Y. (2024). Toward Writing Effective Solutions for Computational Problems: An Analysis of LeetCode Solutions. In Lindgren, R., Asino, T. I., Kyza, E. A., Looi, C. K., Keifert, D. authors_list: Lu, Y.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; Humanities, Language & Literacy
tpack_ck_labels: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; Humanities, Language & Literacy
abstract: Solving computational problems plays a significant role in learning computer science. However, the complexity involved often leads to frustration. This study aims to address these challenges by finding out how we can write effective solutions. The author analyzed top-voted community-posted solutions and identified their common characteristics: detailed descriptions, clear code, mention of computer science terms, and efforts to engage readers. The results can inform future developments of guidelines for writing solutions.

abstract: This study responds to the challenge of cultural imperialism often encountered by teachers in non-western contexts. We report on a formative intervention (Engeström et al., 2014) for a community of teachers in Egypt, and the collective expansive learning they experienced through the process of designing culturally relevant pedagogies centered on 21st-century competencies. This study was conducted as part of the Critical Action Learning Exchange (CALE), an international community of critical educators (Carvalho et al., 2021).

title: Appropriating Tools to Foster Productive Professional Learning Conversations in a Literacy Coaching Program
citation: Li, T., Matsumura, L. C., Correnti, R., & Zook-Howell, D. (2024). Appropriating Tools to Foster Productive Professional Learning Conversations in a Literacy Coaching Program. abstract: Drawing on sociocultural theory, this study explores how literacy coach-teacher dyads use cognitive tools to foster productive professional learning conversations with respect to evidence-based specificity, establishment of a dialogic stance, and connecting specifics of lesson interactions to broader principles. The results reveal that, overall, the use of cognitive tools increased the quality of the coach-teacher professional learning conversations across all three dimensions. However, the integration of the tools in coach-teacher conversations was not consistent. Implications for coach professional development are discussed.
