We report our analysis of five design team meetings and five individual semi-structured interviews, spaced strategically throughout the design process. We share what design considerations the team prioritized over time and highlight how team members verbalized assumptions about student-centered learning.

title: Comparative Analysis of the Rule-Based and Machine Learning Approach for Assessing Student Reflections
citation: Butt, A. A., Anwar, S., Magooda, A., & Menekse, M. (2022). Comparative analysis of the rule-based and machine learning approach for assessing student reflections. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1577-1580). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Butt, A. A., Anwar, S., Magooda, A., & Menekse, M.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; STEM - Engineering & Robotics; Humanities, Language & Literacy
tpack_ck_labels: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; STEM - Engineering & Robotics; Humanities, Language & Literacy
abstract: This study describes Natural Language Processing (NLP) and rule-based algorithms used to assess the students’ written reflection quality. We used the CourseMIRROR application to gather student reflections from 120 engineering students and converted the reflections into an equivalent quality score using human coders and algorithms. We used Cohen’s kappa statistics to explore the agreement between the algorithm’s reflection quality and the human coding. The results revealed a strong agreement between the NLP algorithm and human coding. Furthermore, we used Spearman correlation statistics to evaluate the relationship between the predicted quality scores and the human coding. The results showed a strong correlation between reflection quality evaluated by the NLP algorithm and human coders. Overall results revealed that the NLP algorithm embedded in the CourseMIRROR application is a good fit for assessing students’ reflections and can be used to guide them during the reflection writing process.

title: “Love Struggle, Love Self, Regardless*:” Arts Organization Leader’s Use of Socio-Historical Analytic Artifacts in Their Determinations of Successful Teaching Artists
citation: Bryant, J. (2022). “Love struggle, love self, regardless*:” arts organization leader’s use of socio-historical analytic artifacts in their determinations of successful teaching artists. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1581-1584). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Bryant, J.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Black artists fill the (art)world with images, objects, sounds, and experiences that disrupt sociopsychological functions shaped by anti-Black racism (Fanon, 1952; Wynter, 1999, 2005; Gikandi, 2011). Learning in and through the arts has been a major vehicle for animating Black communities’ resistance to dehumanizing experiences across space and time. Out-ofschool time arts organizations serve as fugitive learning ecologies where creative risks can be taken up and celebrated as material and embodied forms of resistance. This paper details the ways three Black women-identifying out-of-school time arts organization (BW-OSTA) leaders use social analytic artifacts (Vossoughi, 2014) derived from an historical art exemplar to determine what makes a successful teaching artist. Using a socio-historical approach to remediation (Cole & Griffin, 1983) and risk (Lee, 2009), this paper tethers the politics and ethics of an exemplary Black artist to the determinations of successful teaching made by three contemporary BW-OSTA leaders.

title: Moments of Pedagogical Feedback With Explanations: Interactional Foundations for Supporting Educational Dignity
citation: Echevarria, R., Vogelstein, L., & Jackson, A. (2022). Moments of pedagogical feedback with explanations: Interactional foundations for supporting educational dignity. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1585-1588). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Echevarria, R., Vogelstein, L., & Jackson, A.
subject: Social & Civic Studies
abstract: This paper explores pedagogical design processes of educational dignity by analyzing data across three learning contexts and configurations–a facilitator and student in a museum-based tinkering environment, a professional choreographer and dancers in their dance studio, and two students in a high school history class–to show how moments of feedback with explanations can contribute to the process of coordination in joint activity, invite meaningful participation, and support educational dignity. In particular, we present three case studies to illustrate two primary findings: (1) through moments of feedback with explanations, participants invited one another to embody forms of meaningful participation, and (2) these invitations to engage in meaningful participation created a collective, educationally dignifying conceptual space in which activity was continued forward. These findings offer developing insights into the how and towards what ends of designing for educationally dignifying learning environments, contributing to discussions on the revisioning of equitable education systems.

title: Tuning Perceptions and Inferences to See a Graph in a New Way
citation: Swanson, H., Sherin, B., & Wilensky, U. (2022). Tuning perceptions and inferences to see a graph in a new way. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1589-1592). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Swanson, H., Sherin, B., & Wilensky, U.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This work examines the representational and social features of a computational modeling activity to understand the role they play in helping a student make sense of a simulation graph. Specifically, it examines shifts in the student’s thinking as she reflects on the output of a computational model of thermal equilibration, which she has built. By analyzing the student’s trajectory through the lens of Coordination Class theory, the paper illuminates how she comes to see the simulation graph in a more sophisticated way through her interactions with the technology and the interviewer. The paper shows how these features of the computational modeling activity support her transition from seeing oscillations of temperature about the mean as a visual effect caused by the computer screen, to understanding that oscillation amplitudes are related to microscopic fluctuations in temperature, which decrease as the number of particles in the system increases.

title: Proposing a Role-Based Framework for Data Literacy
citation: Risha, Z., Mallavarapu, A., Farzan, R., Booth, J., Sondel, B., & Walker, E. (2022). Proposing a role-based framework for data literacy. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1601-1604). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Risha, Z., Mallavarapu, A., Farzan, R., Booth, J., Sondel, B., & Walker, E.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; Humanities, Language & Literacy
tpack_ck_labels: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; Humanities, Language & Literacy
abstract: Efforts to cultivate critical data literacies in youth calls for further research that emphasizes supporting collaboration in team environments. We propose a role-based framework of four roles (Journalist, Detective, Scientist, and Artist) that seeks to go beyond just facilitating data analysis by representing the multitude of ways data literacy plays a role in people’s lives. We pilot our role-based curriculum within an advocacy-focused summer program to study how our approach facilitates collaboration and critical data literacies.

title: Atunements to Socioecological Histories of Places in Learning and Decision-Making in Complex Socioecological Systems
citation: Bang, M., Tzou, C., Bricker, L., Sherry-Wagner, J., & Pugh, P. (2022). Atunements to socioecological histories of places in learning and decision-making in complex socioecological systems. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1605-1608). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Bang, M., Tzou, C., Bricker, L., Sherry-Wagner, J., & Pugh, P.
subject: STEM - Natural Science; Social & Civic Studies
tpack_ck_labels: STEM - Natural Science; Social & Civic Studies
abstract: Socio-ecological histories of places are political, contested, and intimately linked with ways of knowing and being in the world. Supporting students in perspective taking and reasoning through contested histories of places are equity practices that allow for multiple and diverse stories to be told, honored, and incorporated in science learning. In this paper, we describe an approach to teaching about socio ecological systems from the Learning in Places project using a framework called Socioecological Histories of Places. We first describe the framework and its design within the Learning in Places project. We then analyze one teacher’s implementation of this approach and discuss implications for understanding issues of power, historicity, and ethical decision-making in field-based science learning and teaching.

title: Disruptions, Dissent, and Discontinuities: What Tensions in Intergenerational Learning Dynamics Reveal About Learning Design
citation: Widman, S., Hayden, R., Stamatis, K., & Roque, R. (2022). Disruptions, dissent, and discontinuities: What tensions in intergenerational learning dynamics reveal about learning design. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1613-1616). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Widman, S., Hayden, R., Stamatis, K., & Roque, R.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This paper describes family member participation in an informal learning setting called Family Create Nights. With attention to the design of equity oriented STEAM learning experiences, we argue that looking at moments of tension or disruption in families’ work together may reveal important needs and desires of learners. Our analysis reveals the ways families positioned themselves in terms of expertise, created collaborative arrangements for working together, and asserted creative control through their project creation. Findings point to the importance of holistically attending to families learning needs, to highlight parents' own curiosities as well as the roles of youth as facilitators and educators within their families.

title: Mapping the Landscape of Assessment in Out-of-School Time Arts Learning
citation: Saplan, K., Norman, K. E., & Probst, C. (2022). Mapping the landscape of assessment in out-of-school time arts learning. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1621-1624). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Saplan, K., Norman, K. E., & Probst, C.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This study represents the first USA-based qualitative investigation on assessment in out-of-school time (OST) arts education. While analysis for this project is ongoing, preliminary findings show how arts leaders conceive of assessment and how those conceptions influenced their practices for documenting and assessing arts learning. By mapping the current landscape of assessment in OST arts learning, we can more clearly identify existing practices and opportunities to adapt and reimagine assessment.

title: Centring BlackJoy in Design for Learning and Research
citation: Adams, J. D. (2022). Centring BlackJoy in design for learning and research. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1625-1628). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Adams, J. D.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This theoretical paper presentation will articulate BlackJoy as a framework for designing research-to-practice spaces that centre Black liberation and flourishing for authentically equitable learning engagements and to counter ongoing deficit narratives and corresponding oppressions that Black and other racialized/minoritized learners experience in schools and other learning environments. The BlackJoy heuristic has four key tenets: Black Excellence, Black Inventiveness, Black Kinship and Black Aesthetics. Data and vignettes from prior research projects will be described of examples of BlackJoy in education and used as a point of departure discussions about the design of research and learning environments that cultivate BlackJoy and expanded ways to think about evidences of learning.

title: Decomposing Practice: Developing Reliable Analyses of Complex Classroom Discussion
citation: Sushil, S., Dennis, K., Clarke, S. N., Gates, Z., Tripathi, T., Gomoll, A., Leung, V., Lee, U., & Lee, B. (2022). Decomposing practice: Developing reliable analyses of complex classroom discussion. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1629-1632). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Sushil, S., Dennis, K., Clarke, S. N., Gates, Z., Tripathi, T., Gomoll, A., Leung, V., Lee, U., & Lee, B.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: There is relatively scant conversation about the details of processes through which research teams arrive at desirable thresholds of statistical measures for inter-rater reliability (IRR) in qualitative research. This paper used autoethnography to describe how a team of five researchers achieved a Cohen’s Kappa of .7 between each pair of researchers over a period of two years while iteratively developing a codebook to be applied to science classroom discussion transcripts. Detailed meeting notes kept by the researchers were used as data. The findings describe factors that contributed to the complexity of the transcripts, strategies that worked for the team, and the role of the purpose of the analysis in shaping the process of the analysis. Some implications for the field of teacher learning are discussed based on these findings.

title: Making Sense of Integer Story-Interpretation Problems
citation: Aqazade, M. (2022). Making sense of integer story-interpretation problems. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 163-170). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Aqazade, M.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Exploring students’ conceptions of integers is more complex than simply explaining the elements of integer knowledge and certainly is challenging to describe how those elements are structured. In this paper, I highlight how fifth graders restructured their whole-number knowledge elements to establish an integer knowledge structure by exploring their interpretations of two integer story-interpretation problems. Students with correct integer order and value interpretations were most successful in solving these problems. Students who knew negative numbers are less than positive numbers but had difficulties interpreting integers’ values were more successful than those who relied on numbers’ absolute value. However, they attempted to use the negative signs in their number-sentences. This study informs the importance of triangulating students’ integer knowledge elements, the process of forming an integer knowledge structure, and further highlights the significance of using problem-solving situations that allow for eliciting diverse mathematical thinking and learning processes.

title: Supporting Empathy in Design Thinking - A Learning Community Approach
citation: Khan, R., Raman, P., & Slotta, J. D. (2022). Supporting empathy in design thinking - a learning community approach. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1641-1644). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Khan, R., Raman, P., & Slotta, J. D.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Empathy plays an imperative role in human-centered design thinking processes. Our research explores how a learning community approach can help students become empathetic designers. By situating the design experience within a community of peers, there are increased opportunities for norming and exchange, shared strategies and resources, and a sense of collective progress. Such design activities allow students to bring in their voices and identities by offering empathetic feedback into the classroom discourse. Using the Knowledge Community and Inquiry (KCI) model, we explore how the diversity in the dispositions and experiences of students plays a unique and major role in framing and shaping design problems through peer feedback and perspective-taking. This paper reports the findings from six graduate-level courses that offered a design assignment in an education faculty taught over two years.

title: Students’ Self-Regulated Use of Diagrams in a Choice-Based Intelligent Tutoring System
citation: Nagashima, T., Tseng, S., Ling, E., Bartel, A. N., Vest, N. A., Silla, E. M., Alibali, M. W., & Aleven, V. (2022). Students’ self-regulated use of diagrams in a choice-based intelligent tutoring system. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1649-1652). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Nagashima, T., Tseng, S., Ling, E., Bartel, A. N., Vest, N. A., Silla, E. M., Alibali, M. W., & Aleven, V.
subject: STEM - Mathematics
abstract: Learners’ choices as to whether and how to use visual representations during learning are an important yet understudied aspect of self-regulated learning. To gain insight, we developed a choice-based intelligent tutor in which students can choose whether and when to use diagrams to aid their problem solving in algebra. In an exploratory classroom study with 26 students, we investigated how learners choose diagrams and how their choice behaviors relate to learning outcomes. Students who proactively chose to use diagrams achieved higher learning outcomes than those who reactively used diagrams when they made incorrect attempts. This study contributes to understanding of self-regulated use of visual representations during problem solving.

title: Designing an Adaptive Dialogue to Promote Science Understanding
citation: Gerard, L., Bichler, S., Bradford, A., Linn, M. C., Steimel, K., & Riordan, B. (2022). Designing an adaptive dialogue to promote science understanding. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1653-1656). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Gerard, L., Bichler, S., Bradford, A., Linn, M. C., Steimel, K., & Riordan, B.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: We used Natural Language Processing (NLP) to design an adaptive computer dialogue that engages students in a conversation to reflect on and revise their written explanations of a science dilemma. We study the accuracy of the NLP idea detection. We analyze how 98 12-13 year-olds interacted with the dialogue as a part of a Diagnostic Inventory. We study students’ initial and revised science explanations along with their logged responses to the dialogue. The dialogue led to a high rate of student revision compared to prior studies of adaptive guidance. The adaptive prompt encouraged students to reflect on prior experiences, to consider new variables, and to raise scientific questions. Students incorporated these new ideas when revising their initial explanations. We discuss how these adaptive dialogues can strengthen science instruction.

title: Implementation of Dialogic Teaching: Exploring Teachers’ Perceptions, Attitudes, and Practical Challenges
citation: Tao, Y. & Chen, G. (2022). Implementation of dialogic teaching: Exploring teachers’ perceptions, attitudes, and practical challenges. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1657-1660). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Tao, Y. & Chen, G.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
conceptualisations_list: Accountable Talk & Dialogic Discourse; Classroom Orchestration
abstract: Research interest in discursive strategies for orchestrating vibrant classroom interactions has burgeoned. Few studies, however, have given details about teachers’ perceptions and attitudes. This paper reports on an on-going study that explored elementary and secondary school teachers’ perceptions and attitudes towards dialogic teaching and the challenges they encountered in the implementation. We recruited three elementary and middle school teachers from different subjects in China to participate in the video-cued interview. The results showed that some teachers with professional vision on dialogic teaching, though attitudinally in favor of this pedagogical approach, tended to be reluctant to adopt it for fear of losing face or being challenged by their students. In parallel, students’ learning ability, learning efficiency, and willingness to participate in class may obstruct teachers’ efforts to unfold classroom instruction in a dialogical way. These findings help enrich our understanding of the effective implementation of dialogic teaching.

title: Understanding and Leveraging Contradictions of Instructional Activities for Fostering Students’ Agency
citation: Swamy, N. & Dasgupta, C. (2022). Understanding and leveraging contradictions of instructional activities for fostering students’ agency. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1661-1664). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Swamy, N. & Dasgupta, C.
subject: STEM - Natural Science
conceptualisations_list: Cultural-Historical Activity Theory (CHAT); Constructionism & Maker-Centered Learning
abstract: Instructional activities are situated in a web of interdependent activity systems such as students’ families, educational institutes, research programs, industries and governments. Historically accumulating tensions between these systems are said to impose contradictory demands on students. For example, during learning, students often feel compelled to choose between being a grade maker versus a sense maker. Such deep-rooted problems cannot be addressed by simply finding better ways of implementing existing practices. Hence we revisit key ideas such as instruction, feedback, competence and their interconnections by considering contradictions across activity systems. Then we carve out a space for students’ agency within such interconnections by introducing and investigating a construct called ‘students’ feedback seeking actions’ using cultural historical activity theory (CHAT). Finally, its affordances in further uncovering and leveraging contradictions of instructional activities for fostering students’ agency are explored using a case study from undergraduate chemistry education.

title: Increasing College STEM Instructors’ Equity-Oriented Teaching Competencies
citation: Phuong, A. E., Nguyen, J., Vo, J., Hunn, C. T., & Mejia, F. D. (2022). Increasing college STEM instructors’ equity-oriented teaching competencies. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1665-1668). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Phuong, A. E., Nguyen, J., Vo, J., Hunn, C. T., & Mejia, F. D.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This study examines what helps university STEM instructors learn and adopt inclusive teaching practices, such as Adaptive Equity-Oriented Pedagogy (AEP). AEP has been shown to improve student achievement by over a full-letter grade. This study randomly assigned 129 student-instructors to treatment and control pedagogy courses. While the control course taught student-instructors about AEP, the treatment course modeled AEP explicitly by using weekly student-instructor reflection data to continuously adjust course discussion and activities. Using multilevel-regression modeling, we found the treatment significantly improved studentinstructors’ AEP competencies over time compared to the control (p<0.001). Compared to the control, more student-instructors in the treatment used multiple data sources to adjust teaching and address equity barriers to advance student learning. Through the novel application of mixed-methods research and validated AEP measures, this study offers insights on what values, motivations, and practices characterize those who do and do not implement AEP.

title: Design-Based Research to Improve the Lesson Study Project for Co-Evolution of Research, Development and Practices
citation: Iikubo, S., Shirouzu, H., & Saito, M. (2022). Design-based research to improve the lesson study project for co-evolution of research, development and practices. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1669-1672). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Iikubo, S., Shirouzu, H., & Saito, M.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: In order to demonstrate that applying design-based research (DBR) methodology to improve a lesson study project provides an arena for co-evolution of implementation research, system development and everyday practices, this paper analyzed a 12-year learning sciences project in Japan. The project consisted of DBR on three levels: 1) a continuous cycle of DBR on each of the practices in the lesson study cycle, 2) DBR on the development of technologies to support the lesson studies and 3) long-term implementation research on the whole sociotechnical system to bridge theory and practice. The analysis revealed that the scheme of the project shifted to support fast but constructive lesson study for practitioners to create design principles based on an understanding of how students learn, requiring the co-evolution above.

title: The Multicompetent Learners
citation: Pérez, G. (2022). The multicompetent learners. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1677-1680). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Pérez, G.
subject: STEM - Engineering & Robotics; Humanities, Language & Literacy
tpack_ck_labels: STEM - Engineering & Robotics; Humanities, Language & Literacy
abstract: Engineering and science are meant to develop solutions and knowledge for a diverse population, yet Black and Brown communities often remain excluded from these intellectual enterprises. This work builds on prior literature in the learning sciences, sociolinguistics as well as science and engineering education to improve access for culturally and linguistically diverse communities. It aims at creating socially just learning spaces where individuals can bring their whole selves through introducing the notion of multicompetent learners described in terms of their language practices, cultural understandings and cognitive resources.

title: The aRithmetic Discourse Profile as a Tool for Mapping Students’ Subjectifying and Mathematizing Discourse
citation: Heyd-Metzuyanim, E., Tabach, M., & Elbaum-Cohen, A. (2022). The arithmetic discourse profile as a tool for mapping students’ subjectifying and mathematizing discourse. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 171-178). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Heyd-Metzuyanim, E., Tabach, M., & Elbaum-Cohen, A.
subject: STEM - Mathematics
abstract: We present a new tool for mapping students’ arithmetic discourse, named the aRithmetic Discourse Profile (RDP). The tool was developed based on the commognitive theory (Sfard, 2008). Its main goal is mapping students’ mastery of arithmetic routines on a continuum between ritual (procedure based) and explorative (goal-based) participation. In addition, the tool maps the subjectifying statements of students (statements constructing their identity in action) to assess the affective aspects of the student’s performance. We exemplify the tool on 3 tasks performed by 12 7th grade students. The findings show various possible relations between subjectifying and ritual/explorative performance.

title: Moving Toward Dignity-Affirming Invitations to Embodied Participation in the Design of Learning Environments
citation: Mathayas, N., Vogelstein, L., Danish, J., Lindberg, L., Marin, A., Kern, A., Orellana, M., Meixi, Dorr, S., Keefe, D., Diaz, V., Zohar, R., Tu, X., Cosic, L., Vickery, M., & Kelton, M. (2022). Moving toward dignity-affirming invitations to embodied participation in the design of learning environments. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1739-1746). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Mathayas, N., Vogelstein, L., Danish, J., Lindberg, L., Marin, A., Kern, A., Orellana, M., Meixi, Dorr, S., Keefe, D., Diaz, V., Zohar, R., Tu, X., Cosic, L., Vickery, M., & Kelton, M.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This symposium questions a basic assumption in the research and design of embodied learning environments: that the embodied forms of participation we design for will always be taken up as good and desired by participants. Across five papers, we reflect on our own design work across various contexts to think about how embodied learning spaces have and can invite embodied forms of participation that engage learners in meaningful participation while also affirming their dignity and human becoming. Across our work we seek to understand how learners’ dignity intersects with embodiment. Together our research offers new directions in embodied methodologies and the design of embodied technologies and activities.

title: Data Storytelling in the Classroom
citation: Matuk, C., Amato, A., Davidesco, I., Rubel, L., Stornaiuolo, A., Bumbacher, E., Chance, B., DesPortes, K., Eloy, A., Fagan, E., Fuhrmann, T., Gebre, E., Herbel-Eisenmann, B., Jiang, S., Kahn, J., Lim, V., Louie, J., Peralta, L. M., Roy, S., Silander, M., St. Clair, N., Stephens, L., Stiles, J., Glaser, N., Naipaul, J., Tes, M., Vacca, R., Wagh, A., Wei, X., McBride, C., Wilkerson, M., Wolf, J., & Woods, P. J. (2022). Data storytelling in the classroom. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1779-1786). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Matuk, C., Amato, A., Davidesco, I., Rubel, L., Stornaiuolo, A., Bumbacher, E., Chance, B., DesPortes, K., Eloy, A., Fagan, E., Fuhrmann, T., Gebre, E., Herbel-Eisenmann, B., Jiang, S., Kahn, J., Lim, V., Louie, J., Peralta, L. M., Roy, S., Silander, M., Clair, N. S., Stephens, L., Stiles, J., Glaser, N., Naipaul, J., Tes, M., Vacca, R., Wagh, A., Wei, X., McBride, C., Wilkerson, M., Wolf, J., & Woods, P. J.
subject: Humanities, Language & Literacy
abstract: With the rising demand for data skills across industries and disciplines, and the prevalence of data in all aspects and levels of our lives, it is critical to find new, more effective ways to develop students’ data literacies. Stories can be an accessible way for students to personally connect to, and think critically about, data and its implications. But how can data storytelling be effectively implemented into classroom settings, in which instruction is often constrained to focus narrowly on quantitative skills? This interactive poster session showcases eight innovations in data storytelling in the classroom. Together, the contributions consider the various facets and functions of stories for supporting data literacies in contexts that span K-12 to university. By seeking to define the value and roles of storytelling in data literacy learning, this session will inform ways to create more effective and engaging data literacy instruction.

title: The Nature(s) of Embodied Mathematical Failure
citation: Simpson, A., Williams-Pierce, C., Shokeen, E., Katirci, N., Soto, H., Baker, J., DeLiema, D., Kapur, M., Ellis, A., Lockwood, E., Plaxco, D., Alibali, M. W., & Ramirez, D. (2022). The nature(s) of embodied mathematical failure. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1787-1793). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Simpson, A., Williams-Pierce, C., Shokeen, E., Katirci, N., Soto, H., Baker, J., DeLiema, D., Kapur, M., Ellis, A., Lockwood, E., Plaxco, D., Alibali, M. W., & Ramirez, D.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: The purpose of this symposium is to consider the embodied nature of failure in different learning environments, contexts, mathematical situations, and age groups. Our exploratory work was guided by the following questions: (a) How is failure represented through our bodily actions? (b) How is failure co-constructed through our bodies? (c) How are our reactions to failure embodied? (d) How might embodied failure be framed or conceptualized across mathematical situations? We explore these questions through a close examination of the intersection of embodied cognition, failure, and mathematical activity as presented and challenged by a diverse spectrum of scholars. While grounded in mathematical activity, this symposium will contribute to the ongoing state of learning science research regarding how the mind, body, and environment work together to highlight student’s reasoning and thinking, particularly within moments of failure.

title: Designs for Grounded and Embodied Mathematical Learning
citation: Nathan, M. J., Walkington, C., & Swart, M. I. (2022). Designs for grounded and embodied mathematical learning. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 179-186). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Nathan, M. J., Walkington, C., & Swart, M. I.
subject: STEM - Mathematics
abstract: Findings synthesized across five empirical, laboratory- and classroom-based studies of high school and college students engaged in geometric reasoning and proof production during single and multi-session investigations (346 participants overall) are presented. The findings converge on several design principles for embodied mathematical thinking and learning. The Hidden Village is presented as an instance of an embodied learning environment that uses the narrative context of a visual novel to instantiate these design principles and investigate their influences on mathematical thinking and learning, and to inform a broader theoretical framework of grounded and embodied learning. The interplay of theoretical, empirical, and design considerations of grounded and embodied learning reframes learning, transfer, and assessment, offering promising new pathways for an emerging class of learning environments.

title: Mapping the Complexities and Benefits of Research-Design Partnerships
citation: Mercier, E., Lawrence, L., Ahn, J., Wegemer, C., Benichou, M., Kali, Y., Hod, Y., Borge, M., Gomez, K., Lee, U., McKenney, S., Poortman, C., Arce-Trigatti, P., & Cheng, B. H. (2022). Mapping the complexities and benefits of research-design partnerships. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1794-1801). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Mercier, E., Lawrence, L., Ahn, J., Wegemer, C., Benichou, M., Kali, Y., Hod, Y., Borge, M., Gomez, K., Lee, U., McKenney, S., Poortman, C., Arce-Trigatti, P., & Cheng, B. H.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Increasingly our field is recognizing the necessity of close, collaborative relationships with educators, policy makers, students and other potential stakeholders if our design and research work is to have a lasting and more equitable impact on education. However, this work is not easy or quick, and we lack both detailed examples of how it is done and training for new (and current) scholars in how to do it. This symposium brings together a group of scholars who actively engage in RPPs and DBIR in order to highlight the lessons that have been learned and extend our discourse into the realities of this work, how to prepare students and current scholars to design their work with partners at the center, and how to accurately plan for work that engages stakeholders.

title: Regulation of Teaching as an Individual or Collaborative Process: Theory Meets Practice
citation: Zhu, G., Greisel, M., Hegele, R., Printz, H., León, J. M., Calzado, L., Nazeem, R., Borge, M., Teo, C. L., & Bernaus, M. (2022). Regulation of teaching as an individual or collaborative process: Theory meets practice. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1802-1809). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Zhu, G., Greisel, M., Hegele, R., Printz, H., León, J. M., Calzado, L., Nazeem, R., Borge, M., Teo, C. L., & Bernaus, M.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: There are calls for researchers and practitioners to build joint communities to narrow down research-practice gaps. Regulation of teaching, a process during which teachers direct attention, set goals, plan, monitor and evaluate their teaching for improvement, is very likely to benefit from communication and collaboration between researchers and teachers given its complexity in terms of multiple phases and various levels. This symposium aims to facilitate researchers’ and practitioners’ direct conversations on self-, co-, or socially shared teaching regulation. A theoretical framework that details different phases of teaching regulation at the self-, co-, or socially shared teaching levels guides teachers’ reflections on their teaching regulation, which then serve as a basis for a panel discussion between three (groups of) teachers and three invited researchers. The panel discussion will be focused on identifying practical challenges and research gaps regarding teaching regulation and discussing how teacher and researcher communities can collaboratively respond to these issues.

title: Supporting Multilingualism in Preschool: A Play Responsive Teaching Approach Mediated by Digital Technologies
citation: Shengjergji, S., Niklas, P., & Jenny, M. (2022). Supporting multilingualism in preschool: A play responsive teaching approach mediated by digital technologies. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1822-1823). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Shengjergji, S., Niklas, P., & Jenny, M.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This design-based research focuses on timely challenges such as multilingualism and the use of digital technologies that teaching in preschool is facing. Play-responsive teaching is the theory that informs the design and implementation of the study. Data will be generated from recordings where children and teachers engage in playful activities with tablets where multiple languages may be used. Analysis will investigate how teaching in preschool can be responsive to multilingualism by utilizing digital technologies (tablets).

title: Conceptualizations of Teaching and Learning in Impact Statements for Tenure and Promotion
citation: Donaldson, J. P., Chowdhury, M., Zowam, S., Lupiani, B., Wilkinson, H., Larson, B., & Wallace, W. (2022). Conceptualizations of teaching and learning in impact statements for tenure and promotion. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1824-1825). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Donaldson, J. P., Chowdhury, M., Zowam, S., Lupiani, B., Wilkinson, H., Larson, B., & Wallace, W.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This study investigated conceptualizations of teaching and learning using complex systems theory and network analysis. In 226 impact statements for promotion and tenure in one university we found two conceptualizations. In the Content-Processing conceptualization, teaching is the delivery of content and learning is acquisition of knowledge. In the FramingFacilitation conceptualization, teaching is preparation of students for future careers and imparting truth, and learning is skill development. We also identified leverage points within each conceptualization.

title: The Gateway for Optimizing Design of Micro-Credentials:Higher Education Faculty
citation: Reed, A. & Abramovich, S. (2022). The gateway for optimizing design of micro-credentials:higher education faculty. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1826-1827). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Reed, A. & Abramovich, S.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
abstract: Despite the growing prevalence of micro-credentials in higher education, there is still no consensus on best design practices. To address this, we identified existing design knowledge held by faculty that designed micro-credentials in a pilot program at a large public research university. We found that faculty may know how to design micro-credentials to address credentialing affordances, but may need support in recognizing and designing for assessment affordances.

title: Taking Up Opportunities to Practice in a Social Studies-Themed Digital Simulation Game: A Quantitative Ethnography
citation: Kessner, T. (2022). Taking up opportunities to practice in a social studies-themed digital simulation game: A quantitative ethnography. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1828-1829). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Kessner, T.
subject: STEM - Engineering & Robotics; Social & Civic Studies
tpack_ck_labels: STEM - Engineering & Robotics; Social & Civic Studies
abstract: We use quantitative ethnography and Epistemic Network Analysis to examine how the social studies-themed digital simulation game Offworld Trading Company generates opportunities for players to practice using disciplinary knowledge, skills, and concepts (DKSCs) as tools for taking goal-mediated action. Our study design places particular emphasis on establishing inferences regarding specific game mechanics as generative of such opportunities to practice, as well as the DKSCs they invite and require of players.

title: Undergraduate and Graduate Student Perspective on Teaching for Critical Pedagogy
citation: Reyes, P. O. & Govea, C. (2022). Undergraduate and graduate student perspective on teaching for critical pedagogy. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1830-1831). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Reyes, P. O. & Govea, C.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: In critical pedagogy there is an intrinsically interrelated relationship between education and society. The fundamental purpose for education is to improve society and fight for justice for all. These core ideas translate into a set of principles for the design of transformational learning. These principles involve rejecting positivism and embracing constructivism, developing critical consciousness, questioning assumptions, learner autonomy and authority, and transforming realities. To explore these principles, the first and second author presents an autoethnographic analysis of these principles in their own educational experience.

title: Looking Beyond Disciplinary Silos: Students’ Interdisciplinary Science Understanding of Carbon Cycling
citation: You, H. & Hong, M. (2022). Looking beyond disciplinary silos: Students’ interdisciplinary science understanding of carbon cycling. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1832-1833). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: You, H. & Hong, M.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Natural phenomena and scientific issues are intrinsically interdisciplinary. A variety of academic disciplines of natural science are essential for students to explain a phenomenon or related issues along with their reasonings for the phenomenon. The primary goal of the current study is to examine how students’ interdisciplinary understanding of carbon cycling manifests itself using the latent Dirichlet allocation model. This study provides important insight into the potential impact on diverse curricular and instructional approaches in science.

title: Instructional Dialogues in an Inquiry-Based Classroom: Towards a Typology of Teacher Self-Positioning
citation: So, H. W. & Cheng, K. L. (2022). Instructional dialogues in an inquiry-based classroom: Towards a typology of teacher self-positioning. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1834-1835). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: So, H. W. & Cheng, K. L.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Effective classroom dialogues are vital for knowledge building in inquiry-based classrooms, and the positioning of teachers and students play an essential role. This qualitative study explored the patterns of and decision-making process underpinning the dialogues through analyzing lesson recordings and conducting stimulated recall interviews. Three types of teacher self-positioning were identified, which were associated with considering the cognitive-developmental needs of the respective students and the contextual constraints.

title: Effects of Narratives on Undergraduate Student Understanding of Fundamental Concepts in Biology
citation: Tobler, S., Sinha, T., Köhler, K., Hafen, E., & Kapur, M. (2022). Effects of narratives on undergraduate student understanding of fundamental concepts in biology. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1836-1837). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Tobler, S., Sinha, T., Köhler, K., Hafen, E., & Kapur, M.
subject: STEM - Natural Science
abstract: Undergraduate students frequently struggle to understand biological concepts. Embedding conceptual information in a historical narrative holds the potential to support their learning. We developed learning materials comparing narrative or expository texts and assessed studentsÕ conceptual understanding via post-tests. Results showed that students, who read the narrative text, understood the concept of randomness better. No difference was found for the enzyme energetics concept. Furthermore, students in the narrative group reported higher situational interest after the intervention. Keywords: Narrative, Biology, Conceptual Change, Understanding, Higher Education

title: Building an Interdisciplinary Community of Emerging Scholars Amid the COVID-19 Pandemic
citation: Dragnić-Cindrić, D., Fusco, J., & Roschelle, J. (2022). Building an interdisciplinary community of emerging scholars amid the COVID-19 pandemic. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1840-1841). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Dragnić-Cindrić, D., Fusco, J., & Roschelle, J.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
abstract: With increasing funding for synergistic research and educational solutions informed by multiple disciplines (e.g., learning sciences, computer science), there is a need to build the field’s interdisciplinary capacity and nurture the next generation of researchers. In this poster, we share our approach to creating a community of emerging scholars inspired by the concept of landscapes of practice and based on a design thinking process. We discuss our approach’s key design features, affordances, and challenges.

title: Examining the Complex Webs of Supports That Sustain Classroom Practices
citation: Zeller, L. (2022). Examining the complex webs of supports that sustain classroom practices. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1842-1843). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Zeller, L.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Reform of educational systems is difficult, with changes often fading or diverting in unproductive ways. To disrupt this pattern and understand why unwanted practices persist and new ones distort, we need to consider how new and old practices are sustained at multiple levels. I discuss the framing and methodological findings from a larger study that investigated practices and supports within an undergraduate course for elementary education majors and discuss how these can inform educational change.

title: Imagining Inquisitive Futures for Learners With Developmental Disabilities
citation: Sedgwick, M. (2022). Imagining inquisitive futures for learners with developmental disabilities. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1844-1845). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Sedgwick, M.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Two activists with developmental disabilities designed a learning activity for learners with developmental disabilities. Their talk during design meetings was analyzed using discourse analysis (Gee & Green, 1998) to learn what imagined futures (Gutiérrez & Jurow, 2016) they assumed for the learners. These futures tended towards the inquisitive, and suggest that including activists in the development of learning activities for youth from the communities those activists represent could lead to fruitful new designs.

title: Strategies to Manage Scientific Uncertainties for Productive Sensemaking
citation: Ha, H., Park, J., & Chen, Y. (2022). Strategies to manage scientific uncertainties for productive sensemaking: Case studies from korean and american classrooms. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1846-1847). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Ha, H., Park, J., & Chen, Y.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This study aims to explore instructional strategies to manage students’ scientific uncertainties in sensemaking activities in the science classroom. Sensemaking activities in four science teachers’ classrooms were analyzed for this study, two from Korea and two from the USA. The analyzed data include video-recordings of classroom discourses. Six themes about features of teachers’ instructional strategies that supported students’ productive management of the uncertainties were identified through analysis.

title: Student Motivation in Science Learning With Embodied Computational Thinking
citation: Dohn, N. B. & Dohn, N. B. (2022). Student motivation in science learning with embodied computational thinking. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1850-1851). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Dohn, N. B. & Dohn, N. B.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; STEM - Natural Science
tpack_ck_labels: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; STEM - Natural Science
abstract: In an on-going multiple-case study, we investigate the use of unplugged, embodied Computational Thinking activities to learn topics within biology and chemistry. We utilize Educational Design Research in collaboration with 4 teachers at 2 upper secondary schools, focusing on students’ experience and how the activities affect their motivation for learning the topics in question. Tentative results indicate that students find such activities fun, allowing them to address curricular content in new ways, but also confusing.

title: Informing Advanced Digital Technologies’ Design for Refugee Language Education in Greece
citation: Tzirides, A. O. (2022). Informing advanced digital technologies’ design for refugee language education in greece. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1852-1853). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Tzirides, A. O.
subject: Humanities, Language & Literacy
abstract: This paper focuses on needs finding for computer-assisted language learning for vulnerable population living in difficult circumstances. It presents semi-structured interviews with teachers and volunteers working with refugee students in Greece. It explores their needs regarding digital technologies in teaching and learning of Modern Greek as a second language. The findings outline the context of technology and Greek refugee language education, the capacity that teachers have, as well as the challenges within this context.

title: Teacher Discourse in Scaffolding a Knowledge Building Group：A Case Study
citation: LEI, C. & Zhang, J. (2022). Teacher discourse in scaffolding a knowledge building group：a case study. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1854-1855). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: LEI, C. & Zhang, J.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
abstract: In a group of one teacher and 30 students engaged in collaborative knowledge building, the teacher’s 165 posts in Knowledge Forum were parsed out for analysis. A coding scheme was developed to categorize the posts into three patterns, namely, managerial, low order, and high order. While managerial and low order discourse seemed inevitable, high order discourse was more pervasive. The posts also suggested a shifting role of the teacher in scaffolding knowledge building over time.

title: Grounded Creativity
citation: Donaldson, J. P. & Woodward, J. (2022). Grounded creativity. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1856-1857). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Donaldson, J. P. & Woodward, J.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: We used complex conceptual systems theory to analyze conceptualizations of creativity in the context of a course in which students engaged in group projects to develop creativity tests and creativity games. Using semantic network analysis, we were able to identify conceptualizations of creativity and emergent practices. Groups which developed games tended to conceptualize creativity as organic, while groups which created tests conceptualized creativity as an object or state. Different practices were emergent from each conceptualization.

title: Uplift Modeling for Educational Data
citation: Zhang, T. (2022). Uplift modeling for educational data. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1860-1861). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Zhang, T.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Traditional learner model focuses on modeling students’ mastery level of a knowledge component based on their historical learning trajectories. Uplift modeling tries to predict the difference between the treatment group and the control group so that the model can predict the actual causal effect of the intervention. We found that the hint effectively increases the learning gain and learners’ prior probability is an important factor affecting the learning gain.

title: The Influence of an Intervention on Students’ Historical Arguing Skills
citation: Hulders, I., Voet, M., & De Wever, B. (2022). The influence of an intervention on students’ historical arguing skills. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1862-1863). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Hulders, I., Voet, M., & Wever, B. D.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Despite the importance of reasoning skills in today's knowledge-based society, students do not appear to possess sufficient arguing skills. This study aimed to examine the improvement of those arguing skills after implementing an intervention in grade 8. In total, 699 students participated, and data was collected using a document-based essay. Results show that students receiving limited and full arguing lessons showed significantly better progression from pre- to post-test compared to students not receiving the intervention. Keywords: historical reasoning skills, arguing, intervention

title: Asking people to “think again” can have unexpected consequences
citation: Bruun, S., Geithner, C., & Kuhn, D. (2022). Meeting people where they are can alter where they are. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1868-1869). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Bruun, S., Geithner, C., & Kuhn, D.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Asking people to “think again” can have unexpected consequences.

title: Implicit and Explicit Emotion Regulation for Conflict Resolution: Narrative and Self-Compassion as Anti-Bullying Training
citation: Park, S. & Tsovaltzi, D. (2022). Implicit and explicit emotion regulation for conflict resolution: Narrative and self-compassion as anti-bullying training. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 187-194). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Park, S. & Tsovaltzi, D.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Bullying poses a risk for equity and justice in learning. It can compromise learning achievement and hinter task performance. Emotions are key to handling bullying, thus need to be understood for the development of anti-bullying technological supports. We investigate effects of combining implicit and explicit emotion regulation strategies on empathy and conflict resolution styles among adolescents in a school bullying context. Based on dual-process framework of emotion regulation (Gyurak et al., 2011), the experimental group engaged in selfcompassion induction as explicit regulation in combination with narrative construction as implicit regulation whereas the control group completed narrative construction only. The combination of implicit and explicit regulation was associated with significant increases in selfcompassion subscales of self-kindness and mindfulness. It also elicited indicators of prosocial conflict resolution style: namely other-inclusion behavior and a tendency to inclusive choice of beneficiary from the bystander perspective. Effects on empathy were not larger with additional explicit support.

title: How Do Learners Use in-Game Learning Support in Digital Game-Based Math Learning?
citation: Dai, C., Ke, F., & Pan, Y. (2022). How do learners use in-game learning support in digital game-based math learning?. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1870-1871). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Dai, C., Ke, F., & Pan, Y.
subject: STEM - Mathematics
abstract: Learners often encounter difficulties in constructing knowledge in digital gamebased learning. In-game learning supports offer in-situ guidance for knowledge-constructive gameplay. Yet, how learners use learning supports are still inconclusive. With a mixed methods study, we investigated learners’ varied usage of different learning support features in digital game-based math learning. Preliminary findings with 22,615 speech utterances of thirty-four students revealed seven clusters of learning support use.

title: The Power of Gestures: Video Club to Support Teacher Awareness of Gestures as a Form of Multimodal Science Instruction
citation: Blue, L. & Pierson, A. (2022). The power of gestures: Video club to support teacher awareness of gestures as a form of multimodal science instruction. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1872-1873). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Blue, L. & Pierson, A.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Teacher candidates attend to many responsibilities and interactions during lesson enactment. Video club (Barnhart & van Es, 2020; Jilk 2016) can narrow reflection to focus on specific aspects of teaching. This study explores the power of video club to develop awareness of multimodal resources, such as gestures. We analyze data from a science methods course, finding that video club makes visible teachers candidates’ subconscious gestures and can position gestures as resources for inclusive science teaching.

title: Emotion Objects: An Embodiment of Learning Socioscientific Issues With Heart
citation: Leung, J. S. & Cheng, M. M. (2022). Emotion objects: An embodiment of learning socioscientific issues with heart. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1880-1881). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Leung, J. S. C. & Cheng, M. M. W.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This multiple-case study examined students’ patterns of emotion objects and their learning of obesity as a socioscientific issue. We tracked the emotion objects of four university students over a 12-week general education course on obesity. We found that students with different depth of learning had distinguishable sets of referents of emotions. This paper points out the need to attend to and specify emotion objects as a key variable in future research regarding emotions.

citation: Beier, J. P. & Rau, M. A. (2022). The role of visual representations in impasses during collaborative problem solving in undergraduate chemistry. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y.
