title: Brazilian Educators’ Perceptions of STEAM Education
citation: Lopes, R., Ficheman, I., Souza, E., & Maia, D. (2022). Brazilian educators’ perceptions of STEAM education. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1890-1891). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Lopes, R., Ficheman, I., Souza, E., & Maia, D.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
abstract: This paper investigates the perceptions of Brazilian educators of STEAM education. The analysis was based on an online survey of participants of the STEAM TechCamp Brasil program. We analyzed two open questions using the Discursive Textual Analysis method. Results indicate that participants perceive STEAM as a pedagogical approach, but have a restricted view of the sciences. This discussion contributes to the current understanding of STEAM in Brazil and to the evolution towards a self-contained conception.

title: A Growing Problem: Student-Worker Retention at an Urban Farm
citation: Sager, M. T., Binford, L., & Petrosino, A. J. (2022). A growing problem: Student-worker retention at an urban farm. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1892-1893). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Sager, M. T., Binford, L., & Petrosino, A. J.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: We investigate student-workers’ motivation at an urban farm situated on a Historically Black College’s campus. This is one phase of research embedded within the beginning stages of a larger research practitioner partnership (RPP). This paper aims to address: How do student-workers stay motivated to continue their work placements at an HBCU’s urban farm in the Southwest US? The basis of our analyses are interviews, observation field notes, and artifacts collected over the course of this research. We examined the data to identify recurring themes which led to student-worker turnover and discuss opportunities for improvement of student-workers’ learning motivation. As a whole, we seek to support key partners, as the ICLS 2022 calls for, by investigating innovative learning environments.

title: Growing Student-Workers as Informal Learners
citation: Sager, M. T., Binford, L., & Petrosino, A. J. (2022). Growing student-workers as informal learners. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1894-1895). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Sager, M. T., Binford, L., & Petrosino, A. J.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: We investigate an urban farm as an informal learning setting and the interactions between experts and novices using situated cognition as our framework. The poster is situated within a large research practitioner partnership (RPP). Initial findings are reported as they relate to learning in a novel environment, and that it relates to the 2022 ICLS theme of “elucidating theories and processes of learning and teaching.”

title: Biology Isn’t Black and White: Deconstructing Biology Instructors’ Knowledge Networks of Biological Processes to Explore Nuance
citation: Flowers, S. & Gardner, S. M. (2022). Biology isn’t black and white: Deconstructing biology instructors’ knowledge networks of biological processes to explore nuance. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1896-1897). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Flowers, S. & Gardner, S. M.
subject: STEM - Natural Science
abstract: To fully appreciate the intricacies of biology, undergraduate students must understand how the components and processes of complex biological systems relate to each other over space and time. However, building normative knowledge networks and transferring across biological contexts is a challenge. In this study, we sought to identify the features of a model describing the relationships between three fundamental processes in biology: cell-cell communication, gene regulation, and phenotypic expression. Through interviews with six biology instructors, we found a diversity of knowledge networks relating the processes. Further investigation revealed that their knowledge networks are influenced by their definitions of phenotype, their biological disciplines, and accumulated professional experiences. Our data reinforce the idea of situated cognition and suggest that a single, acontextual knowledge network is difficult to transfer across biological contexts. We suggest educators invite students to critique models and to engage in explicit instruction about how and when to use them.

title: Science Teachers’ Ideological Shifts About Multilingual Learners
citation: Daniel, B., Pierson, A., Keifert, D., Lee, S., & Askew, R. (2022). Science teachers’ ideological shifts about multilingual learners. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1902-1903). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Daniel, B., Pierson, A., Keifert, D., Lee, S., & Askew, R.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Drawing on theories of ideologies in interaction, this poster considers the extent to which professional development supported elementary teachers’ rearticulations of monolingual ideologies toward expansive views of young multilingual learners’ capabilities in science.

title: Visualizing Family Engagement in Museum Settings
citation: Han, A., Keune, A., Huang, J., & Peppler, K. (2022). Visualizing family engagement in museum settings. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1904-1905). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Han, A., Keune, A., Huang, J., & Peppler, K.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: The purpose of the study is to explore the affordances and limitations of information visualization for analyzing video data of small family groups in museum settings. In this paper, we analyze visitor engagement by visualizing space, time, and group interactions. Using observational video data from a museum exhibit, we designed three visualization techniques: transcript variations, floor plan diagrams, and infographic charts. Using variations of these techniques, we examine each approach’s affordances and limitations.

title: Co-Design of AI-enhanced Learning Analytics: Considerations for Ensuring Diversity, Equity, Justice
citation: Celik, I. & Muukkonen, H. (2022). Co-design of AI-enhanced learning analytics: Considerations for ensuring diversity, equity, justice. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1906-1907). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Celik, I. & Muukkonen, H.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
abstract: The majority of the participatory/co-design research has somehow ignored the considerations tackling the diversity, equity, and justice challenges in the design process of learning analytics. We suggest four considerations: (1) while determining the needs and expectations of targeted learners, consider all subgroups of populations (2) determine the transparent and inclusive algorithm for meeting the needs (3) consider diversity and equity for model training data (4) consider heterogeneous participants while testing prototypes of learning analytics.

title: Towards a Theory of Dialogic Play for Learning
citation: Gaydos, M. & Nardo, A. (2022). Towards a theory of dialogic play for learning. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1908-1909). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Gaydos, M. & Nardo, A.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: In this paper, we argue that differentiating dialectic from dialogic play can illuminate important differences between current approaches to game-based learning and can suggest new directions for the field of game-based learning. Expanding on Vygotsky’s work on imaginary play, we work towards a theory of dialogic play with particular focus on the role of vulnerability in learning and propose it as an alternative to prior approaches that emphasize content learning or tool-mastery. Because it encourages curriculum that supports new ways of relating to difference and otherness, we believe that dialogic play is important to consider in play-based learning, as it more closely aligns with sociocultural approaches that address issues of power and may be useful in the design of related curriculum.

title: To Wait or Not to Wait: Adding to the Debate on Immediate Versus Delayed Feedback
citation: Smith, H., Ngo, V., Sales, A., Closser, A. H., Chan, J. Y., & Ottmar, E. (2022). To wait or not to wait: Adding to the debate on immediate versus delayed feedback. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1910-1911). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Smith, H., Ngo, V., Sales, A., Closser, A. H., Chan, J. Y., & Ottmar, E.
subject: STEM - Mathematics
abstract: Prior work investigates the impact of feedback timing on math performance; however, when feedback is most effective remains unclear. We define immediate and delayed feedback and examine how timing affects student algebra performance. 1,629 students were randomly assigned to an immediate or delayed feedback condition, completed a two-hour intervention solving math problems in an online tutoring system, and received immediate or delayed feedback. We found overall learning gains, but no differences between the conditions.

title: Using Organizational Change Theories to Examine Women-in-Computing Groups
citation: Wu, J. & Uttal, D. (2022). Using organizational change theories to examine women-in-computing groups. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1912-1913). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Wu, J. & Uttal, D.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; STEM - Mathematics; STEM - Engineering & Robotics
tpack_ck_labels: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; STEM - Mathematics; STEM - Engineering & Robotics
abstract: The gender imbalance in computer science is getting worse, with computer science being the only Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) field in which women’s representation has steadily declined throughout the past few decades. This study focuses on one attempt to redress the lack of women in computer science—Women-inComputing (WiC) college clubs. Drawing on organizational change theories, we ask: How do students engage in WiC? Do WiC clubs engender changes? If so, how? We argue that WiC is an identity, a community, a safe space, and the beginning of a career-long practice of mentoring future women in computer science. Moreover, changes driven by such clubs have brought impacts to both the individual level students and the organizational level computer science departments. This study offers a new perspective on applying organizational change theories and contributes to the broader research community on diversity, equity, and inclusion in higher education.

title: Validating a Code-Free Computational Thinking Assessment for Elementary School Students: Preliminary Results
citation: Rachmatullah, A., Tate, C., Beesley, A., & Levin-Guracar, E. (2022). Validating a code-free computational thinking assessment for elementary school students: Preliminary results. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1914-1915). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Rachmatullah, A., Tate, C., Beesley, A., & Levin-Guracar, E.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
abstract: Computational thinking (CT) assessments are increasingly available, but it is still challenging to measure the impact of CT interventions. Assessments employing the same coding context as the intervention confer an advantage to treatment students, and possibly also to comparison group students with prior coding experience. Here we report initial findings of our effort to validate a CT assessment without a coding context and to account for prior coding experience in the validation process.

title: Learning Natural Selection Through Computational Models in a High School A.P. Biology Classroom
citation: Davey, B., Peel, A., Horn, M., & Wilensky, U. (2022). Learning natural selection through computational models in a high school A.P. biology classroom. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1916-1917). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Davey, B., Peel, A., Horn, M., & Wilensky, U.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; STEM - Natural Science
tpack_ck_labels: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; STEM - Natural Science
abstract: Science education communities understand the importance of computational thinking but lack empirically tested learning materials. We report the implementation of a computationally driven natural selection unit in an A.P. high school biology classroom. Epistemic network analyses of student responses indicate that computational tools can facilitate learning of natural selection, and to varying degrees. We interpret these results to show that attention should be given to the fit between computational tools and natural selection concepts.

title: Game Design Experience for Teachers’ Design Thinking in Participatory Design Culture
citation: Pan, Y., Ke, F., & Dai, C. (2022). Game design experience for teachers’ design thinking in participatory design culture. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1922-1923). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Pan, Y., Ke, F., & Dai, C.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This case study explored how the experience of game design in the culture of participatory design contributed to teachers’ design thinking. Three in-service middle school teachers were invited to be game design partners in an 8-hour workshop, aiming to enhance the reliability and validity of an architecture-based game. Data were collected from in-field observation, screen recording videos, and semi-structured interview debriefing. Three salient themes were extracted to explore teachers’ game design experience in relation to their development of design thinking.

title: The Practices of Documenting in Research-Practice Partnership
citation: Rubin, E. B., Sandoval, C., & Conlin, D. M. (2022). The practices of documenting in research-practice partnership. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1924-1925). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Rubin, E. B., Sandoval, C., & Conlin, D. M.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Documenting is critical for shaping and codifying processes in research-practice partnerships (RPPs). Prior work highlights a need for further theorizing of how documenting can support or undermine equitable partnership work. Drawing on practice theory, we examine how RPP documenting practices relate to participation and outcomes. Findings indicate a continuum spanning two affordance-constraint dyads: durable/static versus dynamic/ephemeral. This continuum illustrates how documenting surfaces and addresses tensions, which can inform decisions in RPPs regarding practices of documenting.

title: Embodied Learning in Classrooms: Machine-Learning-Enhanced Computer Vision for Geometry Math Game
citation: Na, H. (2022). Embodied learning in classrooms: Machine-learning-enhanced computer vision for geometry math game. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1926-1927). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Na, H.
subject: STEM - Mathematics
abstract: Embodied learning has been considered as an effective way of teaching and learning, having pedagogical potentials. Motion-tracking devices have been frequently used in research; however, it was difficult to apply them in classrooms. To bring embodied learning interventions into K-12 classroom settings, this research used machine learning enhanced computer vision techniques. Three hand gestures that are expected to be mathematically relevant were designed and implemented in a geometry math game through the techniques.

title: Pre-Service Teachers’ Growth in Epistemic Cognition Through Learning Pedagogical Knowledge
citation: Kawasaki, M., Oshima, J., & Oshima, R. (2022). Pre-service teachers’ growth in epistemic cognition through learning pedagogical knowledge. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1930-1931). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Kawasaki, M., Oshima, J., & Oshima, R.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This study examined pre-service teachers’ growth in epistemic cognition by learning pedagogical knowledge. We evaluated whether pre-service teachers could describe a classroom practice’s aim, processes, and ideals coherently by referring to the pedagogical knowledge they had learned in a course on learning theories. The results suggested that they did not necessarily recognize that aims, processes, and ideals should be coherent as components of the lesson.

title: A Study of the Development of Evaluation Methods for Dialogical Reports in PBL Classes
citation: Makino, M., Shoji, G., & Ozawa, S. (2022). A study of the development of evaluation methods for dialogical reports in PBL classes. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1932-1933). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Makino, M., Shoji, G., & Ozawa, S.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This study developed methods of evaluating students’ outcomes in remotely conducted project-based learning. “Dialogical reports” which used a hypothetical interview were introduced to encourage reflection on learning outcomes from others’ perspectives. As a result of qualitatively analyzing the questions of dialogical reports, it was found that dialogical reports have the potential to encourage reflection on courses from the perspectives of others.

title: Scaffolding Math Learning and Motivation by Integrating Casual Play in Computer-Based Practice for Fifth Graders
citation: Shay, L. & Langbeheim, E. (2022). Scaffolding math learning and motivation by integrating casual play in computer-based practice for fifth graders. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1934-1935). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Shay, L. & Langbeheim, E.
subject: STEM - Mathematics
abstract: The difficulties experienced by many students in mathematics are characterized by anxiety and lack of motivation to learn. Intrinsic and even extrinsic integration of play, can influence students' attitudes and increase their motivation to learn. The purpose of this study was to examine the effect of external integration of play as a break between exercises in a computer-based tutorial on the topic of fractions. We hypothesized that compared to non-gamebased learning, students’ perseverance in solving math exercises would increase, which is reflected in performing more questions while investing sufficient time in solving the problems. Our pilot study compares the number practice questions solved between two groups of 5th graders: 30 students in the play condition, and 33 in the control condition. The results show that there is no significant difference in the number of questions answered in each condition, but that integrating play moderates the differences between motivated and less motivated students.

title: Online Pre-Service Teacher Learning Communities as a Tool for Teacher Education
citation: Skoulia, T. & Louca, L. T. (2022). Online pre-service teacher learning communities as a tool for teacher education. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1936-1937). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Skoulia, T. & Louca, L. T.
subject: STEM - Natural Science
abstract: The purpose of this descriptive case study was to better understand the characteristics of Teacher Professional Learning Communities(TPLCs) of pre-service teachers(PsTs). Data were derived from 2 TPLCs in which 15 PsTs volunteered to participate, within the context of a pre-school Science Education course they were enrolled in. We analyzed transcripts of videotaped TPLC meetings following the thematic analysis approach. Our findings provide insights about how this group of PsTs utilized opportunities for professional growth.

title: Leveraging Student-Written Chapter Summaries to Assess Understanding and Motivation in an Introductory Statistics Course
citation: Yang, S., Sung, G., C., M. T., & Schneider, B. (2022). Leveraging student-written chapter summaries to assess understanding and motivation in an introductory statistics course. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1940-1941). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Yang, S., Sung, G., C, M. T., & Schneider, B.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Instructors often assign students to write summaries of what they have learned. Beyond being a helpful learning exercise, written summaries can reveal latent models of what students do and don’t understand about the instructional content. Drawing on data from an introductory statistics course, the current study assessed the relationship between written summaries and student understanding and motivation in the course. Findings revealed significant associations which can inform support for struggling learners.

title: Student Profiling on Behavioral Patterns in an Online Mathematics Game: Clustering Using K-Means
citation: Norum, R., Lee, J., & Ottmar, E. (2022). Student profiling on behavioral patterns in an online mathematics game: Clustering using k-means. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1942-1943). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Norum, R., Lee, J., & Ottmar, E.
subject: STEM - Mathematics
abstract: This preliminary study examined whether distinct student profiles (N = 760) emerged based on their behavioral patterns in an online algebraic learning game. We applied k-means clustering analysis to clickstream data collected in the game and then examined how students’ behavioral patterns varied across the clusters using data visualization. The results identified four groups of students based on their in-game behaviors, showing that there was a large variation in their behavioral patterns for engaging with the game.

title: Designing for Connected Arts Learning Through Culturally Sustaining Practices
citation: Dahn, M., Cawelti, L., Schindler, E., & Peppler, K. (2022). Designing for connected arts learning through culturally sustaining practices. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1946-1947). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Dahn, M., Cawelti, L., Schindler, E., & Peppler, K.
subject: Social & Civic Studies
abstract: Community-based arts organizations curate and build experiences rooted in local culture through culturally sustaining practices. Through analysis of interviews with leaders at community-based arts organizations, we found that each took a different route to supporting culturally sustaining arts practices, which enacted relational elements of connected learning environments. We describe three models of culturally sustaining arts approaches (i.e., heritage and history, intergenerational, and youth culture) and suggest that each supports relational elements of connected learning.

title: What if the Computer Crashes? Findings From an Exploratory Factor Analysis on Stressors in Online Exams
citation: Jeitziner, L. T., Roos, A., Ruf, A., & Zahn, C. (2022). What if the computer crashes? Findings from an exploratory factor analysis on stressors in online exams. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1948-1949). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Jeitziner, L. T., Roos, A., Ruf, A., & Zahn, C.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: The pandemic has forced higher education to shift from onsite to online environments. This novel situation may increase students’ exam stress and induce new stressors. In the present study, we identified stressors in online exams by conducting an exploratory factor analysis of a novel questionnaire. The analysis revealed five factors that categorize students’ experience of stress. Preliminary descriptive results suggest that possible system failures and social pressures cause the highest stress for students.

title: Navigating the Conceptual and Critical Demands of Data Literacy in High School Spaces Using Firsthand Data
citation: Noushad, N. F., Shim, J., & Yoon, S. A. (2022). Navigating the conceptual and critical demands of data literacy in high school spaces using firsthand data. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 195-202). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Noushad, N. F., Shim, J., & Yoon, S. A.
subject: Humanities, Language & Literacy
abstract: Curriculum efforts to promote data literacy continue to evolve in K-12 spaces to meet the larger need of developing data-informed citizens. The learning objectives of these efforts tend to shift from conceptual data literacy objectives such as demonstration of adequate statistical reasoning to critical data literacy objectives such as empowering students to design, collect and analyze data to serve their needs. However, most studies do not delineate between these objectives, often giving an incomplete picture of student understanding of data, and the effectiveness of the curriculum in meeting these two data literacy objectives. In this paper, we study the outcomes that emerged from a curriculum unit designed to empower students to collect, analyze and present data from their neighborhood. We specifically evaluate the conceptual and critical data objectives of 14 high school students. Our findings indicate that students struggled to demonstrate equal competence in conceptual and critical data literacy goals.

title: Development and Formative Evaluation of a Learning Game for Overcoming Typical Difficulties in Historical Thinking
citation: Ikejiri, R. (2022). Development and formative evaluation of a learning game for overcoming typical difficulties in historical thinking. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1952-1953). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Ikejiri, R.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Research has been conducted on teaching materials for historical thinking using historical sources. However, historical thinking encounters challenges in the use of historical sources, and short-term interventions have limited effectiveness. This study developed a learning game by combining the ideas of a studying-errors guideline and game-based learning to overcome typical difficulties in historical thinking using historical sources. The formative evaluation showed that the learning game affected challenging historical thinking using historical sources.

title: Demonstrating Core Components of a Game-Based Fraction Supplemental Curriculum
citation: Hunt, J. H., Taub, M., Marino, M., Duarte, A., Bentley, B., & Holman, K. (2022). Demonstrating core components of a game-based fraction supplemental curriculum. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1958-1959). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Hunt, J. H., Taub, M., Marino, M., Duarte, A., Bentley, B., & Holman, K.
subject: STEM - Mathematics
abstract: Simulated learning environments, such as serious games, have the potential to significantly advance engagement and conceptual understanding for all students. The need to bolster engagement and conceptual understanding is pronounced for students with learning disabilities and difficulties. Dream2B includes a web-based video game designed with the Universal Design for Learning framework to maximize access, advancement, and power for fourth through sixth grade students in supplemental mathematics instructional settings. A demonstration of the game-based curriculum’s design and development are shared.

title: Machine Learning and Student Reasoning Patterns in NGSS Assessments
citation: Liu, L., Cisterna, D., Qi, Y., Kinsey, D., Chen, X., & Riordan, B. (2022). Machine learning and student reasoning patterns in NGSS assessments. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1960-1961). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Liu, L., Cisterna, D., Qi, Y., Kinsey, D., Chen, X., & Riordan, B.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: SPIN-NGSS (Student Reasoning Patterns in NGSS Assessments), an NSF funded project, responds to the national need to document various student reasoning patterns in threedimensional (3D) science assessments and tied machine learning techniques to automated diagnosis and feedback to support science learning. This presentation describes a framework of student reasoning patterns illustrated by example student responses, the development and evaluation of machine learning methods, and an exploratory study on how students reacts to the automated system.

title: What Do Teachers Learn About Assessment via Co-Design of Game Dashboard
citation: Kim, Y. J. & Scianna, J. (2022). What do teachers learn about assessment via co-design of game dashboard. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1962-1963). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Kim, Y. J. & Scianna, J.
subject: Humanities, Language & Literacy
conceptualisations_list: Co-Design & Participatory Design; Constructionism & Maker-Centered Learning
abstract: Increased use of educational technologies, such as games and simulations, requires classroom teachers develop new assessment literacies and practices related to understanding data affordances of playful learning environments. In this paper, we discuss how a co-design process that involves teachers to develop dashboards for an educational game can serve as a constructionist model of teacher professional development and report two ways the co-design process shifted teachers’ understanding of assessment.

title: Examining the Development of Perspective-Taking Through Social Annotations in Collaborative Text Study
citation: Cohen, S. G. (2022). Examining the development of perspective-taking through social annotations in collaborative text study. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1970-1971). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Cohen, S. G.
subject: Humanities, Language & Literacy
abstract: Reading literature has been found to be positively related to perspective-taking. We studied perspective-taking through the use of social annotations of texts and asked how perspective-taking develops during collaborative text study, and which elements of social annotation support perspective-taking development? Specifically, we studied an undergraduate education philosophy course in order to gain insights about perspective-taking in online spaces, using a social annotation tool.

tpack_tk_labels: Immersive VR / AR; Simulations & Scientific Modeling
abstract: This article describes the development of a chatbot designed to simulate students in a 3D virtual environment for the purpose of pre-service teacher training. Using a generative pretrained transformer-based deep neural network model, researchers created an artificially intelligent chatbot using language resource data from authentic classroom dialogues. Results indicate that the chatbot needs to be fine-tuned with additional programming. This program is intended to be used in future research on teacher-training in virtual simulations.

title: Design of an Argumentation-Based Learning Activity: Connecting Veterinary Students to Real-World Problems
citation: Zhao, Y., Kao, S., Donaldson, J. P., & Chaney, K. P. (2022). Design of an argumentation-based learning activity: Connecting veterinary students to real-world problems. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1976-1977). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Zhao, Y., Kao, S., Donaldson, J. P., & Chaney, K. P.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
conceptualisations_list: Scaffolding & Guided Inquiry; Accountable Talk & Dialogic Discourse
abstract: The study investigated the design of an argumentation-based activity that focused on animal welfare and advocacy in a first-year veterinary class. The objective was to understand students’ learning experience and to provide evidence-based insights for future improvement. The reflections of eighty students were analyzed using semantic network analysis. We found that allowing for topic selection, providing background resources, and scaffolded evaluation of biases and evidence may be important design considerations.

title: Analyzing Teacher Learning in a Research Practice Partnership
citation: Akgul, E. S. & Superfine, A. C. (2022). Analyzing teacher learning in a research practice partnership. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1978-1979). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Akgul, E. S. & Superfine, A. C.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Teachers are increasingly participating in RPPs with the goal of improving their schools and districts. This context provides teachers with unique learning opportunities as they directly take part in school improvement work, yet we know little about what teachers learn from their involvement in RPPs. This study explores teacher learning over the course of the first year of a multiyear RPP with a team of researchers from a local university.

title: Tensions in Supporting Equity During Sense-Making Activities in Mathematics
citation: Zhan, W. & Louie, N. L. (2022). Tensions in supporting equity during sense-making activities in mathematics. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1980-1981). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Zhan, W. & Louie, N. L.
subject: STEM - Mathematics
abstract: This paper demonstrates how pedagogical practices that are deemed to be equitable may lead to both inclusion and exclusion effects. We present an illustrative vignette of a mathematics lesson. The teacher demonstrated practices that are consistent with what has been suggested in discourse around epistemic agency as equity. However, the interaction manifested the assumptions of what count as sense-making in mathematics that have historically functioned to differentiate kinds of students.

title: Directed Actions Scaffold Gestural Insights in Geometric Reasoning
citation: Xia, F., Schenck, K. E., Swart, M. I., & Nathan, M. J. (2022). Directed actions scaffold gestural insights in geometric reasoning. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1982-1983). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Xia, F., Schenck, K. E., Swart, M. I., & Nathan, M. J.
subject: STEM - Mathematics
abstract: Spontaneous gestures often express thoughts that differ from speech. Priming students to perform directed actions, movements designed to foster conceptual understanding, may give a way for students to organize their thoughts by providing a gestural vocabulary. Gestural insights are nonverbal expressions of movement that reveal students’ mathematical reasoning even when they were unable to verbalize their insights. This case study demonstrates how body-based resources like directed actions can foster gestural insights that support conceptual thinking.

title: Effects of Level Trajectory on Mathematical Gameplay
citation: West, L., Ke, F., Dai, C., Kim, B. J., Chaulagain, R., Mondol, T. C., Xu, J., Kuba, R., & Jung, S. (2022). Effects of level trajectory on mathematical gameplay. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1986-1987). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: West, L., Ke, F., Dai, C., Kim, B. J., Chaulagain, R., Mondol, T. C., Xu, J., Kuba, R., & Jung, S.
subject: STEM - Mathematics
abstract: We investigate the effect of free-choice versus adaptively recommended level trajectories on gameplay for middle-school learners playing a 3D architectural game involving ratio and geometric reasoning. We compare data between groups examining students’ game performance and level selection patterns to examine the potential impact of level trajectories on a learner’s gameplay performance and process. Using data from an online-facilitated study (n=23) we find that students playing with an adaptively recommended level trajectory spend more of their time on the target math-related levels. We confirm this with data from an onsitefacilitated study (n=51) and propose that adaptive level recommendation guides learners toward game levels relevant to target learning objectives while allowing some freedom of choice.

title: Dynamic Modelling of Collaborative Sensemaking: A Case Study
citation: Abes, A., Ami, H. B., & Kapon, S. (2022). Dynamic modelling of collaborative sensemaking: A case study. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1988-1989). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Abes, A., Ami, H. B., & Kapon, S.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: How do explanations emerge and evolve in collaborative sensemaking? We present a preliminary attempt to model the evolution of collaborative sensemaking over a short timespan with high temporal resolution. We operationalized Sherin et al.’s (2012) node-mode framework of individual knowledge systems to a distributed knowledge system and examined its dynamics in high temporal resolution.

title: Preparation for Future Learning and Disposition Development in a Social Studies-Themed Digital Simulation Game: A Quantitative Ethnography
citation: Kessner, T. (2022). Preparation for future learning and disposition development in a social studies-themed digital simulation game: A quantitative ethnography. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1990-1991). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Kessner, T.
subject: STEM - Engineering & Robotics; Social & Civic Studies
tpack_ck_labels: STEM - Engineering & Robotics; Social & Civic Studies
abstract: We use quantitative ethnography and Epistemic Network Analysis to examine how the game mechanics of a social studies-themed digital simulation game may facilitate disposition development and preparation for future learning.

title: Using Interest and Identity to Design for Mentor Persistence
citation: Ramey, K., Berger, W., Thompson, N., & Pinkard, N. (2022). Using interest and identity to design for mentor persistence. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1996-1997). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Ramey, K., Berger, W., Thompson, N., & Pinkard, N.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Mentorship is identified as a successful approach to supporting youth in out-ofschool learning. However, less attention has been paid to how to develop and support a mentor workforce. This study examines how to design supportive infrastructure that encourages mentors to persist in mentoring by providing opportunities for interest and collaborative identity development. Drawing on two case studies constructed from interview and interaction data, we demonstrate how these processes unfolded in a summer mentoring practicum.

title: Elementary Students’ Epistemic Ideas Within Design-Based Learning Projects
citation: Jin, Q. & Ke, L. (2022). Elementary students’ epistemic ideas within design-based learning projects. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1998-1999). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Jin, Q. & Ke, L.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Students’ epistemic ideas influence how they engage in science practices. This study employed the Epistemologies in Practice (EIP) framework to explore elementary students’ epistemic ideas within design-based projects in a science classroom. Data were collected from multiple sources and analyzed qualitatively. Findings indicated that students meaningfully used their epistemic considerations while engaging in their design projects. It was also found that contextual factors such as task settings influenced how students prioritized their epistemic ideas.

title: Processing Team Feedback: Exploring Emotional and Cognitive Responses to Team-Level Feedback
citation: Gabelica, C. & Popov, V. (2022). Processing team feedback: Exploring emotional and cognitive responses to team-level feedback. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2004-2005). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Gabelica, C. & Popov, V.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Research on feedback in teams acknowledges the importance of feedback mechanisms to team success. However, although processing performance feedback in teams is seen as an important prerequisite to its effectiveness, the processes emerging after feedback reception have been overlooked in past research. This paper provides insights into the emotional and cognitive reflective responses of graduate students (N=111) to team-level feedback. The results of our explorative study reveal that (a) students from high-performing teams generally report positive activating emotions and generally reflect on feedback when prompted to do so, (b) many students from low performing teams were able to show adaptive emotional responses to team-level feedback, and (c) there is a complex interplay between feedback valence and affective and cognitive reactions to team feedback as evidenced and visualized by Epistemic Network Analysis model.

title: Student-Created Math Walks in Informal Learning Spaces
citation: Walkington, C., Milton, S., Petrosino, A. J., Sager, M. T., & Dhingra, K. (2022). Student-created math walks in informal learning spaces. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2006-2007). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Walkington, C., Milton, S., Petrosino, A. J., Sager, M. T., & Dhingra, K.
subject: STEM - Mathematics
abstract: Math walks are a form of inquiry learning where students can observe and create mathematical meaning from their everyday surroundings. Here we report on a study of 5th and 6th graders in an informal learning setting where they create and present their own math walks covering concepts of ratio, scale, and proportion. The students may have developed more positive attitudes towards math and were able to meaningfully engage with powerful math ideas.

title: Managing Deference, Leadership, Vision, and Voice: Dilemmas From Antiracist School-University Partnerships
citation: Louie, N. L. & Berland, L. (2022). Managing deference, leadership, vision, and voice: Dilemmas from antiracist school-university partnerships. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. abstract: None

title: AI Voice Tutor Usability Study: Understanding Impact on Math Self-Efficacy and Metacognition Among Middle Schoolers
citation: Ko, E. G., , Atarod, R., Nguyen, K., & Lee, M. K. (2022). AI voice tutor usability study: Understanding impact on math self-efficacy and metacognition among middle schoolers. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2012-2013). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Ko, E. G., Marconette, Atarod, R., Nguyen, K., & Lee, M. K.
subject: STEM - Mathematics
abstract: We present CAI, a voice-based intelligent tutor that helps middle schoolers learn prealgebra concepts. Users interact with CAI by solving math problems presented by the AI-tutor, each with a varied mode of narration and type of feedback. We describe the design, methods, and findings from our testing with middle schoolers. We provide insight into how voice-based intelligent tutors can impact motivation and metacognition, yet also require personalization and complementary video-based instruction to improve their performance.

title: Learning in Your Own Direction: Examining Relationships Between Non-Sequential User Choice and Learning
citation: Valentine, E. P. (2022). Learning in your own direction: Examining relationships between non-sequential user choice and learning. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2014-2015). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Valentine, E. P.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This study sought to address an aspect of learner control known as non-sequential user choice. Leveraging open driver education resources, this research explored how learners’ chosen learning sequences and the time they spend with each learning resource relate to performance on an assessment of learning. The study examined learning outcomes for subjects with free choice over learning sequence based on time spent and chosen sequence. Analyses yielded a significant regression model and raise the possibility that time spent and chosen order may be able to predict performance.

title: Makerland: Mathematics in Makerspace Resources to Enhance Maker-Based Learning
citation: Pimentel, C. S. (2022). Makerland: Mathematics in makerspace resources to enhance maker-based learning. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2016-2017). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Pimentel, C. S.
subject: STEM - Mathematics
abstract: This work investigates the Math concepts that are applied when using the resources of a Makerspace. The research highlights Math concepts that are usually employed throughout the modeling, prototyping and production processes. An exploratory study was conducted on a Brazilian high school, and the results indicate that students can identify the Math concepts and that the systematization of these subjects can be used as a learning object.

title: Viviendo Aquí: Designing for Transformative Agency Through Museum Exhibit Curation With Latinx Youth
citation: Stamatis, K., Polman, J. L., Manriquez-Hernandez, J., & Zinn, E. (2022). Viviendo aquí: Designing for transformative agency through museum exhibit curation with latinx youth. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2018-2019). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Stamatis, K., Polman, J. L., Manriquez-Hernandez, J., & Zinn, E.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This paper showcases preliminary research on the process of curating a museum exhibit with Latinx youth. During the 2020-2021 school year, a group of Latinx teenagers developed an exhibit with a local museum. They reported feeling excited to see themselves and their stories represented in their mostly white community. This paper explores preliminary analysis of their engagement with the museum project and the potential community curation holds for disrupting whiteness perpetuated in public spaces.

title: Training a Text Classification Algorithm to Predict the Presence of Dispositions and Learning Shifts in Students’ Self-Reflection
citation: Forshaw, T., Carroll, M., & Carter, C. (2022). Training a text classification algorithm to predict the presence of dispositions and learning shifts in students’ self-reflection. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2020-2021). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Forshaw, T., Carroll, M., & Carter, C.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; Humanities, Language & Literacy
tpack_ck_labels: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; Humanities, Language & Literacy
abstract: The body of literature on how to best leverage learning analytics to measure students’ acquisition of 21st-century dispositional skills is in emergent stages. This project, based on over 800 student self-reflections, leverages natural language processing and qualitative data analysis to attempt to train a text classification algorithm to predict the presence of dispositions and learning shifts in students’ self- reflection.

title: Inquiry of (Re)configurings: Toward a Review of Posthumanist Methods for the Study of Learning
citation: Keune, A. & Ruiz-Cabello, P. (2022). Inquiry of (re)configurings: Toward a review of posthumanist methods for the study of learning. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2022-2023). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Keune, A. & Ruiz-Cabello, P.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Educational researchers are increasingly adopting posthumanist approaches, questioning methodological assumptions toward the study of learning. Yet, it remains under documented how researchers align methodological doing to this aim. The present poster presents two studies that employed posthumanist perspectives and how they led to think methodologically with theory. The paper points to the need for a systematic review of posthumanist methodological approaches and decisions for the study of learning.

title: Accessible Computational Thinking in Elementary Science
citation: Bernier, J., Figueroa, F., Ha, J., Mak, J., Su, M., Yan, L., Nelson, B., Cabrera, L., Kramarczuk, K., Xin, Y., Ketelhut, D. J., & Shockley, E. T. (2022). Accessible computational thinking in elementary science. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2024-2025). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Bernier, J., Figueroa, F., Ha, J., Mak, J., Su, M., Yan, L., Nelson, B., Cabrera, L., Kramarczuk, K., Xin, Y., Ketelhut, D. J., & Shockley, E. T.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; STEM - Natural Science
tpack_ck_labels: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; STEM - Natural Science
abstract: Computational thinking (CT) is ubiquitous in modern science, yet rarely integrated at the elementary school level. Moreover, access to computer science education at the PK-12 level is inequitably distributed. We believe that access to CT must be available earlier and implemented with the support of an equitable pedagogical framework. Our poster will describe our Accessible Computational Thinking (ACT) research project exploring professional development with elementary teachers on integrating computational thinking with Culturally Responsive Teaching practices.

title: Local-Global Maker-Places: Toward an Instrument for International Maker Education
citation: Keune, A., Cain, R., Dahn, M., Kargin, T., & Thompson, N. (2022). Local-global maker-places: Toward an instrument for international maker education. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2026-2027). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Keune, A., Cain, R., Dahn, M., Kargin, T., & Thompson, N.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: After the establishment of a makerspace in any context, sustainability is becoming increasingly important. As an international group of early career scholars with experience in maker education, we engaged in a series of reflective conversations that called us to consider visions for makerspaces as sustainable maker-places. We offer a representation that cuts across visions for sustainable maker-places with the intention to begin to develop an instrument for international maker-education.

title: Exploring Elementary School Students’ Clusters in Blended Mathematics Learning
citation: Lee, S., Cho, Y. H., Han, Y., Han, S., & Lee, S. (2022). Exploring elementary school students’ clusters in blended mathematics learning. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2028-2029). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Lee, S., Cho, Y. H., Han, Y., Han, S., & Lee, S.
subject: STEM - Mathematics
abstract: Blended learning is effective in enhancing meaningful learning in online and faceto-face learning environments. For adaptive learning supports, teachers should understand the diversity of students and identify student clusters with different educational needs in blended learning. This study explored the clusters of Korean students in a mathematics class, collecting blended learning data for one month. This study found three clusters: (1) students with the need for integrated support, (2) students with positive affective characteristics and high-level, selfregulated learning skills, and (3) students with high-level academic achievements and online learning participation. Thus, this study determined unique characteristics of Korean students that were typically overlooked by teachers.

title: “With You I’ll Be Able to Actually Learn Everything”: Exploring Learner Experiences With a ‘Study With Me’ Video
citation: Ibtasar, R., Heineke, C. M., & Michaelis, J. E. (2022). “With you I’ll be able to actually learn everything”: Exploring learner experiences with a ‘study with me’ video. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 203-210). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Ibtasar, R., Heineke, C. M., & Michaelis, J. E.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Study With Me (SWM) videos are recordings of individuals silently studying for hours with minimal interaction with the viewers. Despite the lack of any instructional and conversational elements, these unique virtual spaces continue to attract millions of viewers. In this paper, we conducted a Thematic Analysis on the comments generated by viewers for one popular SWM video to understand why viewers engaged with the video and what benefits they may be getting from their engagement. Our analysis revealed four themes: (1) the SWM video provided social support for studying, (2) the SWM video created an idealized structured study experience, (3) the video content creator was seen as a relatable role model and, (4) viewers found the SWM video benefitted short-term and long-term goals. We discuss the theoretical implications on social learning processes and practical implications for designing social aspects of learning environments.

title: Exploring the Interaction Between L2 Learners and AI Translator in English Writing
citation: Kim, H., Cho, Y. H., & Park, S. (2022). Exploring the interaction between l2 learners and AI translator in english writing. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2032-2033). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Kim, H., Cho, Y. H., & Park, S.
subject: Humanities, Language & Literacy
abstract: This study investigated how L2 learners interact with an artificial intelligence (AI) translator for English writing and explored the effects of the English writing skills on interaction patterns. L2 learners (n=21) wrote an essay in English using an AI translator. As a result, three clusters were found: English writing, Korean writing, and Interactive writing. The interaction pattern was different according to the expression scores. The results provide implications in designing interactions between learners and AI.

title: Meaningful Movement Towards Campus-Based Outdoor Learning: Characterizing Pre-Scenery With Stakeholder Perspective
citation: Schmidt, A. C. & Zuiker, S. (2022). Meaningful movement towards campus-based outdoor learning: Characterizing pre-scenery with stakeholder perspective. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2034-2035). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Schmidt, A. C. & Zuiker, S.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This study seeks to characterize what matters to stakeholders as a school moves towards campusbased outdoor learning. Results from a survey (n=87) demonstrate stakeholder alignment in relation to a longstanding outdoor education movement and emerging movements responding to COVID-19. Discussion considers the polylogic of local communities that work to inspire, enable, and sustain commitments to campusbased outdoor learning.

title: An Adaptive, Agile Learner-Centered Computer Science Curriculum Design Approach Based on Deep Knowledge Tracing
citation: Xiao, R. & Chi, C. (2022). An adaptive, agile learner-centered computer science curriculum design approach based on deep knowledge tracing. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2036-2037). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Xiao, R. & Chi, C.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
abstract: While the focus of the curriculum is on the students, their voices are rarely heard in the creation or adaptation of the curriculum. It is often impractical and difficult to try to address the needs of each student in a single curriculum. With the use of Deep Knowledge Tracing (DKT), we propose a learner-centric curriculum design that is adaptive and agile, performing interventions on an individualized basis.

title: Real Work With Real Consequences in an Evolving Classroom Context: Consequential and Connected STEM Learning
citation: Jongewaard, R. & Jordan, M. E. (2022). Real work with real consequences in an evolving classroom context: Consequential and connected STEM learning. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2038-2039). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Jongewaard, R. & Jordan, M. E.
subject: STEM - Engineering & Robotics
abstract: In this DBR study, we explore how one middle school STEM teacher designed for real work with real consequences by supporting students’ agentive and productive participation in community-based engineering activities across virtual, hybrid, and face-to-face settings across multiple project cycles.

title: Embracing Diversity and Connectivity for Entrepreneurship Education Innovation: An Observation Study of Co-Creation Pedagogy for Design Thinking Capacity Building Program of Higher Education
citation: Cheng, L., Peng, Y., Chan, A., Zhang, W. C., & Wang, Y. (2022). Embracing diversity and connectivity for entrepreneurship education innovation: An observation study of co-creation pedagogy for design thinking capacity building program of higher education. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2042-2043). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Cheng, L., Peng, Y., Chan, A., Zhang, W. C., & Wang, Y.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
conceptualisations_list: Computer-Supported Collaborative Learning (CSCL); Co-Design & Participatory Design
abstract: With the growing popularity of design thinking capacity building initiatives for entrepreneurship education, educators are striving to explore technology-supported learning environments and pedagogy to achieve the inter-disciplinary, easily accessible, and studentoriented entrepreneurship education innovation. The lingering effects of unfinished learning amid the COVID-19 and mixed-mode learning have become part of a new normal, we designed and implemented a novel learning framework to put co-design pedagogical structures in place that allow educators, students, and stakeholders to form new learning experiences and create innovation together. Through the case study we designed and implemented in three universities across different regions, we propose and investigate an approach that enables micro-level analysis of knowledge creation model for student’s design thinking capacity building as well as macro-level understanding of learning dynamics for entrepreneurship education. This study presents a pedagogy-based template, and the findings have implications for the design of technology-empowered educational interventions and pedagogical innovation. Keywords: Collaborative Learning, Entrepreneurship Education Innovation

title: Argumentative Characteristics of Equal and Active Participation in Project-Based Learning
citation: Peng, S., Matsuya, H., & Nemoto, a. (2022). Argumentative characteristics of equal and active participation in project-based learning. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2044-2045). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Peng, S., Matsuya, H., & Nemoto, H.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
conceptualisations_list: Computer-Supported Collaborative Learning (CSCL); Epistemic Network Analysis (ENA)
abstract: Equal and active participation is a desirable team state in the process of collaborative learning. In this study, we analyzed an argumentative aspect of equal and active participation in project-based learning: an 8-day online innovation workshop. Epistemic network analysis revealed that learners engage in elaborative discourse when they participate equally and actively. Furthermore, such time can be clustered into two types which have a distinct mechanism for facilitating participation.

title: Developing Computational Thinking via Knowledge Building
citation: Huang, H., Chang, Y., & Hong, H. (2022). Developing computational thinking via knowledge building. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2046-2047). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Huang, H., Chang, Y., & Hong, H.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
abstract: This study explored the impact of knowledge building pedagogy within a collaborative learning community on students’ understanding of computational thinking (CT). The participants were 101 middle school students who attended a 6-week course to work on Scratch programming guided by knowledge building principles. An international challenge test on computational thinking called “Bebras Challenge” was employed to evaluate students’ CT. Primary findings indicate that students significantly improved their CT skills in the end of the course.

title: Reading Minds: Exploring Relationships Between Sensor-Data and Self-Reported Cognitive-Affective States of Learners
citation: Lal, S., Eysink, T. H., Gijlers, H. A., Verwey, W. B., & Veldkamp, B. P. (2022). Reading minds: Exploring relationships between sensor-data and self-reported cognitive-affective states of learners. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2048-2049). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Lal, S., Eysink, T. H., Gijlers, H. A., Verwey, W. B., & Veldkamp, B. P.
subject: Humanities, Language & Literacy
abstract: Cognitive-affective states (CASs) strongly affect learning outcomes. Therefore, learning systems need to be CAS-aware to truly cater to learners’ needs. In this study, we explore the possibility of multimodal sensor data as reliable indicators of learner CASs. Data collected will include skin conductance, heart rate, skin temperature and global gaze properties, which will be compared with self-reported CASs of learners. Linear mixed models will be applied and results will be presented at the conference.

title: Opportunities and Challenges for Enacting Equity and Justice-Centered CS Learning in “Drag vs. AI” Workshops
citation: Ruppert, J., Roque, R., & Shapiro, R. B. (2022). Opportunities and challenges for enacting equity and justice-centered CS learning in “drag vs. AI” workshops. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2052-2053). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Ruppert, J., Roque, R., & Shapiro, R. B.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
abstract: We present initial reflections from a study investigating how learning materials and moment-to-moment interactions can enact equity and justicecentered learning in youth STEAM programming. We explore these questions in the context of Drag vs. AI, a library workshop in which a professional drag queen leads teens in an exploration of facial recognition technologies (FRTs) and drag makeup as a tool to subvert, fool, and refuse recognition. We are examining ethnographic data from workshops at two sites and plan to conduct follow-up interviews. We will share insights and reflections from our inprogress data analysis around the affordances and limitations of materials and interactions for justice-centered computing education.

title: CT for All? Computational Thinking in Danish Language Arts
citation: Hachmann, R. & Hansen, S. B. (2022). CT for all? Computational thinking in danish language arts. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2054-2055). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Hachmann, R. & Hansen, S. B.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; Humanities, Language & Literacy
tpack_ck_labels: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; Humanities, Language & Literacy
abstract: This poster presentation discusses ongoing, design-based research that investigates how middle school pupils use computational thinking strategies as part of their collaborative effort to write interactive stories, using the online tool Twine within the school subject of Danish (L1). A tool, specifically designed to support pupils’ processual text production is introduced, and its affordances and constraints as a structuring resource, supporting the pupil’s computational participation and literacy skills, are discussed.

title: Draw-a-Computer-Scientist-Teacher? Designing for Expansive Identities in Undergraduate Computer Science
citation: Weidler-Lewis, J. & Doore, S. (2022). Draw-a-computer-scientist-teacher? Designing for expansive identities in undergraduate computer science. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2056-2057). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Weidler-Lewis, J. & Doore, S.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
abstract: This poster investigates integrating teacher identities with disciplinary identities in the domain of computer science. Initial findings from a study analyzing undergraduate perceptions of both computer scientists and teachers are presented. Drawing on socio-cultural theories of learning and identity, we argue, and our findings suggest, that surfacing perceptions of both computer scientists and teachers is a productive exercise to reveal areas of commonality and contradictions to overcome in our designs for learning in both domains.

title: Designing for Youth-Centered Experiences in Informal STEM-rich Making With Minoritized Youth During the Pandemic: Conjectures & Considerations
citation: Worsley, T. & Tan, E. (2022). Designing for youth-centered experiences in informal STEM-rich making with minoritized youth during the pandemic: Conjectures & considerations. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2060-2061). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Worsley, T. & Tan, E.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
abstract: The pandemic has brought an abrupt shift from in-person community-based programming at an informal weekly STEM-rich making club with minoritized youth, to one of socially-distanced, solo-work only, virtually-facilitated experience. We explore what such an abrupt pivot from in-person to virtual programming meant, including the challenges and tensions, for the design of pedagogical materials and virtual facilitation practices, when facilitators aim to maintain an asset-based, relational engagement where youth can make in agentic ways, pandemic notwithstanding.

title: Supporting Elementary School Teachers in Their Learning of Programming and Robotics: A Case Study
citation: Boz, T. & Allexsaht-Snider, M. (2022). Supporting elementary school teachers in their learning of programming and robotics: A case study. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2062-2063). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Boz, T. & Allexsaht-Snider, M.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; STEM - Engineering & Robotics
tpack_ck_labels: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; STEM - Engineering & Robotics
abstract: We examined elementary school teachers’ learning of block-based programming and robotics under the guidance of an instructor in a professional learning (PL) course. Data consisted of teacher artifacts and videos recorded in the PL course. Data analysis revealed that the type of guidance and support the instructor provided helped teachers develop their programming skills and shaped their attitudes toward programming integration in elementary schools. The instructor’s guidance also posed a few barriers to teachers’ learning.

title: Online Instructional Coaching During the COVID-19 Pandemic
citation: Wieselmann, J. R. & Sager, M. T. (2022). Online instructional coaching during the COVID-19 pandemic. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2064-2065). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Wieselmann, J. R. & Sager, M. T.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: With COVID-19 necessitating a shift to online teaching and professional development, a unique opportunity to study online instructional coaching emerged. With prior evidence that the provision of a STEM curriculum unit and online coaching supported a firstyear science teacher in improving his instructional practices, this study utilized interaction analysis to explore the coaching moves that were implemented by three STEM instructional coaches and identify the online coaching moves that prompted teacher reflection. Findings highlight the distinct coaching styles of the individual coaches and the range of moves that preceded teacher reflection. Implications for online instructional coaching are considered.

title: Exploring Different Facilitator Roles in Maker-Based Learning
citation: Zhang, E., White, A., Todd, K., & Wardrip, P. (2022). Exploring different facilitator roles in maker-based learning. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2070-2071). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Zhang, E., White, A., Todd, K., & Wardrip, P.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: The purpose of this study is to investigate how different facilitator roles (educator, adult caregiver, peer and self-facilitation) influence children’s learning engagement--specifically, the learning practices of seeking and sharing resources (SSR)--in a museum’s makerspace. We address two research questions: 1). In what ways do learners' engagement vary when facilitated by different facilitator roles? 2). In what ways do different types of facilitators influence SSR practices across age ranges? The results show that facilitation from caregivers and self-directed facilitation is associated with significantly more SSR practices. Additionally, we found that the influence of different types of facilitators on learning engagement varies across ages. Self-directed learning is associated with an increase of SSR as children grow, while facilitation from caregivers is associated with a decline of SSR as children age. Based on these findings, we discuss implications for facilitation in museum makerspace.

title: Novice Versus Advanced Undergraduate Computing Students’ Engagement in Collaboration in an Online Flipped Classroom
citation: Vickery, M. & Mithun, S. (2022). Novice versus advanced undergraduate computing students’ engagement in collaboration in an online flipped classroom. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2072-2073). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Vickery, M. & Mithun, S.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
abstract: This paper explores students' engagement in collaborative learning activities within two data science courses (one introductory and one advanced) taught synchronously online during the 2020-2021 academic year. Here, we draw on a multidimensional perspective of student engagement to understand novice and advanced computing students' collaborative learning practices and propose instructional design elements informed by students’ unique needs and the limitations of the virtual format.

title: Key Elements of a Critical Approach to Financial Literacy
citation: Sandoval-Llanos, J. (2022). Key elements of a critical approach to financial literacy. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2076-2077). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Sandoval-Llanos, J.
subject: Humanities, Language & Literacy
abstract: Financial Literacy is a topic of recent emergence, still subject of debate about its epistemology and disciplinary background. While Latin American governments are implementing National Strategies for Financial Education under the guidance of multilateral institutions, arguments against these initiatives consider that they perpetuate oppressive practices while displacing the focus of the problem from the financial system to individuals. This poster presents a theoretical proposal for a critical approach to financial literacy to address these concerns.

title: Methodological Progress in Co-Regulation and Socially Shared Regulation of Learning Research: A Systematic Review
citation: Dang, B., Hong, Y., Nguyen, B. T., & Nguyen, A. (2022). Methodological progress in co-regulation and socially shared regulation of learning research: A systematic review. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2078-2079). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Dang, B., Hong, Y., Nguyen, B. T., & Nguyen, A.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
conceptualisations_list: Self-Regulated Learning (SRL) & Metacognition; Multimodal Learning Analytics (MMLA)
abstract: Self-regulated learning (SRL), co-regulation (CoRL), and socially shared regulation of learning (SSRL) have been essential for successful learning and collaboration. However, it is challenging to objectively capture the “invisible” cognitive and emotional processes at the foundation of learning regulation. To better understand and support SSRL, the study reviewed 118 journals published between 2003 and 2020. Results highlighted the need for methodological development of reliable multilevel analysis methods to analyze multimodal data at different proximal levels.

title: Towards Automated Tracking of Affect: Testing the Use of Continuous Self-Reports and Multimodal Metrics
citation: Sung, G., Hassan, J., & Schneider, B. (2022). Towards automated tracking of affect: Testing the use of continuous self-reports and multimodal metrics. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2080-2081).
