abstract: This paper informs designs for teacher learning and reflection that advance equitable discourse practices in secondary science classrooms. We share design insights from the initial iteration of a design-based research project, ClassInSight, that supports teachers’ facilitation of dialogic-discourse practices in science classrooms through guided reflection on classroom discourse visualizations. We analyze transcripts of reflection sessions of the participants and ask: How did teacher-researcher dyads interact with the initial design prototypes of classroom discourse data visualization and reflection practices? How were reflections on data visualizations constrained by design? We found that teachers and researchers did not share an understanding of classroom discourse moves and that teacher reflections did not connect explicitly to issues of equity in the classroom. The findings show the need to design for shared meaning-making between teachers and researchers on classroom discourse categories and make visible the ways they conceptualize equity in science classroom discourse practices.

abstract: This study validates an Adaptive Equity-Oriented Pedagogical Competency (AEPC) assessment, a measure of college instructors’ teaching effectiveness. AEPC integrates core elements that have together been shown to improve student learning by over a letter grade. These elements include: 1) Clarifying learning outcomes, 2) Aligning formative assessment with learning outcomes, 3) Identifying students’ competencies, needs and interests, 4) Understanding equity barriers to meeting outcomes, 5) Adapting based on needs and barriers, and 6) Iterating: Reflecting upon pedagogy to support continuous learning. Developed under Wilson's (2005) validity framework and calibrated using a partial credit Rasch model, the AEPC measure has both high reliability (0.94) and significant correlation with independent reviews of instructional quality. This measure includes materials that are often included in portfolios used in part to evaluate college teaching, such as teaching philosophy and practice statements, learning outcomes, formative assessment, and reflections on teaching (Seldin, Miller, Seldin, 2010). Unlike course evaluations, this measure shows no gender or URM assessment bias. A learning progression of inclusive practices shown to improve student success provides a measurement foundation for the AEPC assessment.

Guided by social cognitive career theory (SCCT), this paper applies epistemic network analysis (ENA) to examine the data collected from in-depth interviews with 8 YSP participants. It was found that YSP participation was linked to the development of motivation and self-efficacy and subsequent decisions to pursue STEM fields.

abstract: Epistemic practices are the goal- and norm-guided actions people use to develop knowledge within a domain, such as analyzing evidence to support scientific claims. Developing sound epistemic practices is critical considering the current rise in post-truth discourse that constrains society’s abilities to make informed decisions. Learning scientists have increasingly offered frameworks and methodologies to support improved epistemic performance. However, there is a lack of consensus in the field about what epistemic practices are that students can take up, as well as strategies to best support teachers in this endeavor. This symposium brings together seven teams of researchers who have been working on developing epistemic practices in K-12 classrooms. In conversation with each other and the audience, we aim to understand how epistemic growth is conceptualized in its myriad forms across students and teachers in addition to the design characteristics and indicators of growth of learning environments that promote epistemic performance. abstract: Over the past decade, science education has been pushed to an inflection point. What was once a given of scalable standards-based science education is now being reimagined as adaptable models for teaching science through collaborative student-led sensemaking. This tension of supporting individual students’ ways of knowing and being in coordination with canonical STEM practices has teachers caught between a paradigmatic binary. The field of the Learning Sciences provides comprehensive knowledge about the need for opening up diverse learning pathways in the classroom, yet little is discussed about what to do once those learning pathways are made visible. In this symposium, the authors consider how teachers “make space” for student contributions in classroom-based science education, and consequently, analyze what happens after it is made.

Although reasoning with data is rooted in epistemic processes, the stances people take are—and should be—influenced by values, concerns about maintaining cultural group membership, and concerns about equity and justice.

abstract: Black, Brown, and Indigenous communities have long drawn upon storywork - the interrelated processes of storytelling and storylistening - as central strategies of wellness and thriving despite histories of dispossession and domination. This collection of papers theorizes with storywork and provides five contexts of storywork-in-praxis, where acts of creating, telling, and listening to stories feature centrally in critically re-designing spaces towards Black life, Indigenous futures, and the mutual flourishing of communities and lands. Through a syncretic approach, we bring together learning sciences research and perspectives from Black and Indigenous studies to further theorize the role that storywork plays within (1) sense-making activities, (2) the lives of communities that we have been a part of, and (3) our own lives as researchers-storylisteners. We consider the multiple roles of stories in research and design, the political/ethical nature of stories, and how storywork can re-organize power relations in ways that support individual and collective life.

abstract: In this symposium, we will reconceptualize our methodologies and research design centering histories in places, bodies, and disciplinary learning. We re-engage in qualitative methodologies that guided us so far yet limited us in fully accounting for the sociopolitical and sociohistorical nature of our research and analyses. This symposium challenges individualized knowledge production and invites the field of the learning sciences to bring forth collective and dialogic figuring and refiguring, co-thinking, and community/solidarity building. Four sets of paired dialogues will defamiliarize familiar methodologies in the learning sciences (e.g., videobased research, interaction analysis, ethnography) toward fuller consideration of power and radical transformation. These paired dialogues will also open new horizons on the role of arts and affect in research from the perspectives of histories in places and in bodies. Collectively, we will revisit the epistemological assumptions that shaped what were rendered visible and invisible in our research process.

abstract: This double symposium brings together activity-theoretical formative intervention research conducted in six continents. The aim is to illuminate and examine the common threads, important differences, and new challenges of formative intervention studies to address “wicked problems” in different cultural, political, and economic contexts. Formative interventions facilitate expansive learning and systemic transformation led by local stakeholders in organizations and social movements. The formative intervention methodology is based on the principles of double stimulation and ascending from the abstract to the concrete. Its most well-known application is the Change Laboratory method. Formative interventions generate and support expansive learning and transformative agency. The current global crises of climate change, poverty and deepening inequalities are giving rise to what is called fourth generation activity theory for tackling fateful challenges by building heterogenous multiactivity coalitions. The symposium will present the theoretical and pedagogical challenges and possibilities in Change Laboratories and other formative interventions to develop just and sustainable solutions to global crises.

abstract: This symposium brings together research that examines equity as it relates to facilitation across a diverse set of tinkering and making activities and settings. Drawing on an equity framework for out-of-school learning, we focus on the potential for facilitation to create transformative learning opportunities for learners who have been historically marginalized in making and tinkering activities, including communities of color; note the complexity of equitable facilitation across settings and contexts; and highlight the importance of facilitator reflection to acknowledge and challenge hegemonic approaches in STEAM. Taken collectively, these papers highlight not only how facilitation is essential for making productive connections between making and tinkering and the sociopolitical issues at play in our world, but how those pedagogical practices themselves are sociopolitical, connected with histories and disciplines in ways that can either reify existing inequities in STEAM or create new, more equitable futures for learners and facilitators.

abstract: Educators and designers of learning experiences must make critical decisions not only about the what, why, to what ends and for whom of learning (Philip et al., 2018), but also when, where and at what pace. This symposium is organized around the conjecture that by more explicitly and systematically considering the time-space dimensions of learning and design processes, we can more reliably surface differences in how we understand learning as well as inequities that result from how it is conceptualized and designed for, helping make progress towards more just educational futures. Collectively, this symposium shows the progress that one group of learning scientists assembled in the ISLS 2021 Early Career Workshop has made in bringing careful attention, useful theory, and systematic approaches to understanding equity issues related to space and time, while also working out ways to attend to these issues in our temporally and spatially distributed design processes.

This symposium explores these approaches with a multi-disciplinary group of researchers presenting empirical studies on designing and studying AI learning environments. These studies provide unique insights towards design recommendations, challenges, and opportunities in the rapidly emerging area of study in K-12 education.

subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Over the last few years, learning scientists have become increasingly interested in research around student’s motivational and emotional processes, guided by a commitment to affirm learners' individual identities and support justice-oriented design and pedagogies. With ample evidence to show that the Covid-19 pandemic has exaggerated learner’s struggles with their thoughts, feelings, and identity, the importance of such research has never been higher. This symposium brings together an international group of scholars with varying research contexts (online, in-person, hybrid, blended), working with students of different age groups (K12, Undergraduates, pre-service teachers) to present their work around affective learning and teaching. The symposium’s focus on affective learning designs that acknowledge learner emotions, affirm their identity, foster designer empathy and build a pedagogy of care will springboard deeper discussions in the ISLS community to further explore “global perspectives on equity and justice that promote the empowerment of educational innovation for all” (ISLS, 2022).

title: The Neural Basis of Learning Through Productive Failure
citation: Formaz, C., Gashaj, V., Trninic, D., Hoffmann, S., & Kapur, M. (2022). The neural basis of learning through productive failure. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1820-1821). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Formaz, C., Gashaj, V., Trninic, D., Hoffmann, S., & Kapur, M.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Productive Failure (PF) is a learning design wherein learners generate solutions for novel problems prior to formal instruction. Research has demonstrated the effectiveness of PF, indicating cognitive mechanisms for why students learn better after encountering difficulties. However, neurophysiological mechanisms underpinning “learning from failure” have yet to be explored, despite robust evidence connecting neural activity, heartbeats, and cognitive processes. The present study explores neural and physiological mechanisms underlying PF, employing neural signature and heartrate variability measurements.

title: Museum Educators' Knowledge Brokering With Boundary Objects
citation: Ostrowdun, C. & Kim, B. (2022). Museum educators' knowledge brokering with boundary objects. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1838-1839). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Ostrowdun, C. & Kim, B.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Museum educators often use objects as part of education programs for visiting school groups. We examined how museum educators leveraged boundary objects and forms of talk to as part of knowledge brokering between the bounded communities of palaeontology and school groups. Findings show how educators broker with talk and objects, and how brokering can fail.

title: Designing to Enhance Academic Buoyancy: A Snapshot of First Steps in a Second Level School Setting
citation: Connolly, E., Flynn, P., & Garland, S. (2022). Designing to enhance academic buoyancy: A snapshot of first steps in a second level school setting. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1848-1849). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Connolly, E., Flynn, P., & Garland, S.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Academic buoyancy generally refers to students' ability to respond to everyday challenges in academic settings. This paper presents insights in to a design-based research pilot intervention that is informed by a multi-ontological framework that included conceptual pillars of: engagement, collaboration and reflection. Preliminary findings are presented, the emergence of co-creation as a core element of the success of the pilot is explored, and next steps discussed.

title: “You Are Not Valued as They Said”: Re-Constructing a U.S. Higher Education Environment Negotiated by an International Student
citation: Li, P. J. (2022). “You are not valued as they said”: Re-constructing a U.S. higher education environment negotiated by an international student. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1858-1859). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Li, P. J.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This paper responds to the call for examining and promoting a more diverse and equitable education environment by shedding light on an international student’s experience in U.S. higher education. Using narrative analysis, the author unfolds the participant’s proactive actions and resistant voices. The results also show the hidden “de facto” in the environment that the participant experienced with, further contributing to the education practices by unveiling the limitations of the current U.S. educational system.

title: Data-Driven Badge Design for Gamified Learning App
citation: Langenhagen, J. (2022). Data-driven badge design for gamified learning app. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1864-1865). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Langenhagen, J.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Although badges belong to the most used game elements in gamified learning tools, little is known about their optimal design. This poster will therefore discuss a data-driven approach to determine an optimal set of badges based on usage data from the corresponding learning tools. This approach will be tested with actual usage data from a learning app that was used for four semesters in a university lecture.

title: How a Teacher’s Personal Reflections Shape Her Decision Making for Classroom Management
citation: Pelekanou, G. & Louca, L. T. (2022). How a teacher’s personal reflections shape her decision making for classroom management. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1866-1867). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Pelekanou, G. & Louca, L. T.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
abstract: We investigate how a teacher’s personal reflection shapes her decision-making process in classroom management. Following open coding, we analyze the teachers’ reflections seeking to identify her rationale in the decision-making process during the language arts lessons. Our findings indicated that her thinking was based on the student’s behavior, the student’s personality, the educational context, her own emotional perspective and condition, her pedagogical knowledge, and her reflective experience. We discuss the theoretical and methodological implications.

title: Using Electronic Textiles to Visualize the Loss of Tribal Lands Over Time
citation: Searle, K. A. & Fischback, L. (2022). Using electronic textiles to visualize the loss of tribal lands over time. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1874-1875). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Searle, K. A. & Fischback, L.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; STEM - Engineering & Robotics; Social & Civic Studies
tpack_ck_labels: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; STEM - Engineering & Robotics; Social & Civic Studies
abstract: This poster shares the design and development of a data visualization project that brings together social studies, Indian Education For All, and computing to center understanding of the loss of tribal lands by the Blackfeet Nation in Montana. Students utilize Circuit Playground Express microcontrollers to program LEDs representing the percentage of original (pre-contact) tribal lands still owned by the Blackfeet Nation at various points in United States history.

title: Using Delivery Simulation Experiences in Hiring in the Technology Field
citation: Weber, S. (2022). Using delivery simulation experiences in hiring in the technology field. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1876-1877). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Weber, S.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Technical assessments and interviews are a unique facet of the technology field. Unfortunately, they have gaps that lead to frustration for candidates and result in companies missing top talent. I propose using delivery simulation experiences to better assess and meet the needs of a modern workforce.

title: Professional Learning to Promote Three-Dimensional Teaching Using Computational Modeling in Remote Classroom Contexts
citation: Shin, N., Brennan, L., Bowers, J., Eidin, E., Stephens, L., McIntyre, C., Roderick, S., & Damelin, D. (2022). Professional learning to promote three-dimensional teaching using computational modeling in remote classroom contexts. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1878-1879). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Shin, N., Brennan, L., Bowers, J., Eidin, E., Stephens, L., McIntyre, C., Roderick, S., & Damelin, D.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This study explores how to support teachers in developing and implementing effective pedagogical strategies to promote students in making sense of phenomena through computational modeling in remote contexts. Qualitative analyses of eight teachers’ interviews were conducted to characterize their pedagogical strategies to achieve three-dimensional learning. Findings indicate that typical teacher strategies include the teacher and students coconstructing a model and using whole class or group discussions to support students’ modeling practices.

title: Fostering TPACK via Idea Improvement in Teacher Education
citation: Seet, C. H., Chang, Y., Hung, G., & Hong, H. (2022). Fostering TPACK via idea improvement in teacher education. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1882-1883). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Seet, C. H., Chang, Y., Hung, G., & Hong, H.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This study examined 38 pre-service teachers’ ideas regarding TPACK development in their lesson design during online discussion. Data include all discourse posts and the findings showed three main kinds of idea development processes existing in teacher’s discussion. Such results indicate that to help advance teachers’ TPACK, teachers’ idea development must go through an integration process instead of stagnating at a diversification or elaboration stage.

title: Learning and Developing Positive Psychology via Knowledge Building
citation: Chen, J., Chen, M., & Hong, H. (2022). Learning and developing positive psychology via knowledge building. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1884-1885). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Chen, J., Chen, M., & Hong, H.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This study explores how 56 college students engaging in knowledge-building to advance their knowledge about positive psychology. Data include online behaviors, course evaluation results, and a survey. The findings showed: 1) students were able to work collaboratively to discuss online about two psychological theories; 2) knowledge-building, esp. knowledge-sharing, was significantly related to final course assessment; 3) surveys showed improved well-being scores among students.

title: Multiplicity Matters: The Development of Interest Profiles During Dynamic Institutional Transitions
citation: Draijer, J., Bronkhorst, L., Flunger, B., & Akkerman, S. (2022). Multiplicity matters: The development of interest profiles during dynamic institutional transitions. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1886-1887). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Draijer, J., Bronkhorst, L., Flunger, B., & Akkerman, S.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Students pursue multiple interests within their daily lives. The current study aims to describe the development of interest profiles (the total composition of all interests one pursues) in terms of the amount of interests, their domain divergence and developmental stages. Using Latent Growth Models on interest data of 309 students over the course of three years (10 timepoints), we will specifically explore interest profile development, also in the context of institutional transitions and COVID-19 measures.

title: UTeach/NYC: A Research Practice Partnership to Expand and Improve Computer Science Education for All
citation: Petrosino, A. J., Hughes, K., Sager, M. T., & Sherard, M. K. (2022). UTeach/NYC: A research practice partnership to expand and improve computer science education for all. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1898-1899). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Petrosino, A. J., Hughes, K., Sager, M. T., & Sherard, M. K.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; STEM - Natural Science
tpack_ck_labels: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; STEM - Natural Science
abstract: This 3-year Design-Based Implementation Research (DBIR) study focuses on a Research Practice Partnership (RPP) that encourages broad student participation in computer science (CS), looking at underrepresented urban youth in New York City. In particular, the research examines what organizational conditions, processes, and supports are associated with improved participation by Black and Latino/a students in CS, as measured by the diversity of students enrolling in CS courses. Results indicate an increase in trust has been reliant on the strides made from the partners involved, as well as building upon the RPP framework. Improved communication has resulted from continuity of meetings, regular exchanges of email, and having detailed agendas and expectations for the partners involved.

title: Interactive Transcription Techniques for Interaction Analysis
citation: Mathur, A. & Shapiro, B. R. (2022). Interactive transcription techniques for interaction analysis. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 19-26). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Mathur, A. & Shapiro, B. R.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
abstract: Interaction analysis is a valuable method and approach to study knowledge in use in the learning sciences and CSCL communities. Central to interaction analysis is the creation of transcripts to selectively encode and represent audio and video data. However, current transcription techniques used in interaction analysis, including multimodal transcription techniques, have yet to explore the strengths and weaknesses of interactive visualization to selectively encode and represent people’s interaction in context. Drawing from recent efforts to amplify, not automate, transcription in qualitative research, this paper interactively visualizes one video dataset in five different ways using contemporary interactive visualization techniques. Findings and discussion characterize these visualizations as interactive transcripts that demonstrate techniques valuable to interaction analysis, but also highlight the need to expand how people, things, and context are represented through visualization mediums such as visualization programming languages to align with work more meaningfully in the learning sciences and CSCL communities.

title: Embodied Cognition in Virtual Reality to Support Learning of Scale
citation: Gampp, T., Delgado, C., Peterson, M., & Chen, K. B. (2022). Embodied cognition in virtual reality to support learning of scale. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1900-1901). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Gampp, T., Delgado, C., Peterson, M., & Chen, K. B.
subject: STEM - Natural Science
abstract: This work-in-progress poster reports on the development process of a virtual environment to support embodied cognition about the scale of scientific entities from subatomic particles to galaxies. Research shows that learners struggle to comprehend the sizes of entities beyond human scale. In order to determine specific entities to use in the virtual environment, a document analysis of US K-undergraduate science education standards was undertaken. Entities, categories of entities, and ranges of sizes were identified.

title: Exploring Identity Resources in Co-Designing Chatbots
citation: Nguyen, H. (2022). Exploring identity resources in co-designing chatbots. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1918-1919). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Nguyen, H.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Co-design with students honors their lived experiences and invites participants to create novel solutions. We present insights from designing with youth ages 14-16 to create a collaborative chatbot in science. We explore the identity resources (material, relational, and ideational) embedded in the design activities, with implications for how designers and educators can provide access to resources and expand how youths participate in design practices.

title: Machine Learning for Evaluating Critical Data Literacy in Open Online Learning Environments
citation: Mushi, D. (2022). Machine learning for evaluating critical data literacy in open online learning environments. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1920-1921). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Mushi, D.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; Humanities, Language & Literacy
tpack_ck_labels: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; Humanities, Language & Literacy
abstract: The study highlights the application of machine learning in assessing critical data literacy in an open online learning network. The study uses Support Vector Machine algorithm to build a predictive model based on a labeled dataset with students’ comments on data visualizations. Features that indicate reflection and curiosity can be used with machine learning algorithms to assess the level of critical data literacy in activities that are adaptive to data representation.

title: How Adolescent Learners in a STEM Summer Camp Represent Astronomy Concepts Through a Drawing Exercise
citation: Gadbury, M., Zimmer, K., Ginger, J., & Lane, H. C. (2022). How adolescent learners in a STEM summer camp represent astronomy concepts through a drawing exercise. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1928-1929). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Gadbury, M., Zimmer, K., Ginger, J., & Lane, H. C.
subject: STEM - Natural Science
abstract: Learners in an informal, STEM-focused summer camp (n = 19) spent one week exploring hypothetical versions of Earth and known exoplanets in a customized version of the digital sandbox game, Minecraft. On the third day of camp, learners were asked to draw their own exoplanets and incorporate various scientific measurements used in the game (i.e. oxygen levels, temperature, etc..). A semiotics analysis was applied to the drawings to understand how learners use representations to explain scientific phenomena and convey specific contextual themes related to the content of the camp. Outcomes showed about 70% of learner drawings included multiple celestial objects, depicting planetary system relationships.

title: Eye Movement Tracking During an Embodied Collective Activity in Science Teacher Training
citation: Zohar, R. (2022). Eye movement tracking during an embodied collective activity in science teacher training. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1938-1939). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Zohar, R.
subject: STEM - Natural Science
abstract: Middle-school science teachers who trained in the field of embodied pedagogy for teaching and learning physics, experienced an embodied collective activity for learning the concept of angular velocity. We tracked the teachers' eye movements during the collective activity in order to characterize their gaze behavior. The findings show that the subjects looked ahead during the activity, in contrast to their verbal report but in line with studies showing that eye movements can precede body movements.

title: What We Ought to Know: How Digital Museums Can Facilitate Reflection and Discourse of the Nigerian Civil War
citation: Aduro, J. & Davis, P. (2022). What we ought to know: How digital museums can facilitate reflection and discourse of the nigerian civil war. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1944-1945). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Aduro, J. & Davis, P.
subject: Social & Civic Studies
abstract: The Nigerian Civil War is a key event often unspoken of in public or taught in schools, despite its aftermath still being felt decades later in Nigerian society. In this paper, we make a case for how a digital museum offers room to reflect, discuss and remember this important part of the country’s history. We use design-based research to develop a digital museum to improve access to this history through a diversity of voices.

title: Self-Regulated Learning With Task-Centered Microlearning
citation: Palti, A. & Rosenberg-Kima, R. B. (2022). Self-regulated learning with task-centered microlearning. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1954-1955). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Palti, A. & Rosenberg-Kima, R. B.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: The need for self-regulated learning (SRL) skills was intensified during COVID-19, with schools shifting to online-learning. Using microlearning (short videos with self-evaluation) may promote SRL while an organizing-task may help assemble learning-units into a wider concept. We propose a task-centered microlearning framework for promoting SRL and other 21st century skills. Our pilot with middle school students revealed practicing aspects of SRL such as controlling the learning-environment, self-reflecting, and overcoming obstacles by using peers’ support.

title: Intertwining Research and Practice in Higher Education: Presenting LPI’s Learning Sciences Master Program
citation: Çakı, E., Corneloup, V., & Zenasni, F. (2022). Intertwining research and practice in higher education: Presenting LPI’s learning sciences master program. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1956-1957). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Çakı, E., Corneloup, V., & Zenasni, F.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
abstract: The LPI and Université de Paris have developed the AIRE Master program to train future change-makers and researchers in response to the transformation happening in our world. This innovative program offers high-level training through a learning-by-doing-based curriculum and social implications. It aims to embark on a rich discussion between various stakeholders on how research and hands-on practices can be combined in such a way to transform our higher education system.

title: Beyond the Design of Assessment Tasks: Expanding the Assessment Toolkit to Support Teachers’ Formative Assessment Practices in Elementary Science Classrooms
citation: Zaidi, S. Z., Arnold, S., Lehman, E. M., & Strickland, C. (2022). Beyond the design of assessment tasks: Expanding the assessment toolkit to support teachers’ formative assessment practices in elementary science classrooms. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1964-1965). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Zaidi, S. Z., Arnold, S., Lehman, E. M., & Strickland, C.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Teachers experience challenges in effectively using formative assessment practices in their classrooms. In the US, only 28% of elementary teachers report using formative assessment. This study highlights the need to design resources to meet teacher needs and support teachers in making sense of assessment information to inform three-dimensional learning and teaching. By surveying and interviewing five elementary school teachers, we identified specific barriers in using assessment information and 10 key needs from resources designed to support their formative assessment practice in science.

title: What Do Diagrams Reveal? A Comparative Analysis of Impact of Different External Representations on Conceptual Understanding
citation: Srivastava, A. (2022). What do diagrams reveal? A comparative analysis of impact of different external representations on conceptual understanding. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1966-1967). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Srivastava, A.
subject: STEM - Natural Science
abstract: Learning is both guided by and constrained by the features of the external representation (ER) used for developing conceptual understanding. This work uses a case-study design to study three groups of 5 pre-college biology students (n=15) who used three different ERs- concept-map, symbolic model and molecular model, to perform tasks related to the structure of the DNA (Deoxyribonucleic acid) molecule. A descriptive synthesis analysis of students’ diagrams revealed ER-specific changes in their conceptual knowledge.

title: Robots in Science: How Middle School Science Teachers Design Integrated Robotics Units for Their Science Classes
citation: Bernstein, D., Cassidy, M., Mucth-Jones, K., & Cross, J. L. (2022). Robots in science: How middle school science teachers design integrated robotics units for their science classes. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1968-1969). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Bernstein, D., Cassidy, M., Mucth-Jones, K., & Cross, J. L.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; STEM - Engineering & Robotics
tpack_ck_labels: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; STEM - Engineering & Robotics
abstract: Robotics activities can provide students with opportunities to engage in computational thinking (CT) as well as support disciplinary learning goals. The goal of the Robots in Science project is to create, implement, and refine a PD program for middle school science teachers to design and implement robotics and CT-integrated science lessons. Two case studies illustrate how teachers used robotics activities to provide opportunities for science learning.

title: What Songo Board Game Can Teach Us About Culture and Literacies
citation: Bayeck, R. Y. (2022). What songo board game can teach us about culture and literacies. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1974-1975). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Bayeck, R. Y.
subject: Humanities, Language & Literacy
abstract: Contending that gameplay is a constellation of literacy practices could imply that video/digital games are the only spaces where players engage in literacy practices. Literacies in game environments have mainly been evidenced by video/digital game research. Literature on board game literacies is still scarce. This paper investigates literacy practices in the gameplay of the board game Songo and demonstrates that culture shapes literacies.

title: Intertwining Art and STEM: An Analysis of STEAM Activities
citation: Tsurusaki, B., Sullivan, P. T., Tzou, C., Pugh, P., Guthrie, M., & Conner, L. D. (2022). Intertwining art and STEM: An analysis of STEAM activities. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1984-1985). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Tsurusaki, B., Sullivan, P. T., Tzou, C., Pugh, P., Guthrie, M., & Conner, L. D. C.
subject: STEM - Mathematics; STEM - Engineering & Robotics
abstract: The integration of Art with Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEAM) has been growing in popularity, however, there are a variety of conceptualizations of what it looks like. This study explores images of STEAM by examining activities created by informal educators. We found that STEAM activities were conceptualized as using one discipline in the service of another, intertwined, or parallel. This provides concrete images of what STEAM can look like in educational settings.

title: Learning Geometry Through Collaborative, Embodied Explorations With Augmented Reality Holograms
citation: Walkington, C., Nathan, M. J., Hunnicutt, J., Washington, J., & Holcomb-Webb, K. (2022). Learning geometry through collaborative, embodied explorations with augmented reality holograms. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1992-1993). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Walkington, C., Nathan, M. J., Hunnicutt, J., Washington, J., & Holcomb-Webb, K.
subject: STEM - Mathematics
abstract: Novel forms of technology, like shared Augmented Reality (AR) holograms, can spur the discovery of new hypotheses about cognition and how it is embodied and distributed. These holograms have affordances for exploration, collaboration, and learning that have never been seen before. In the present study, we examine the multimodal ways that high school students interact with shared AR holograms while exploring geometric conjectures. Through multimodal analysis, we fine both possibilities and important design considerations.

title: Can Educational Researchers Help Reduce Accident Rates in a Big Construction Company?
citation: Manalo, E., Ayabe, H., Yoshida, R., Watanabe, Y., & Tanabe, A. (2022). Can educational researchers help reduce accident rates in a big construction company?. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 1994-1995). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Manalo, E., Ayabe, H., Yoshida, R., Watanabe, Y., & Tanabe, A.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: It is not common for big construction companies to call upon educational researchers to collaborate with them in efforts at reducing worksite accident rates. In this paper, we describe one such collaboration, including the background and rationale for it, and the progress that the small team of educational researchers and construction company managers have made in the first 7 months of the project. We outline some of the processes through which strategies for addressing the problem have evolved, and consider how it may be possible for a project like this to manifest characteristics of the four dimensions of quality that Furlong and Oancea (2005) proposed for applied, practice-based educational research (epistemic, economic, technological, and capacity building and value for people). Our overall aim is to reflect on the extent to which educational researchers may be able to contribute to a more diverse range of applied research.

title: Using Immersive Augmented Reality to Guide Families’ Observations and Visualizations of Pollinator Habitats in Outdoor Spaces
citation: McClain, L. R., Zimmerman, H. T., Land, S. M., Faimon, L., Chiu, Y., Bowles, S., & Keith, C. A. (2022). Using immersive augmented reality to guide families’ observations and visualizations of pollinator habitats in outdoor spaces. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2000-2001). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: McClain, L. R., Zimmerman, H. T., Land, S. M., Faimon, L., Chiu, Y., Bowles, S., & Keith, C. A.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Immersive AR technologies can support students’ learning processes and deep engagement with outdoor science pursuits, yet few studies explore these technologies with out-of-school learners. We analyze how immersive AR features built into an outdoor-based mobile app shaped nine families’ learning experiences as they explored pollinator habitats. Preliminary findings revealed that immersive AR scanning tools built into the Pollinator Explorers app guided families’ observational practices of real-world objects through virtual overlays representing pollinator habitats.

title: Technological Repurposing: Extending Pedagogical Design Capacity to Include Technological Adaptations
citation: Witt, N. (2022). Technological repurposing: Extending pedagogical design capacity to include technological adaptations. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2002-2003). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Witt, N.
subject: STEM - Mathematics
abstract: This report builds upon Brown’s (2009) Pedagogical Design Capacity Framework, to describe instances of “technological repurposing” of technologically-enhanced curriculum developed with prospective mathematics teachers (PMTs). The presentation will highlight the progression of one PMT’s understanding of compactness and how this contributed to making an innovative technological adaptation in a set of lesson resources developed to help middle school students make sense of Gerrymandering.

title: Teachers Noticing Student Interest: A Micro-Interactional Foundation for Interest-Driven Learning
citation: Schindler, E. & Peppler, K. (2022). Teachers noticing student interest: A micro-interactional foundation for interest-driven learning. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2010-2011). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Schindler, E. & Peppler, K.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This study shares a descriptive framework for noticing student interest, building on extensive scholarship in teacher education on Teacher Noticing. Scholarship presented here documents differences in educator narratives of student interest, which has implications for how they then go on to sponsor it in their immediate learning environment. The overall contribution of this work is a nascent framework for operationalizing educator noticing skills to support student interest.

title: Tinkering in Parallel: Pathways for Professional Learning in Education
citation: Thomas Murphy, C. & Martin, L. (2022). Tinkering in parallel: Pathways for professional learning in education. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2030-2031). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Murphy, C. T. & Martin, L.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
abstract: This study explores professional learning that occurred during a summer program in which educators engaged with a series of tinkering activities facilitated online. Analysis revealed two primary themes: (1) generative starting points with multiple pathways for exploration, and (2) resolution of sticking points through social connections. An analytic frame of parallel process, adapted from counseling psychology, highlights the way these themes simultaneously speak to learning through tinkering and to professional development. This study explores the learning experiences of a group of STEM educators who completed an informal online professional development program in summer 2020 that featured a series of tinkering activities.

title: Sociomateriality of Apprenticeship Learning in Ecological Fieldwork
citation: Lo, S. C., Bridges, S., Yip, V. W., Williams, G. A., Chan, K. K., Chen, G., Leung, J. S., Russell, B., Not, C., & Goodwin, A. L. (2022). Sociomateriality of apprenticeship learning in ecological fieldwork. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2040-2041). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Lo, S. C. T., Bridges, S., Yip, V. W. Y., Williams, G. A., Chan, K. K. H., Chen, G., Leung, J. S. C., Russell, B., Not, C., & Goodwin, A. L.
subject: STEM - Natural Science
abstract: Learning in and through fieldwork usually occurs as apprenticeship in a situated, real-life context. This Interactional Ethnography of an ecology fieldwork initiative in Hong Kong adopts a microethnographic discourse analysis (ME/DA) using video recordings from point-of-view (POV) glasses. Analysis of university ecologist and secondary biology student micro-interactions illustrates how the ecologist shuttled between two sociomaterial ‘presences’ weaving scientific reasoning with the physical manipulation of natural objects in the field.

title: Student Reflections on Data Investigations of Local and Extreme Weather: A Cultural Historical Activity Theory Perspective
citation: Sezen-Barrie, A., Louie, J., Roche, B., Fegan, E., Buffington, P., Fitzgerald, B., Waterman, K., Finzer, W., & Morrison, D. L. (2022). Student reflections on data investigations of local and extreme weather: A cultural historical activity theory perspective. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2050-2051). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Sezen-Barrie, A., Louie, J., Roche, B., Fegan, E., Buffington, P., Fitzgerald, B., Waterman, K., Finzer, W., & Morrison, D. L.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
abstract: This study analyzes middle-school students' reflections on working with large-scale scientific data to investigate local extreme weather using the digital tool CODAP. Drawing from student focus group interviews and Cultural Historical Activity Theory, we examine factors that appeared to impede or facilitate data science learning in a sample of rural middle schools.

title: Bridging the Distance': Developing Entrepreneurial Thinking in an International and Interdisciplinary Learning Environment
citation: Gil, E., Zahav, A. E., & Siemionow, J. (2022). Bridging the distance': Developing entrepreneurial thinking in an international and interdisciplinary learning environment. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2058-2059). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Gil, E., Zahav, A. E., & Siemionow, J.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: The Covid19 pandemic presented challenges and opportunities for students' learning worldwide. An international interdisciplinary learning environment was designed to bridge the distance, address students' socio-emotional needs and to develop entrepreneurial thinking, a skill needed in times of uncertainty. Twenty-four education students from two countries took part in six online sessions. Initial results support the contribution of the project to developing the participants' entrepreneurial thinking and to the role socio-emotional aspects play in it.

title: Reframing Design for Transformative Change: Supporting Pre-Service Teachers in Adopting Designerly Stances Towards Inquiry
citation: Clark, D. B., Scott, D., & Becker, S. (2022). Reframing design for transformative change: Supporting pre-service teachers in adopting designerly stances towards inquiry. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2066-2067). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Clark, D. B., Scott, D., & Becker, S.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: We need transformative change in K-12 education to address the myriad challenges and inequities facing the world today. Traditional approaches to design in education as taught to pre-service teachers, however, support incremental improvements to efficacy and efficiency rather than transformative change. Guided by contemporary theory and research from design fields, we propose a framework for conceptualizing K-12 educators’ stances towards design organized along a continuum from technical rational to designerly. We use this framework as a lens to analyze data drawn from a case study examining 28 pre-service teachers' conceptualization and engagement in design within the context of a design course taken by over 400 pre-service teachers. Our analysis of a range of data sources demonstrated that most participants adopted either a technical rational or exploratory stance towards design by the end of the course. We conclude by explicating why certain shifts took place and proposing ways pre-service teachers could be supported in adopting more human-centered approaches to design.

title: Sociopolitical Discourses Within Student Farms and Gardens
citation: Sager, M. T. & Sherard, M. K. (2022). Sociopolitical discourses within student farms and gardens. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2068-2069). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Sager, M. T. & Sherard, M. K.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: We identified 46 university-based student farms or gardens’ (SFG) mission statements from around the U. S. and used sociosemantic analysis to describe and compare the individuals involved, the actions conducted, and the objects involved. Two discourses emerged from our analysis: (a) a depoliticized framing of SFGs as sites for producing food for higher education communities; and, (b) a politicized framing of SFGs as sites for engaging with issues of social and environmental justice within the broader community.

title: “I Would Rather Argue a Point”
citation: Mirra, N. & Garcia, A. (2022). “I would rather argue a point”: How academic argument writing mediates civic cognition and stifles democratic dreaming. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2074-2075). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Mirra, N. & Garcia, A.
subject: Humanities, Language & Literacy; Social & Civic Studies
tpack_ck_labels: Humanities, Language & Literacy; Social & Civic Studies
abstract: This study explores how the forms of writing that young people utilize to discuss civic issues with each other mediate their understandings of the nature and purpose of civic life and open (or close) potential communicative pathways to creative and empathetic forms of civic worldbuilding. Drawing upon a theoretical framework of speculative civic literacies and scholarship in civic cognition, democratic education, and academic argumentation, this study analyzes the discourse practices of 238 high school students from six communities across the United States who participated in a social design-based experiment aimed at fostering democratic dialogue across lines of geographic, social, and cultural difference. Findings from a content analysis of students’ digital posts and a qualitative case study of one student’s civic literacy repertoires demonstrate that student leveraging of normative academic argument writing structures largely stifles understandings of divergent perspectives and vulnerable civic communication by flattening considerations of identity, affect, and ideology.

title: Adolescents’ Interdisciplinary Learning in Self-Driven Learning
citation: Zhu, G. & Burrow, A. (2022). Adolescents’ interdisciplinary learning in self-driven learning. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2086-2087). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Zhu, G. & Burrow, A.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
abstract: Increasingly complex societal and environmental issues demand interdisciplinary solutions. However, there are barriers to implementing interdisciplinary learning, especially in the K-12 context. This study explored whether adolescents (i.e., mainly high-school-age students) chose to pursue interdisciplinary learning topics when they could choose learning topics. Through a content analysis of the application materials of 800 adolescents (Mage =16.59) participating GripTape – a 10-week self-driven learning program, we found that 44% of learners chose interdisciplinary learning topics. The results suggest that adolescents care about complex societal issues and are willing to tackle them using interdisciplinary knowledge in self-driven learning.

title: Creating Comics About COVID-19 to Understand the Intersections Between Science, Community, and Equity
citation: Honwad, S., Gopal, S. D., White, A., Rish, R., & Scates, J. (2022). Creating comics about COVID-19 to understand the intersections between science, community, and equity. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2092-2093). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Honwad, S., Gopal, S. D., White, A., Rish, R., & Scates, J.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic is a complex socio-scientific problem that needs to be understood and addressed at local and global levels. The problem has illuminated inequities among and within communities around the world. Given the importance and complexities of this concern, we targeted COVID-19 to examine student understanding of the interconnectedness between the science (What is COVID-19?), the local context (How does COVID-19 impact community?) and equity (How does COVID-19 impact different members of the community?).

title: Constructionist Design for Sustainable Development
citation: Thanapornsangsuth, S. (2022). Constructionist design for sustainable development. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2094-2095). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Thanapornsangsuth, S.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This poster introduces “Constructionist Design for Sustainable Development” as a design principle to engage students in a constructionist learning experience while addressing environmental and social challenges. To this end, we conducted a two-year qualitative designbased research project that engaged undergraduate and graduate-level students, lecturers, and community members from two universities in Thailand and Japan to design and build innovations that solve environmental and social problems in their communities.

title: Creating Space for Formative Peer Feedback in a Community-Oriented MOOC
citation: Aguinaga, J. M. & Quintana, R. M. (2022). Creating space for formative peer feedback in a community-oriented MOOC. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2096-2097). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Aguinaga, J. M. & Quintana, R. M.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
abstract: To advance community-oriented instructional approaches within MOOCs, we examine the impact of creating space for formative peer feedback using a digital workbook in a Resilient Teaching MOOC. We use a coding scheme for classifying peer feedback to analyze responses to shared workbook entries. Findings revealed the presence of five attributes in the feedback: content, explanations, advice, questions, and community connections. Our study elaborates approaches for creating productive forms of knowledge exchange among peers.

title: Physical Microcosms: Potentials for Enriching Classroom Investigations in Ecology
citation: Dickes, A., Wisittanawat, P., & Lehrer, R. (2022). Physical microcosms: Potentials for enriching classroom investigations in ecology. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2098-2099). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Dickes, A., Wisittanawat, P., & Lehrer, R.
subject: STEM - Natural Science
abstract: Ecologists construct physical microcosms that exemplify mechanisms and relations in ecosystems. This poster describes how a 7th-grade classroom complemented field study of an intertidal ecosystem with design of classroom microcosms. Initial designs appeared constrained by literal resemblance. As students’ inquiry increasingly focused on interactions among organisms, they configured microcosms to facilitate observation of these interactions. Microcosms became sites for studying processes that could be inferred from field data but rarely observed directly.

title: Do Current Visions of Engineering Literacy Capture Family Engineering Practices? A Microgenetic Analysis of Engineering Learning in a Museum Makerspace
citation: Goeke, M. & Loiselle, T. (2022). Do current visions of engineering literacy capture family engineering practices? A microgenetic analysis of engineering learning in a museum makerspace. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2108-2109). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Goeke, M. & Loiselle, T.
subject: STEM - Engineering & Robotics; Humanities, Language & Literacy
tpack_ck_labels: STEM - Engineering & Robotics; Humanities, Language & Literacy
abstract: The recent Engineering Learning framework (ASEE, 2020) calls for research on how students can be supported to reach full engineering literacy in PreK-12 education. The current study analyzes a microgenetic engineering moment with a child, parent, and staff member in a museum makerspace. We found evidence of the Engineering Learning framework, but instances where the framework did not fully represent some nuances during making.

title: Mental Simulations to Advance Adaptive Teaching Expertise in Reflection-Based Instructional Coaching
citation: Walsh, M., Schunn, C., Matsumura, L., & Zook-Howell, D. (2022). Mental simulations to advance adaptive teaching expertise in reflection-based instructional coaching. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2112-2113). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Walsh, M., Schunn, C., Matsumura, L., & Zook-Howell, D.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Reflection on classroom artifacts is a core feature of teacher professional development. Despite its ubiquity, however, reflection as a learning mechanism is often illdefined and lacking clear connection to a larger theory of teacher learning and change. Here, we present Mental Simulations for Teacher Reflection (MSTR) as one kind of robust teacher learning routine. Our aim is to offer a well-specified routine that embodies core principles for developing adaptive teaching expertise in expert-guided reflection contexts.

title: Centering Ethics in AI Education: Cutting Through the Controversy
citation: Stoiber, A., Kim, Y., & Altuwaiyan, A. (2022). Centering ethics in AI education: Cutting through the controversy. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2120-2121). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Stoiber, A., Kim, Y., & Altuwaiyan, A.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Current efforts teaching the ethical implications of AI neglect current dilemmas rooted in biases. We propose two design considerations for curriculum designers in this area: embedding ethics across the curriculum and foregrounding authentic problems facing the AI field. Our proposals are compared to a responsible AI curriculum we are helping build to explore the implications of each approach to ethics in AI.

title: E-Textile Fashion: Designing Maker Activity for Chinese Migrant Girls
citation: Tu, X., Yang, J., Zhong, Q., Wang, C., & Maltese, A. (2022). E-textile fashion: Designing maker activity for chinese migrant girls. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2130-2131). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Tu, X., Yang, J., Zhong, Q., Wang, C., & Maltese, A.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: We present a low-cost STEAM workshop for twenty-five Chinese migrant girls to learn electronics through making hats. Data sources include video recordings of all classroom activities and post-interviews of students. We analyzed post-interviews of all participants and then narrowed our focus to Meimei, a girl who expressed an interest in art design. We hope this study will inspire future designers and educators to design maker activities for local schools.

title: Learning Health Sanitary Practices Through Scaffolded Questioning in Interactive eBooks for Young Children
citation: Kang, J. H. & Choi, G. W. (2022). Learning health sanitary practices through scaffolded questioning in interactive ebooks for young children. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2136-2137). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Kang, J. H. & Choi, G. W.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Adult assistance during the usage of digital devices may not always be available for children in certain circumstances. Taking this into account, we seek to study how far young children can learn in a scaffolded environment through interactive eBooks without adult intervention. Using the topic of learning sanitary hand practice concepts, the eBook will use scaffolded questioning methods to guide the child in the self-learning process.

title: “Keeping Them With Us”: Constructing Equitable Online Spaces for the Theatre Classroom
citation: Yankova, N., Dahn, M., Peppler, K., Lee, J., Montgomery, A., Moser, S., & Sikkema, S. (2022). “Keeping them with us”: Constructing equitable online spaces for the theatre classroom. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2138-2139). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Yankova, N., Dahn, M., Peppler, K., Lee, J., Montgomery, A., Moser, S., & Sikkema, S.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: We draw on notions of space-making as relational and constituted in interaction to explore how teaching artists construct space as power is redistributed in the online theatre classroom. We use case study methods to illustrate how the shift in power has impacted the design of online learning environments. Findings highlight tensions and possibilities for how power is negotiated and the importance of student voice, with implications for the design of more equitable online learning spaces.

title: How Young Children Pursue Their Interests With Questions
citation: Nguyen, V. & Stevens, R. (2022). How young children pursue their interests with questions. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2146-2147). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Nguyen, V. & Stevens, R.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This case study is an investigation of how children pursue their interests and concerns in interaction with adults. This processual focus led us to study children’s spontaneous questions, which have mostly been at the margins of research on children’s learning and development. Our analysis found that questions are important interactional tools that allow children to simultaneously pursue their interests and concerns while also working within the familiar asymmetries of adult caregiver and child.

title: Shifts in Positions, Epistemic Authority, and Epistemic Agency in a Secondary Mathematics Classroom
citation: Machaka, N., Parr, E. D., Dyer, E. B., & Krist, C. (2022). Shifts in positions, epistemic authority, and epistemic agency in a secondary mathematics classroom. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2148-2149). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Machaka, N., Parr, E. D., Dyer, E. B., & Krist, C.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; STEM - Mathematics
tpack_ck_labels: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; STEM - Mathematics
abstract: In this study, we investigate the interactional positions negotiated among students and the teacher during joint mathematical exploration in the classroom. Using qualitative coding of two video episodes in a secondary mathematics classroom, we found participants take up positions of uncertain knower and explorer in addition to positions of knower and actor identified in previous research. These additional positions help illuminate collaborative knowledge building and negotiation of shared epistemic agency and authority in learning.

title: Justice-Centered Ambitious Science Teaching in Community Spaces: Foregrounding Creativity, Connectedness and Joy
citation: Luehmann, A., Zhang, Y., Smith, J., & Sullivan, K. (2022). Justice-centered ambitious science teaching in community spaces: Foregrounding creativity, connectedness and joy. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2158-2159). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Luehmann, A., Zhang, Y., Smith, J., & Sullivan, K.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: This poster explores the unique and powerful affordances of justice-centered ambitious science teaching (JuST) in two intergenerational community spaces as reflections of an interdisciplinary theory of learning. The results of a cross-case analysis exploring ways JuST practices impacted learning in two related but distinct educational settings spaces revealed boundaries between teaching and learning as blurred, agentic creativity that led to connectedness and joy, and leadership by people of Color as shaping perspectives and priorities.

title: Thrive Online: Preparing Learners for Success in Online Learning
citation: West, L., Measom, E., Leary, H., Call, H., Tuiloma, S., Arts, A., Rogers, A., Brooksby, D., & Nielsen, G. (2022). Thrive online: Preparing learners for success in online learning. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2166-2167). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: West, L., Measom, E., Leary, H., Call, H., Tuiloma, S., Arts, A., Rogers, A., Brooksby, D., & Nielsen, G.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: The need for students to learn online continues to increase. Many students report feeling unprepared, lacking the skills and confidence to succeed. Efforts are needed to bridge a student’s transition from traditional learning environments to online. We developed Thrive Online, an asynchronous short course aimed to increase students’ knowledge, skills, attitudes, and self-efficacy to learn online. A pilot study evaluated the impact of Thrive Online with a sample of 28 students, with results reporting promising data this course can support students’ successful transition to online learning.

title: The Hidden Meaning of Physical Interaction With Exhibits: The Relevance of the Instrumented Activity Situation Model
citation: Iłowiecka-Tańska, I. & vel Żabik, K. P. (2022). The hidden meaning of physical interaction with exhibits: The relevance of the instrumented activity situation model. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2174-2175). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Iłowiecka-Tańska, I. & Żabik, K. P. V.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: Authors discuss the relevance of The Instrumented Activity Situation (IAS) model in analysis of visitor–exhibit interactions. Observing visitors playing with exhibits in science museums raises questions about the relevance of the actions they undertake. We argue that visitors’ conceptual understandings of scientific phenomena are seeded via rapid iterative cycles of explorative co-attuning between processes of instrumenting and instrumentalization. In our analysis we have demonstrated how the adapted IAS model helps to analyze visitors’ interactions with exhibits.

title: Design Considerations for a Middle School Computer Science Pedagogical Content Knowledge Instrument
citation: Basu, S., Rutstein, D., Tate, C., Rachmatullah, A., & Yang, H. (2022). Design considerations for a middle school computer science pedagogical content knowledge instrument. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2176-2177). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Basu, S., Rutstein, D., Tate, C., Rachmatullah, A., & Yang, H.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding
abstract: K-12 Computer Science (CS) education is developing rapidly but still lacks a comprehensive measure for CS teachers’ pedagogical content knowledge (PCK). We respond to this need by describing the design of a CS-PCK instrument for ‘Algorithms and Programming’ that measures three broad constructs: (a) teachers’ understanding of standards and standardsalignment, (b) teachers’ formative assessment practices, and (c) teachers’ self-efficacy for teaching and assessing CS.

title: Game-Based Punctuation Training to Promote Clause Analysis: A Proposal
citation: West, L. & Xu, J. (2022). Game-based punctuation training to promote clause analysis: A proposal. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2184-2185). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: West, L. & Xu, J.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: High-school-level standardized exams devote 10-15% of its content to grammar and punctuation skills, yet the rules of and best practices for training punctuation are often elusive. We describe an ongoing pilot study where students preparing for the ACT/SAT participate in game-based training sessions for advanced English punctuation. Game levels require active organization of sentences, and students are supported through (1) text from a virtual agent, (2) hints, and (3) a visual cognitive organizer.

title: Intergenerational Conversations Through Redesigning Tabletop Games: Playing, Designing, and Learning With Canadian Families
citation: Kim, B., Bastani, R., Acton, J., & Clyde, J. (2022). Intergenerational conversations through redesigning tabletop games: Playing, designing, and learning with canadian families. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2186-2187). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Kim, B., Bastani, R., Acton, J., & Clyde, J.
subject: Interdisciplinary & General
abstract: In this poster, we present our study of the activities for families in Canada to redesign tabletop games, reflective of their interest and culture on their own time during the global pandemic. We collected data through online communications (e.g., video recordings, games). We describe how they expressed what matters to them individually and collectively.

title: Categorization and Framing Teaching Discussions in an Online Physics Classroom
citation: Dunford, G. D., Modir, B., Lock, R. M., & Newton, W. G. (2022). Categorization and framing teaching discussions in an online physics classroom. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2188-2189). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Dunford, G. D., Modir, B., Lock, R. M., & Newton, W. G.
subject: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; STEM - Natural Science; STEM - Mathematics
tpack_ck_labels: STEM - Computer Science & Coding; STEM - Natural Science; STEM - Mathematics
abstract: We analyze written discussions of in-service high school physics teachers as part of the coursework of an online Master in Physics with Teaching Emphasis program. We categorize the form and scope of teaching talks made in response to course structure using the theories of community of practice and framing: Strategies for Teaching Math in Physics; Integration of MPTE Course Content into High School Courses; Pedagogical Strategies for Teaching Physics. We discuss the instructional implications.

title: Trajectories of Practice: Characterizing Students’ Decision Making Agency in Science Investigations
citation: Hayes, R., Gouvea, J., & Wagh, A. (2022). Trajectories of practice: Characterizing students’ decision making agency in science investigations. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2194-2195). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Hayes, R., Gouvea, J., & Wagh, A.
subject: STEM - Natural Science
abstract: An aim of science education is for students to be able to participate in science by making adaptive local decisions that interconnect and integrate scientific practices. We build towards this goal by articulating a trajectory of practice -- a series of moves students make to pursue the scientific aims of their investigations, and showing how this description can be used to investigate the role of curriculum in supporting students exercising decision making agency.

title: Nayah-Irú: The Design of a Participatory Game to Foster Critical Data Literacy Through Storytelling And
citation: Aleman, E. (2022). Nayah-irú: The design of a participatory game to foster critical data literacy through storytelling and. In Chinn, C., Tan, E., Chan, C., & Kali, Y. (Eds.), Proceedings of the 16th International Conference of the Learning Sciences - ICLS 2022 (pp. 2200-2201). International Society of the Learning Sciences.
authors_list: Aleman, E.
subject: Humanities, Language & Literacy
abstract: Countering oppressive practices in digital spaces is essential to prevent control and exploitation. Youth need to be empowered to reflect on their use of such spaces.
